subjects.expectIntro: Grade 10 Afrikaans FAL enters the FET Phase with increased demands on reading, writing and language accuracy. Learners engage with more complex Afrikaans texts including literary extracts, write extended essays and transactional texts, and develop a comprehensive command of Afrikaans grammar. The focus shifts from building basic literacy to using Afrikaans independently and accurately across a range of formal contexts.

expectItems.label: Text types
expectItems.value: Literary extracts, argumentative, transactional, visual, poetry

expectItems.label: Key shift
expectItems.value: Extended formal writing · literary engagement · FET grammar demands

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Literary and narrative texts
topics: Read Afrikaans literary extracts and longer texts — literal, inferential, evaluative, critical
Complex sentence structures: multiple subordinate clauses of different types
All tenses revision including perfect and pluperfect forms
Direct and indirect speech — all tenses, full conversion practice
Write a multi-paragraph Afrikaans essay (narrative or descriptive) — 200–250 words
Vocabulary: register, connotation, context clues, Afrikaans idioms
Figurative language: extended metaphor, paradox, irony, antithesis
Oral: prepared Afrikaans talk on a contemporary SA topic

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Transactional and formal texts
topics: Read formal Afrikaans texts — letters, reports, advertisements, articles
Passive voice: all tenses — formation and conversion
All four conditional sentence types in Afrikaans
Formal Afrikaans letter and email — layout and register
Afrikaans report writing — structure, tone, factual language
Concord: subject-verb agreement in complex Afrikaans sentences
Vocabulary: synonyms, antonyms, homonyms, word families
Oral: formal Afrikaans speech with persuasive intent

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Argumentative texts and poetry
topics: Read Afrikaans argumentative texts — identify claim, evidence, counter-argument, fallacies
Write a short Afrikaans argumentative essay — thesis, body, rebuttal, conclusion
Afrikaans poetry: imagery, tone, mood, theme, figurative language
Compare two Afrikaans poems in a structured paragraph response
Relative clauses and nominal clauses — extended use in own writing
Revision of all grammar covered in Grades 7–10
Visual texts: analyse purpose, audience, layout, technique in Afrikaans
Oral: argue a point of view or present a visual analysis in Afrikaans

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Unseen texts, revision and exam preparation
topics: Unseen Afrikaans comprehension — apply all reading skills to unfamiliar texts
Summary writing in Afrikaans: identify main points, paraphrase, write concisely
Revision of all writing formats: letter, essay, report, summary, paragraph
Grammar consolidation: all tenses, voice, speech, concord, clauses
Examination techniques: reading questions carefully, time management
Oral: final prepared speech or dramatic reading in Afrikaans
Vocabulary revision: build and review personal word list
Reflect on growth and set goals for Grade 11 Afrikaans FAL

Use all four conditional sentence types
Write a structured Afrikaans argumentative essay
Produce a formal Afrikaans letter and report

Compare two Afrikaans poems with textual evidence

Analyse visual texts in Afrikaans

subjects.expectIntro: Graad 10 Afrikaans Huistaal begin die OBF-fase met voorgeskrewe prosatekste, gedigte en drama. Leerders produseer uitgebreide analitiese en kreatiewe skryfwerk en demonstreer beheer oor gevorderde grammatika en transaksionele skryfwerk. Die vier vaardighede — luister en praat, lees en kyk, skryf en aanbied, taalstrukture — word nou formeel in hoërisiko-take geassesseer.

expectItems.label: Sleutelverskuiwing
expectItems.value: Voorgeskrewe tekste · formele letterkundige opstelle · matriekgereedheid begin

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Prosa: romanstudies en analitiese skryfwerk
topics: Lees voorgeskrewe prosateks — karakter, agtergrond, konflik, tema, narratiewe tegniek
Identifiseer literêre middele: ironie (verbaal, situasioneel, dramaties), simbool, motief, aankondiging
Analitiese opstel: tesis, PEEL-liggaamsparagrawe, gevolgtrekking — minimum 250 woorde
Tydhersiening: alle vorme insluitend voltooide voortgaande en toekomende voltooide tye
Kongruensie: moeilike gevalle — kollektiewe naamwoorde, korrelatiewe voegwoorde, omgekeerde sinne
Woordeskat: register, konnotasie, denotasie, eufemisme, omgangstaal
Transaksioneel: formele brief, e-pos, memo — uitleg en register
Mondeling: voorbereide toespraak — oorredend, met strukturele aanwijsers

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Poësie: kritiese analise en vergelyking
topics: Lees en analiseer voorgeskrewe gedigte — beelding, woordkeuse, toon, stemming, tema, struktuur, vorm
Uitgebreide stylfigure: uitgebreide metafoor, apostrofe, toespeling, antitese, oksimoron
Poëtiese vorme: sonnet (Petrargiaans en Shakespeariaans), vrye vers, ode, elegie
Vergelyk twee gedigte uit die antologie in 'n gestruktureerde opstel
Bywoordelike bysinne: tyd, rede, voorwaarde, toegewing, doel, gevolg
Byvoeglike bysinne: beperkende en nie-beperkende betreklike bysinne
Leestekens vir effek: koppelteken, ellips, hakies, kommapunt
Mondeling: gedigopsê met interpretatiewe refleksie

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Drama: teksanalise en uitvoering
topics: Lees voorgeskrewe dramateks — dramatiese struktuur, karakterboog, tema, toneelkuns
Dramatiese middele: dramatiese ironie, aankondiging, solilokie, terzyde, tragiese fout
Konteks en subteks: wat karakters sê vs wat hulle bedoel
Argumenterende opstel: tesis, drie liggaamsargumente, teenargument, weerlegging, gevolgtrekking
Beskouende opstel: gebalanseerde siening — weeg beide kante eerlik
Transaksioneel: notule, agenda, verslag, CV en dekbrief
Naamwoordelike bysinne as onderwerp, voorwerp en komplement
Mondeling: dramatiese voorlees of groeptoneeluitvoering

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Ongesiene tekste, visuele geletterdheid en eksamenbereiding
topics: Ongesiene prosa begrip — pas alle letterkundige vaardighede onafhanklik toe
Ongesiene poësie-analise — identifiseer en verduidelik middele sonder leiding
Visuele en mediatekste: advertensie, spotprent, infografika, filmplakkaat — doel, gehoor, tegniek
Opsommingskryfwerk: identifiseer hoofpunte, parafraseer, skryf bondige opsomming
Hersiening: alle grammatika, tye, stem, rede, kongruensie, bysinne
Kreatiewe skryfwerk: narratiewe en beskrywende opstelbeplanning en uitvoering
Eksamenstrategie: tydbestuur, paragraaflengte, aanhaling
Mondeling: formele voorbereide aanbieding oor 'n navorsingsonderwerp

skillChips: Analiseer voorgeskrewe prosa vir literêre middele en tema
Skryf 'n tesis-gedrewe letterkundige opstel
Vergelyk twee gedigte met teksgetuienis
Identifiseer en verduidelik uitgebreide metafoor en toespeling
Analiseer drama vir struktuur, toneelkuns en karakter
Produseer argumenterende en beskouende opstelle
Skryf gepoleerde transaksionele tekste
Identifiseer en gebruik byvoeglike en bywoordelike bysinne
Analiseer ongesiene prosa en poësie onafhanklik
Skryf 'n gestruktureerde opsomming
Evalueer mediatekste vir doel en vooroordeel
Demonstreer beheer oor alle OBF-fase grammatika

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Ken jou voorgeskrewe tekste diep. Herlees sleutelhoofstukke en gedigte. Annoteer aanhalings. Jy kan nie 'n goeie letterkundige opstel uit geheue skryf nie.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: PEEL elke analitiese paragraaf. Punt → Bewys (aanhaling) → Verduidelik die effek → Skakel na tema.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Beplan opstelle voor jy skryf. 5 minute se beplanning = 'n sterker, meer samehangende opstel.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Transaksionele formate moet gememoriseer word. CV, formele brief, notule — elk het 'n vaste uitleg. Leer dit eenmalig.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Graad 10 stel jou matriekbaan in. Die gewoontes en vaardighede wat jy nou bou, dra direk na Graad 11 en 12 oor.

subjects.expectIntro: Grade 10 English Home Language marks the start of the FET Phase and a significant step up in literary and language demands. Learners study prescribed prose, poetry and drama texts in depth, produce extended analytical and creative writing, and demonstrate command of advanced grammar and transactional writing. The four skills — listening and speaking, reading and viewing, writing and presenting, language structures — are now assessed formally across a range of high-stakes tasks.

expectItems.label: Key shift
expectItems.value: Prescribed texts · formal literary essays · matric readiness begins

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Prose: novel study and analytical writing
topics: Read prescribed prose text — character, setting, conflict, theme, narrative technique
Identify literary devices: irony (verbal, situational, dramatic), symbolism, motif, foreshadowing
Analytical essay: thesis statement, PEEL body paragraphs, conclusion — minimum 250 words
Tenses revision: all forms including perfect progressive and future perfect
Concord: difficult cases — collective nouns, correlative conjunctions, inverted sentences
Vocabulary: register, connotation, denotation, euphemism, colloquialism
Transactional: formal letter, email, memo — layout and register
Oral: prepared speech — persuasive, with structural signposting

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Poetry: critical analysis and comparison
topics: Read and analyse prescribed poems — imagery, diction, tone, mood, theme, structure, form
Extended figures of speech: extended metaphor, apostrophe, allusion, antithesis, oxymoron
Poetic forms: sonnet (Petrarchan and Shakespearean), free verse, ode, elegy
Compare two poems from the anthology in a structured essay
Adverbial clauses: time, reason, condition, concession, purpose, result
Adjective clauses: defining and non-defining relative clauses
Punctuation for effect: dash, ellipsis, parentheses, semicolon
Oral: poetry recital with interpretive reflection

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Drama: text analysis and performance
topics: Read prescribed drama text — dramatic structure, character arc, theme, stagecraft
Dramatic devices: dramatic irony, foreshadowing, soliloquy, aside, tragic flaw
Context and subtext: what characters say vs what they mean
Argumentative essay: thesis, three body arguments, counter-argument, rebuttal, conclusion
Discursive essay: balanced view — weigh both sides fairly
Transactional: minutes, agenda, report, CV and covering letter
Noun clauses as subject, object and complement
Oral: dramatic reading or group scene performance

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Unseen texts, visual literacy and exam preparation
topics: Unseen prose comprehension — apply all literary skills independently
Unseen poetry analysis — identify and explain devices without guidance
Visual and media texts: advertisement, cartoon, infographic, film poster — purpose, audience, technique
Summary writing: identify main points, paraphrase, write concise summary
Revision: all grammar, tenses, voice, speech, concord, clauses
Creative writing: narrative and descriptive essay planning and execution
Examination strategies: time management, paragraph length, quoting
Oral: formal prepared presentation on a research topic

skillChips: Analyse prescribed prose for literary devices and theme
Write a thesis-driven literary essay
Compare two poems using textual evidence
Identify and explain extended metaphor and allusion
Analyse drama for structure, stagecraft and character
Produce argumentative and discursive essays
Write polished transactional texts
Identify and use adjective and adverb clauses
Analyse unseen prose and poetry independently
Write a structured summary
Evaluate media texts for purpose and bias
Demonstrate command of all FET Phase grammar

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Know your prescribed texts deeply. Re-read key chapters and poems. Annotate quotes. You cannot write a good literary essay from memory alone.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: PEEL every analytical paragraph. Point → Evidence (quote) → Explain the effect → Link to theme. Use it for every body paragraph.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Plan essays before writing. 5 minutes of planning = a stronger, more coherent essay. Examiners can tell when there is no plan.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Transactional formats must be memorised. CV, formal letter, minutes — each has a fixed layout. Learn it once, apply it without thinking.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Grade 10 sets your matric trajectory. The habits and skills you build now carry directly into Grade 11 and 12.

subjects.expectIntro: Grade 10 Life Orientation is the first year of the FET Phase and focuses on developing the self-awareness, social responsibility and life skills needed for success in the final three years of school and beyond. The CAPS curriculum covers personal development, citizenship, health, career planning and physical education at a mature level appropriate to young adults entering the FET Phase.

expectItems.label: Assessment
expectItems.value: SBA only — no final exam for LO

expectItems.label: Key focus
expectItems.value: Personal development plan · career research · physical fitness

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Personal development and wellbeing
topics: Self-concept: identity, values, self-esteem, self-efficacy — how they influence choices
Emotional intelligence: self-awareness, self-regulation, motivation, empathy, social skills
Resilience: building a growth mindset — failure as feedback
Healthy relationships: qualities, communication, boundaries, conflict resolution
Social media and digital identity: benefits, risks, managing your online presence
Physical Education: health-related fitness — cardiorespiratory endurance, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility, body composition
Fitness testing: establish personal baseline; set SMART fitness goals
Study skills: effective note-taking, mind mapping, spaced repetition

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Citizenship and democracy
topics: The South African Constitution: Bill of Rights — focus on rights most relevant to FET learners
Democracy and governance: how SA's government works — national, provincial, local
Corruption: causes, consequences, anti-corruption bodies — Hawks, NPA, Public Protector
Social justice: racism, sexism, homophobia, xenophobia — legislation and lived experience
Gender-based violence: Statistics SA data, legislation, support structures
Environmental rights: Constitution Section 24 — environmental justice in SA
Community engagement: how to participate as an active citizen
Physical Education: team sport — advanced tactics, leadership, fair play

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Health and social issues
topics: HIV/AIDS: epidemiology in SA, transmission, ARV therapy, living positively, reducing stigma
Sexual health: reproductive health, contraception, STIs — accurate, age-appropriate information
Substance abuse: types, addiction cycle, impact on learning and relationships
Mental health: anxiety, depression, burnout — recognition and help-seeking
First aid: CPR, choking, bleeding, fractures, shock — DRSABCD protocol
Nutrition and performance: macronutrients, hydration, eating for sport
Physical Education: individual fitness challenge or outdoor education
Stress management: evidence-based techniques — exercise, mindfulness, sleep, social connection

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Career and future planning
topics: Subject choices and career implications: review Grade 10 subjects against career requirements
Career research: gather information on 3 career options — qualifications, pathways, salaries
Holland Codes: match personality type to career clusters — in depth
Tertiary institutions in SA: universities, UoTs, FET colleges, TVET colleges — requirements
NSC requirements: minimum APS scores for different degree programmes
Bursaries: NSFAS eligibility, Funza Lushaka, sector-specific — how to research and apply
Personal development plan: goals for Grade 11, career goals, action steps
Physical Education: fitness reassessment — compare to Term 1 baseline; celebrate progress

skillChips: Describe personal values, identity and self-concept
Apply emotional intelligence in real situations
Explain key sections of the Bill of Rights
Describe SA's governance structures
Explain the causes and consequences of GBV
Describe HIV/AIDS transmission and treatment
Apply the DRSABCD first aid protocol
Use Holland Codes to explore career options
Research career requirements and qualifications
Describe NSC requirements and APS scoring
Write a personal development plan
Demonstrate improved physical fitness

subjects.title: Grade 10 Mathematical Literacy | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Mathematical Literacy for Grade 10. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.tagline: maths that makes sense in real life
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 10 Mathematical Literacy develops the ability to use mathematical knowledge and skills in everyday life, work and civic contexts. The CAPS curriculum covers four topics — Numbers and Operations, Patterns and Relationships, Space and Shape, and Data Handling — all anchored in realistic South African contexts. Mathematical Literacy is not 'easy Maths' — it demands accurate calculation, logical reasoning and the ability to interpret and communicate mathematical results in context.

expectItems.label: Four topics
expectItems.value: Numbers · Patterns · Space & Shape · Data Handling

expectItems.label: Key focus
expectItems.value: Real-world application · financial literacy · data interpretation

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Numbers, operations and finance
topics: Rational and irrational numbers: classify, round, estimate
Percentages in context: percentage increase/decrease, VAT (15%), discount, profit, loss
Ratio and proportion: simplify, use in recipes, maps, scale drawings
Rate: unit rate, best buy comparisons, speed-distance-time
Personal finance: income, expenditure, budget surplus and deficit
Simple and compound interest: calculate interest earned or paid
Hire purchase: total cost including interest — compare with cash price
Tax: income tax (SARS), PAYE — interpret a payslip

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Patterns and relationships
topics: Numeric patterns: constant difference and ratio patterns in context
Input-output tables: identify rule, complete table, write equation in words
Draw graphs from tables: straight-line graphs from real data
Interpret graphs: identify trends, read off values, describe relationships
Break-even: fixed costs, variable costs, revenue — find break-even point graphically
Distance-time graphs: interpret speed, rest, return journey
Mobile phone tariffs, electricity tariffs: tiered pricing — calculate and compare
Cooking and building quantities: scale up and down using ratio

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Space, shape and measurement
topics: Measuring accurately: reading instruments — ruler, tape, scale, thermometer, measuring jug
Converting units: length (mm, cm, m, km), mass (g, kg, ton), capacity (ml, l)
Perimeter and area: rectangles, triangles, circles, composite shapes
Volume and surface area: rectangular prisms, cylinders — apply in packaging and construction contexts
Scale drawings: read and draw to scale — floor plans, maps
Maps and directions: read a road map, calculate distance using scale
Plans: interpret floor plans — identify dimensions, calculate floor area
Time calculations: timetables, time zones, scheduling

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Data handling and probability
topics: Data collection: questionnaires, sampling methods — random, systematic, stratified
Organise data: frequency tables, grouped data
Represent data: bar graphs, histograms, pie charts, line graphs — draw and interpret
Measures of central tendency: mean, median, mode from raw and grouped data
Measures of spread: range, quartiles — box-and-whisker plots
Misleading graphs: identify how graphs can distort data
Probability: theoretical probability — equally likely outcomes
Probability in context: weather forecasts, insurance, gambling — interpret probability statements

skillChips: Calculate percentages including VAT, discount and profit
Apply ratio and rate in real contexts
Calculate simple and compound interest
Interpret and complete a personal budget
Draw and interpret straight-line graphs
Identify break-even point graphically
Convert between units of measurement
Calculate perimeter, area, volume and surface area
Read and draw floor plans to scale
Collect and organise data
Draw and interpret statistical graphs
Calculate mean, median, mode and range

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="2" y="5" width="20" height="14" rx="2"/><path d="M2 10h20"/></svg>
tips.text: Always show units in your answer. 'R450' not just '450'. '12.5 m²' not just '12.5'. Missing units costs marks every time.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="4.5" y="2.5" width="15" height="19" rx="2"/><path d="M8 6.5h8"/><path d="M8 11h.01M12 11h.01M16 11h.01M8 15h.01M12 15h.01M16 15h.01M8 19h.01M12 19h.01M16 19h.01"/></svg>
tips.text: Draw a diagram for every measurement question. Sketching the shape before calculating helps you choose the right formula and avoid errors.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="m3 16 6-6 4 4 8-9"/><path d="M15 5h6v6"/></svg>
tips.text: Graphs must be fully labelled. Title, axes labels with units, scale, data points. An unlabelled graph loses marks even if the numbers are correct.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="4.5" y="2.5" width="15" height="19" rx="2"/><path d="M8 6.5h8"/><path d="M8 11h.01M12 11h.01M16 11h.01M8 15h.01M12 15h.01M16 15h.01M8 19h.01M12 19h.01M16 19h.01"/></svg>
tips.text: Formula sheet is given — but you must know how to use it. The formula means nothing if you don't know what to substitute. Practise applying formulas to real data.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Mathematical Literacy is about context. Always read what the question is asking in real-world terms. Your answer must make sense in the given situation.

subjects.hubDescription: Real-world maths — finance, measurement, data and graphs in South African contexts.

subjects.title: Grade 10 Mathematics | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Mathematics for Grade 10. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 10 Mathematics is the first year of FET and dramatically raises the bar from Grade 9. The CAPS curriculum introduces algebraic manipulation, functions, Euclidean geometry, trigonometry, statistics and probability at a formal level. Grade 10 Maths is foundational — every topic introduced here recurs in Grades 11 and 12 at greater depth. Learners who master Grade 10 thoroughly are positioned strongly for the NSC examination.

expectItems.label: Key topics
expectItems.value: Algebra · functions · Euclidean geometry · trigonometry · statistics

expectItems.label: Key shift
expectItems.value: Formal proofs · function graphs · trig ratios beyond Grade 9

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Algebra: expressions, equations and inequalities
topics: Algebraic expressions: products — (a±b)², (a+b)(a-b), (a±b)³
Factorisation: HCF, difference of squares, sum/difference of cubes, trinomials, grouping
Algebraic fractions: simplify, add, subtract, multiply, divide with polynomial denominators
Equations: quadratic equations — factorisation, completing the square (intro)
Simultaneous equations: linear and quadratic — substitution method
Inequalities: solve and represent on number line and interval notation
Nature of roots: discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac — determine number and type of roots
Word problems: set up and solve quadratic equations from context

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Functions and graphs
topics: Functions: definition, domain, range, notation, function vs non-function
Linear function y = mx + c: gradient, intercepts, sketch, interpret
Quadratic function y = ax² + bx + c: turning point (completing the square), axis, roots, sketch
Hyperbola y = a/x + q: asymptotes, domain, range, sketch
Exponential y = ab^x + q: growth/decay, asymptote, sketch
Trigonometric functions: y = sin x, y = cos x, y = tan x — period, amplitude, sketch
Determine equations of functions from graphs
Financial maths: compound interest A = P(1+i)ⁿ, depreciation A = P(1-i)ⁿ

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Euclidean geometry and trigonometry
topics: Revised axioms and theorems: lines, angles, triangles — proofs required
Circle geometry: parts of a circle, chord, arc, tangent, secant
Midpoint theorem: proof and application
Proportion theorem: a line parallel to one side of a triangle
Trigonometry: sin, cos, tan in right-angled triangles — SOHCAHTOA
Special angles: 30°, 45°, 60° — exact values without calculator
Trig equations: solve for θ in [0°; 360°]
2D problems: angles of elevation and depression

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Statistics, probability and revision
topics: Measures of central tendency: mean, median, mode — ungrouped and grouped data
Measures of spread: range, quartiles, interquartile range, semi-interquartile range
Five-number summary: min, Q1, median, Q3, max
Box-and-whisker plots: draw, interpret, compare two data sets
Scatter plots: draw, identify correlation, line of best fit
Probability: theoretical and experimental probability
Probability of compound events: addition rule, complementary events
Venn diagrams: represent and calculate probability

skillChips: Factorise completely including sum/difference of cubes
Solve quadratic equations by factorisation and completing the square
Solve simultaneous linear and quadratic equations
Determine nature of roots using the discriminant
Draw and interpret all five function types
Determine equations of functions from graphs
Apply compound interest and depreciation formulae
Write proofs using Euclidean geometry theorems
Apply the midpoint and proportion theorems
Solve trig equations in [0°; 360°]
Solve 2D problems using trig ratios
Draw box-and-whisker plots and analyse data

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="4.5" y="2.5" width="15" height="19" rx="2"/><path d="M8 6.5h8"/><path d="M8 11h.01M12 11h.01M16 11h.01M8 15h.01M12 15h.01M16 15h.01M8 19h.01M12 19h.01M16 19h.01"/></svg>
tips.text: Factorise in order every time. HCF first → difference of squares → sum/difference of cubes → trinomial → grouping. Never skip the order.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Functions: always find key points first. x-intercepts, y-intercept, turning point, asymptotes. Plot these, then sketch.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Geometry proofs need reasons. Every statement must have a reason. No reason = no mark. Learn the standard phrasing.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="4.5" y="2.5" width="15" height="19" rx="2"/><path d="M8 6.5h8"/><path d="M8 11h.01M12 11h.01M16 11h.01M8 15h.01M12 15h.01M16 15h.01M8 19h.01M12 19h.01M16 19h.01"/></svg>
tips.text: Discriminant determines roots before you solve. Δ > 0: two real roots. Δ = 0: one real root. Δ < 0: no real roots. Check this first.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Grade 10 Maths repeats in Grades 11 and 12. Master each topic before moving on. Everything here comes back harder next year.

subjects.hubDescription: Algebra, functions, Euclidean geometry, trigonometry, statistics — full FET foundation.

subjects.title: Grade 11 Afrikaans First Additional Language | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Afrikaans First Additional Language for Grade 11. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 11 Afrikaans FAL consolidates and extends the work of Grade 10 at a level that directly prepares learners for the NSC examination. Learners read more complex texts, produce extended essays and NSC-standard transactional writing, and demonstrate comprehensive command of Afrikaans grammar. By the end of Grade 11, all core language structures must be secure.

expectItems.label: Text types
expectItems.value: Literary extracts, argumentative, all transactional types, visual, poetry

expectItems.label: Key shift
expectItems.value: NSC-standard writing · literary analysis · grammar consolidation

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Literary and narrative texts
topics: Read complex Afrikaans literary extracts — sustained inferential and evaluative comprehension
Advanced sentence structures: multiple subordinate clauses, reduced clauses
Full tense revision including all perfect and conditional forms
Direct and indirect speech — all tenses, NSC-level conversion accuracy
Write a multi-paragraph Afrikaans essay — narrative or descriptive — 250–300 words
Vocabulary: idioms, proverbs, register, connotation — identify and use
Figurative language: extended metaphor, antithesis, paradox, irony — in own writing
Oral: formal Afrikaans speech on a socially relevant topic

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Transactional and formal writing
topics: NSC-standard formal Afrikaans letter — full layout, correct register, all conventions
Formal Afrikaans report and memo — structure, objectivity, factual language
Afrikaans advertisement and notice — purpose, audience, format
Passive voice: all tenses — formation, conversion, use in formal writing
All four conditional sentence types — form, meaning, use in extended writing
Advanced concord: complex agreement rules in sophisticated sentences
Vocabulary: word formation — derivation, compounding, abbreviation in Afrikaans
Oral: formal Afrikaans presentation on a research topic

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Argumentative, poetry and visual texts
topics: Read Afrikaans argumentative and persuasive texts — evaluate logic, identify fallacies
Write a sustained Afrikaans argumentative essay — 300+ words, with counter-argument
Afrikaans poetry analysis: imagery, diction, tone, mood, theme, form, figurative language
Compare two Afrikaans poems in a structured essay response
Visual texts: multi-modal analysis — composition, colour, layout, text relationship
Revision of all grammar: nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, pronouns, tenses, clauses
Oral: argue a complex position or analyse a visual text in Afrikaans

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: NSC preparation and consolidation
topics: Unseen Afrikaans comprehension — NSC exam conditions, time pressure
Summary writing: 70-word and 100-word Afrikaans summaries
Revision of all writing formats to NSC standard
Grammar consolidation: all structures from Grades 10–11
NSC paper structure: understand what each section requires
Vocabulary and spelling: personal word lists, common error patterns
Oral: final prepared speech or dramatic reading
Reflect: identify weak areas and make a targeted revision plan

skillChips: Write NSC-standard formal Afrikaans letter and report
Use passive voice in all tenses with accuracy
Apply all four conditional sentence types
Write a 300-word Afrikaans argumentative essay
Analyse Afrikaans poetry with correct terminology
Compare two Afrikaans poems in a structured response
Write 70- and 100-word Afrikaans summaries
Analyse visual and multi-modal texts in Afrikaans
Apply all Afrikaans grammar at NSC level
Write extended Afrikaans essays across all types
Identify and use figurative language in own writing
Demonstrate secure command of all tenses

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: NSC letter format must be perfect. Every layout mark is free. Address, date, reference, salutation, body, closing — know them without thinking.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Argumentative essays need a thesis in paragraph 1. State your position clearly. Examiners look for it immediately.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Summary: every point must come from the text. You cannot add your own ideas in a summary. Find the main points in the source, paraphrase, count words.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Passive voice in all tenses is always tested. Word geskryf / is geskryf / sal geskryf word / sou geskryf word — know all forms.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Grade 11 grammar must be fully secure before Grade 12. There is no time to re-learn basics in Grade 12. Fix gaps now.

subjects.hubDescription: NSC-standard transactional writing, literary analysis, argumentative essays and grammar consolidation.

subjects.title: Grade 11 Afrikaans Home Language | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Afrikaans Home Language for Grade 11. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Graad 11 Afrikaans Huistaal verdiep die letterkundige en taalvaardighede van Graad 10 en berei leerders voor vir die hoërisiko-eise van Graad 12. Leerders werk met meer komplekse voorgeskrewe prosa, gedigte en drama, produseer uitgebreide analitiese, argumenterende en kreatiewe skryfwerk, en demonstreer gesofistikeerde beheer oor grammatika en transaksionele tekste.

expectItems.label: Letterkunde
expectItems.value: Voorgeskrewe roman + gedigte + drama — dieper analise as Graad 10

expectItems.label: Sleutelverskuiwing
expectItems.value: Uitgebreide letterkundige opstelle · gesofistikeerde argument · NSS-voorbereiding

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Prosa: karakter, tema en narratiewe tegniek
topics: Lees voorgeskrewe roman — volgehoue analise van karakterontwikkeling, konflik, tema
Narratiewe tegniek: vertellersperspektief, narratiewe afstand, bewussynstroom, onbetroubare verteller
Identifiseer en verduidelik: ironie (alle soorte), allegorie, intertekstualiteit, uitgebreide metafoor
Letterkundige opstel: 400+ woorde — tesis, ontwikkelde PEEL-paragrawe, gevolgtrekking
Komplekse sinstrukture: naamwoordelike, byvoeglike, bywoordelike bysinne — gebruik in eie skryfwerk
Kongruensie: moeilike konstruksies — nóg...nóg, óf...óf, elke, geen
Woordeskat: konnotasie, denotasie, register, jargon, eufemisme, cliché — vermy in eie skryfwerk
Mondeling: formele voorbereide toespraak — argumenteer 'n standpunt

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Poësie: vergelyking en kontekstuele analise
topics: Analiseer en vergelyk drie voorgeskrewe gedigte — tema, beelding, woordkeuse, toon, stemming, vorm
Kontekstuele vraag: verduidelik 'n gegewe uittreksel in konteks van die volle gedig
Uitgebreide stylfigure: toespeling, apostrofe, antitese, chiasmus, zeugma
Poëtiese vorm en effek: sonnet, vrye vers, dramatiese monoloog, ballade
Woordkeuse-analise: konnotasie, klankmiddele — assonansie, konsonansie, sibilansie
Formele brief, e-pos, CV en dekbrief — hersiening en verfyning tot NSS-standaard
Sinkombinering: verminder meervoudige sinne tot een gesofistikeerde struktuur
Mondeling: poësiebespreking — analiseer en verdedig 'n interpretasie

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Drama: volledige teksanalise en opstel
topics: Lees volledige voorgeskrewe dramateks — dramatiese struktuur, tema, karakter, toneelkuns
Dramatiese middele: tragiese fout, deus ex machina, komiese verligting, dramatiese ironie, katarsis
Kontekstuele vraag: plaas 'n gegewe gedeelte in konteks van die volle drama
Uitgebreide dramatiese opstel: argumenteer 'n tesis oor tema of karakter oor die hele teks
Argumenterende opstel: volgehoue argument — 400+ woorde, met teenargument en weerlegging
Transaksionele skryfwerk: voorstel, memo, notule, formele verslag — NSS-formate
Deelwoord- en infinitiewe frases as sinselemente
Mondeling: dramatiese voorlees of debat

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Ongesiene begrip, visuele geletterdheid en NSS-voorbereiding
topics: Ongesiene prosa: pas volledige letterkundige analise-vaardighede toe
Ongesiene poësie: onafhanklike analise — middele, toon, tema, vorm
Visuele/mediatekste: multimodale analise — filmstill, infografika, advertensie, spotprent
Opsommingskryfwerk: 70-woord en 100-woord opsommings — NSS-tegniek
Kreatiewe skryfwerk: narratiewe, beskrywende, reflektiewe opstelle — beplan, konsep, redigeer
Grammatikakonsolidasie: alle tye, stem, rede, kongruensie, bysinne, leestekens
NSS-vraestelstruktuur: Vraestel 1 (taal), Vraestel 2 (letterkunde), Vraestel 3 (skryfwerk)
Mondeling: finale formele aanbieding — navorsingsgebaseerd

skillChips: Skryf 'n volgehoue letterkundige opstel met 'n ontwikkelde tesis
Analiseer narratiewe tegniek in prosa
Vergelyk drie gedigte met teksgetuienis
Plaas 'n gedeelte in konteks van die volle teks
Analiseer drama vir struktuur, toneelkuns en tema
Skryf uitgebreide argumenterende en beskouende opstelle
Produseer NSS-standaard transaksionele tekste
Skryf 70- en 100-woord opsommings akkuraat
Analiseer ongesiene prosa en poësie onafhanklik
Identifiseer en verduidelik toespeling, antitese, chiasmus
Pas kongruensie toe in komplekse konstruksies
Gebruik bysoorte akkuraat in eie skryfwerk

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Ken jou voorgeskrewe tekste van binne en van buite. Herlees sleutelgedeeltes. Annoteer aanhalings met die tegniek en effek.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: 'n Tesis is 'n argument, nie 'n feitelike stelling nie. 'Die skrywer gebruik ironie' is nie 'n tesis nie. 'Die deurdringende ironie in die teks ontbloot die skynheiligheid van koloniale gesag' is 'n tesis.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Opsommingskryfwerk vereis presiese woordtelling. Tel jou woorde. 'n 70-woord opsomming wat 85 woorde is, verloor punte.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: NSS Vraestel 3 is tydsgebonde skryfwerk onder druk. Oefen om 'n 400-woord opstel in 30 minute te skryf.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Graad 11 is jou laaste kans om gewoontes te bou. Elke opstel wat jy hierdie jaar skryf, is oefening vir Graad 12.

subjects.hubDescription: Uitgebreide letterkundige opstelle, NSS-standaard skryfwerk en eksamenbereiding.

subjects.title: Grade 11 English First Additional Language | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned English First Additional Language for Grade 11. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 11 English FAL consolidates and extends the work of Grade 10 at a level that directly prepares learners for the NSC examination. Learners read more complex texts, produce extended essays and NSC-standard transactional writing, and demonstrate comprehensive command of English grammar. By the end of Grade 11, all core language structures must be secure.

expectItems.label: Text types
expectItems.value: Literary extracts, argumentative, all transactional types, visual, poetry

expectItems.label: Key shift
expectItems.value: NSC-standard writing · literary analysis · grammar consolidation

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Literary and narrative texts
topics: Read complex literary extracts — sustained inferential and evaluative comprehension
Advanced sentence structures: multiple subordinate clauses, reduced clauses
Full tense revision including all perfect and conditional forms
Direct and indirect speech — all tenses, NSC-level conversion accuracy
Write a multi-paragraph essay — narrative or descriptive — 250–300 words
Vocabulary: idioms, register, connotation — identify and use in own writing
Figurative language: extended metaphor, antithesis, paradox, irony — in own writing
Oral: formal speech on a socially relevant topic

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Transactional and formal writing
topics: NSC-standard formal letter — full layout, correct register, all conventions
Formal report and memo — structure, objectivity, factual language
Advertisement and notice — purpose, audience, format
Passive voice: all tenses — formation, conversion, use in formal writing
All four conditional sentence types — form, meaning, use in extended writing
Advanced concord: complex agreement rules in sophisticated sentences
Vocabulary: word formation — derivation, compounding, abbreviation
Oral: formal presentation on a research topic

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Argumentative, poetry and visual texts
topics: Read argumentative and persuasive texts — evaluate logic, identify fallacies
Write a sustained argumentative essay — 300+ words, with counter-argument
Poetry analysis: imagery, diction, tone, mood, theme, form, figurative language
Compare two poems in a structured essay response
Visual texts: multi-modal analysis — composition, colour, layout, text relationship
Revision of all grammar: parts of speech, tenses, voice, speech, concord, clauses
Oral: argue a complex position or analyse a visual text

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: NSC preparation and consolidation
topics: Unseen comprehension — NSC exam conditions, time pressure
Summary writing: 70-word and 100-word summaries
Revision of all writing formats to NSC standard
Grammar consolidation: all structures from Grades 10–11
NSC paper structure: understand what each section requires
Vocabulary and spelling: personal word lists, common error patterns
Oral: final prepared speech or dramatic reading
Reflect: identify weak areas and make a targeted revision plan

skillChips: Write NSC-standard formal letter and report
Use passive voice in all tenses with accuracy
Apply all four conditional sentence types
Write a 300-word argumentative essay
Analyse poetry with correct terminology
Compare two poems in a structured response
Write 70- and 100-word summaries
Analyse visual and multi-modal texts
Apply all grammar at NSC level
Write extended essays across all types
Identify and use figurative language in own writing
Demonstrate secure command of all tenses

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: NSC letter format must be perfect. Address, date, reference, salutation, body, closing — every layout mark is free. Learn it cold.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Argumentative essays need a thesis in paragraph 1. State your position clearly. Examiners look for it immediately.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Summary: every point must come from the text. You cannot add your own ideas. Paraphrase the main points, count words exactly.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Passive voice in all tenses is always tested. Is written / was written / will be written / would be written — know all forms.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Fix grammar gaps before Grade 12. There is no time in Grade 12 to re-learn basics. Every gap costs marks in the NSC.

subjects.hubDescription: NSC-standard transactional writing, literary analysis, argumentative essays and grammar consolidation.

subjects.title: Grade 11 English Home Language | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned English Home Language for Grade 11. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 11 English Home Language deepens the literary and language skills of Grade 10 and prepares learners for the high-stakes demands of Grade 12. Learners engage with more complex prescribed prose, poetry and drama, produce extended analytical, argumentative and creative writing, and demonstrate sophisticated command of grammar and transactional texts. Grade 11 is the most demanding preparation year — the work done here determines readiness for the NSC.

expectItems.label: Literature
expectItems.value: Prescribed novel + poetry + drama — deeper analysis than Grade 10

expectItems.label: Key shift
expectItems.value: Extended literary essays · sophisticated argument · NSC preparation

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Prose: character, theme and narrative technique
topics: Read prescribed novel — sustained analysis of character development, conflict, theme
Narrative technique: point of view, narrative distance, stream of consciousness, unreliable narrator
Identify and explain: irony (all types), allegory, intertextuality, extended metaphor
Literary essay: 400+ words — thesis, developed PEEL paragraphs, conclusion
Complex sentence structures: nominal, adjectival, adverbial clauses — use in own writing
Concord: difficult constructions — neither...nor, either...or, each, every, none
Vocabulary: connotation, denotation, register, jargon, euphemism, cliché — avoid in own writing
Oral: formal prepared speech — argue a position, anticipate counter-arguments

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Poetry: comparison and contextual analysis
topics: Analyse and compare three prescribed poems — theme, imagery, diction, tone, mood, form
Contextual question: explain a given extract in context of the full poem
Extended figures of speech: allusion, apostrophe, antithesis, chiasmus, zeugma
Poetic form and its effect: sonnet, free verse, dramatic monologue, ballad
Diction analysis: connotation, sound devices — assonance, consonance, sibilance
Formal letter, email, CV and covering letter — revision and refinement to NSC standard
Sentence combining: reduce multiple sentences to one sophisticated structure
Oral: poetry discussion — analyse and defend an interpretation

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Drama: full text analysis and essay
topics: Read full prescribed dramatic text — dramatic structure, theme, character, stagecraft
Dramatic devices: tragic flaw, deus ex machina, comic relief, dramatic irony, catharsis
Contextual question: place a given passage in the context of the full play
Extended dramatic essay: argue a thesis about theme or character across the whole text
Argumentative essay: sustained argument — 400+ words, with counter-argument and rebuttal
Transactional writing: proposal, memo, minutes, formal report — NSC formats
Participle and infinitive phrases as sentence elements
Oral: dramatic reading or debate

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Unseen comprehension, visual literacy and NSC preparation
topics: Unseen prose: apply full literary analysis skills — no prescribed text advantage
Unseen poetry: independent analysis — devices, tone, theme, form
Visual/media texts: multi-modal analysis — film still, infographic, advertisement, cartoon
Summary writing: 70-word and 100-word summaries — NSC technique
Creative writing: narrative, descriptive, reflective essays — planning, drafting, editing
Grammar consolidation: all tenses, voice, speech, concord, clauses, punctuation
NSC paper structure: Paper 1 (language), Paper 2 (literature), Paper 3 (writing) — understand each
Oral: final formal presentation — research-based, with visual support

skillChips: Write a sustained literary essay with a developed thesis
Analyse narrative technique in prose
Compare three poems using textual evidence
Place a passage in the context of the full text
Analyse drama for structure, stagecraft and theme
Write extended argumentative and discursive essays
Produce NSC-standard transactional texts
Write 70- and 100-word summaries accurately
Analyse unseen prose and poetry independently
Identify and explain allusion, antithesis, chiasmus
Apply concord in complex constructions
Use clause types accurately in own writing

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Know your prescribed texts inside out. Re-read key sections. Annotate quotes with the technique and effect. You cannot fake literary analysis.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: A thesis is an argument, not a statement of fact. 'The author uses irony' is not a thesis. 'The pervasive irony in the text exposes the hypocrisy of colonial authority' is a thesis.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Summary writing needs exact word count. Count your words. 70-word summaries that are 85 words lose marks. Practise cutting to the exact limit.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: NSC Paper 3 is timed writing under pressure. Practise writing a 400-word essay in 30 minutes. Speed and quality under time pressure is a learnable skill.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Grade 11 is your last chance to build habits. Every essay you write this year is practice for Grade 12. Take the feedback seriously.

subjects.hubDescription: Extended literary essays, NSC-standard writing, unseen analysis and exam preparation.

subjects.title: Grade 11 Life Orientation | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Life Orientation for Grade 11. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 11 Life Orientation continues the personal, social and career development of Grade 10 at a more sophisticated level, with a particular focus on matric preparation, career decision-making and social responsibility. All assessment is school-based — there is no final exam. The CAPS curriculum addresses personal wellbeing, citizenship, health, physical education and career planning at a level appropriate to learners entering their final school year.

expectItems.label: Four focus areas
expectItems.value: Personal development · citizenship · career · physical education

expectItems.label: Key focus
expectItems.value: Matric planning · career decisions · social justice · physical fitness

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Personal development: stress and resilience
topics: Matric stress: sources, physical and psychological symptoms, management strategies
Resilience: grit, growth mindset, post-traumatic growth — research and application
Time management: study timetable, avoiding procrastination, managing social media distraction
Sleep and cognitive performance: research on sleep deprivation and exam performance
Healthy lifestyle for matric: nutrition, exercise, hydration as cognitive tools
Physical Education: aerobic endurance training — measure and improve VO2 max
Fitness testing: establish Term 1 baseline; set measurable goals for the year
Study skills: revision strategies — spaced repetition, retrieval practice, interleaving

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Citizenship: social justice and human rights
topics: South Africa's social justice challenges: land, inequality, unemployment — statistical overview
The Constitution in action: how rights are enforced — courts, human rights commission, Public Protector
Gender-based violence: updated SA statistics, legal framework, community response strategies
LGBTQ+ rights: Constitution, challenges, allyship — respectful discussion
Environmental justice: climate change impacts on poor and marginalised communities in SA
Social media and activism: #FeesMustFall, #RhodesMustFall — power and limits of digital activism
Physical Education: team sport — strategy, leadership, refereeing — mature engagement
Community project: plan and implement a small community contribution

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Health: reproductive health and substance abuse
topics: Reproductive health: contraception efficacy rates, STI prevention, sexual rights
HIV/AIDS in Grade 11: treatment adherence, stigma reduction, peer education
Substance abuse: alcohol and drug use among SA youth — statistics, reasons, consequences
Addiction: neurological basis of addiction — dopamine, reward pathways — why willpower alone fails
Recovery: rehabilitation options in SA — SANCA, Narcotics Anonymous, community support
Mental health: eating disorders, self-harm, suicidal ideation — recognition and response protocols
Physical Education: individual fitness challenge or outdoor education activity
First aid revision: CPR update, AED awareness, snake bite, heat exhaustion

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Career: matric preparation and subject choice review
topics: APS calculation: how to calculate your Admission Point Score from NSC results
University programme requirements: research minimum APS and subject requirements for chosen programmes
Gap year: considerations — productive vs unproductive gap year, reapplication process
Alternative pathways: TVET colleges, learnerships, apprenticeships — dignity and value
Bursary applications: timelines, requirements, NSFAS application process for next year
Personal statement: write a 300-word personal statement for a bursary or university application
Physical Education: final fitness assessment — celebrate measurable improvement
Grade 12 preparation: what changes — intensity, time demands, external exams

skillChips: Apply evidence-based stress management strategies
Describe grit and growth mindset with examples
Explain SA's social justice challenges with statistics
Apply the Constitution to real human rights scenarios
Describe GBV legislation and support structures
Explain addiction using neurological concepts
Calculate APS from NSC results
Research university and TVET programme requirements
Write a 300-word personal statement
Apply first aid including CPR revision
Demonstrate improved physical fitness from Term 1
Plan a realistic matric study timetable

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8.5"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="4.8"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="1.1" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/></svg>
tips.text: SBA is your entire LO mark. Every submission, project and participation mark counts. There is no exam to save a poor SBA.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Personal statement needs a structure. Who you are → What you have achieved → What you want to study and why → How you will contribute. Use this every time.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8.5"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="4.8"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="1.1" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/></svg>
tips.text: PE is assessed practically. Consistent attendance, effort and correct technique = marks. Show up and try.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Use LO to plan Grade 12 seriously. APS, programme requirements, bursary timelines — research all three in Term 4 and act on what you find.

subjects.hubDescription: Matric planning, career decisions, social justice, health and physical education — SBA only.

subjects.title: Grade 11 Mathematical Literacy | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Mathematical Literacy for Grade 11. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.tagline: maths that makes sense in real life
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 11 Mathematical Literacy extends the real-world mathematical contexts of Grade 10 to more complex and multi-step problems. Learners apply mathematics to taxation, insurance, investment, maps, scale drawings, probability and data analysis. The emphasis is on accuracy, interpretation and communication — Mathematical Literacy is assessed in context at all times, and learners must be able to explain their reasoning in writing.

expectItems.label: Four topics
expectItems.value: Numbers · Patterns · Space & Shape · Data Handling

expectItems.label: Key shift
expectItems.value: Multi-step contextual problems · taxation · insurance · probability

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Advanced personal and business finance
topics: Income tax: SARS tax tables — calculate tax payable, tax rebate, net tax
PAYE: calculate from salary — understand payslip deductions fully
UIF: contribution rates, when it applies, how to claim
Medical aid: contribution types, savings account, risk pool — compare plans
Retirement planning: pension, provident fund, retirement annuity — concept and calculation
Hire purchase vs bank loan: compare total cost over the full term
Exchange rates: convert currency, interpret fluctuations — SA rand context
Inflation: calculate real purchasing power — effect on savings and income

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Patterns, graphs and break-even
topics: Non-linear graphs in context: parabola (projectile), hyperbola (inverse proportion) — interpret
Cost, revenue and profit functions: draw on same axes — identify break-even graphically
Tariff systems: electricity, water, mobile data — tiered pricing, calculate bills
Loan repayment graphs: outstanding balance over time — read and interpret
Rates of change: interpret gradient as rate in real contexts — speed, fuel consumption
Proportional reasoning: direct and inverse proportion in complex multi-step problems
Scale: maps, architectural plans — calculate actual dimensions, draw to scale
Graph critique: identify misleading features — truncated axes, inconsistent scale

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Space, shape and measurement
topics: Pythagoras theorem: apply in practical 2D contexts — building, navigation
Area and perimeter: complex composite shapes — irregular polygons, combined circles
Volume and surface area: cone, pyramid, sphere — apply in packaging and construction
Unit conversions: combined — e.g. km/h to m/s, litres to cubic centimetres
Floor plans and elevations: draw from description; calculate costs from floor plan
Tiling and paving: calculate number of tiles/pavers, allow for wastage, cost
Fuel and distance: calculate fuel cost for a road trip using consumption rates
Time and scheduling: project timelines — Gantt charts, critical path (introduction)

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Data handling and probability
topics: Sampling: types — random, systematic, stratified, cluster — when each is appropriate
Questionnaire design: bias, leading questions, response options — critique and improve
Represent data: all chart types — choose the most appropriate for the data
Ogive: cumulative frequency curve — draw, read off median and quartiles
Box-and-whisker: draw, compare two data sets, identify outliers
Standard deviation: concept — what it measures, interpret in context (no calculation required)
Probability: combined events — addition rule, complementary, mutually exclusive
Probability in real contexts: risk assessment, insurance premiums, weather probability

skillChips: Calculate income tax using SARS tax tables
Analyse a payslip including all deductions
Compare hire purchase and bank loan total costs
Convert between currencies using exchange rates
Draw and interpret cost, revenue and profit graphs
Identify break-even point from a graph
Apply Pythagoras in practical 2D contexts
Calculate volume and surface area of 3D shapes
Draw and read floor plans with correct scale
Draw and interpret an ogive
Compare two data sets using box-and-whisker plots
Interpret probability in real-world insurance and risk contexts

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="2" y="5" width="20" height="14" rx="2"/><path d="M2 10h20"/></svg>
tips.text: Tax tables are given — but you must know how to use them. Find the correct bracket, calculate the base tax, add the percentage of the excess. Practise this until it is automatic.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="4.5" y="2.5" width="15" height="19" rx="2"/><path d="M8 6.5h8"/><path d="M8 11h.01M12 11h.01M16 11h.01M8 15h.01M12 15h.01M16 15h.01M8 19h.01M12 19h.01M16 19h.01"/></svg>
tips.text: Always show units. 'R 4 320' not '4320'. '14.5 m²' not '14.5'. Missing units costs marks in every question.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="m3 16 6-6 4 4 8-9"/><path d="M15 5h6v6"/></svg>
tips.text: Choose the right graph type. Bar graph = comparing categories. Line graph = change over time. Pie chart = proportions of a whole. Histogram = frequency distribution.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="4.5" y="2.5" width="15" height="19" rx="2"/><path d="M8 6.5h8"/><path d="M8 11h.01M12 11h.01M16 11h.01M8 15h.01M12 15h.01M16 15h.01M8 19h.01M12 19h.01M16 19h.01"/></svg>
tips.text: Multi-step problems: write each step clearly. ML examiners mark each step. Even if your final answer is wrong, correct steps earn marks.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Context is everything in ML. After calculating, re-read the question. Does your answer make sense in the real-world situation? If not, check your working.

subjects.title: Grade 11 Mathematics | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Mathematics for Grade 11. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 11 Mathematics is the most demanding year of the FET Phase and the direct preparation for the Grade 12 NSC examination. The CAPS curriculum extends algebra, functions, trigonometry, Euclidean geometry, analytical geometry, statistics and probability to a level where formal proof and multi-step reasoning are central. Every topic in Grade 11 recurs in Grade 12 — mastery here is non-negotiable.

expectItems.label: Key topics
expectItems.value: Algebra · trig identities · Euclidean geometry proofs · analytical geometry

expectItems.label: Key shift
expectItems.value: Formal proof · trig identities · circle geometry · counting principles

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Algebra: quadratics, inequalities and surds
topics: Quadratic equations: completing the square (full), quadratic formula x = (−b ± √(b²−4ac)) / 2a
Quadratic inequalities: solve and represent on number line
Nature of roots: discriminant Δ = b² − 4ac — determine and interpret
Quadratic equations with rational expressions: algebraic fractions
Surds: simplify, rationalise the denominator, solve surd equations
Exponential equations: with different bases — use logs (introduction) or inspection
Simultaneous equations: one linear, one quadratic — full solution
Word problems: quadratic models in real contexts

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Functions: advanced and inverses
topics: Quadratic function y = a(x−p)² + q: transformations — shift, reflect, stretch
Cubic function: y = ax³ — basic shape, turning points, roots
Exponential function y = ab^(x+p) + q: transformations
Logarithmic function: y = log_a x — inverse of exponential, domain, range, graph
Inverse functions: definition, notation f⁻¹(x), restrict domain for inverse to be a function
Finance: compound interest, decay, nominal vs effective interest rates
Annuities: future value of annuity — F = x[(1+i)ⁿ − 1]/i
Loan repayment: present value of annuity — P = x[1−(1+i)^(−n)]/i

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Trigonometry and Euclidean geometry
topics: Trig identities: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, tanθ = sinθ/cosθ — prove and apply
Compound angle formulae: sin(A±B), cos(A±B), sin2A, cos2A
Trig equations: general solution — sin θ = k → θ = arcsin k + 360°n
2D and 3D trig problems: apply sine rule, cosine rule, area formula
Circle geometry theorems: angle at centre = 2 × angle at circumference
Cyclic quadrilateral: opposite angles supplementary
Tangent-chord angle: equals inscribed angle in alternate segment
Write formal proofs using circle geometry theorems

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Analytical geometry, statistics and probability
topics: Analytical geometry: distance, midpoint, gradient revision
Equation of a circle: (x−a)² + (y−b)² = r² — centre, radius, write equation
Tangent to circle: perpendicular to radius at point of tangency — find equation
Statistics: regression — least-squares regression line, correlation coefficient r
Interpret r: strength and direction of linear relationship
Probability: counting principles — fundamental counting principle, factorial notation
Permutations: ⁿPᵣ = n!/(n−r)! — with and without repetition
Combinations: ⁿCᵣ = n!/[r!(n−r)!] — apply in probability

skillChips: Solve quadratic equations using completing the square and the formula
Determine and interpret the discriminant
Solve quadratic inequalities
Simplify surds and rationalise denominators
Draw and interpret logarithmic and inverse functions
Calculate future and present value of annuities
Prove and apply trigonometric identities
Use compound angle formulae
Solve trig equations to general solution
Prove and apply circle geometry theorems
Find the equation of a circle and its tangent
Apply counting principles and permutations/combinations

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="4.5" y="2.5" width="15" height="19" rx="2"/><path d="M8 6.5h8"/><path d="M8 11h.01M12 11h.01M16 11h.01M8 15h.01M12 15h.01M16 15h.01M8 19h.01M12 19h.01M16 19h.01"/></svg>
tips.text: Quadratic formula: write it out every time. x = (−b ± √(b²−4ac)) / 2a. Do not try to remember the answer — derive it step by step.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Trig identity proofs: work on one side only. Choose the more complex side. Never move terms across the equals sign.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Circle geometry: state the theorem. Every angle calculation needs a reason: 'angle at centre is twice angle at circumference'. No reason = no mark.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="4.5" y="2.5" width="15" height="19" rx="2"/><path d="M8 6.5h8"/><path d="M8 11h.01M12 11h.01M16 11h.01M8 15h.01M12 15h.01M16 15h.01M8 19h.01M12 19h.01M16 19h.01"/></svg>
tips.text: Annuity formulae are given — but know what each variable means. F = future value, P = present value, x = payment, i = interest per period, n = number of periods.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Grade 11 Maths is the hardest year. The jump from Grade 10 is steep. Work consistently — weekly practice beats last-minute cramming every time.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: NSC letter layout is worth free marks. Adres, datum, verwysing, aanhef, liggaam, afsluiting. Every layout mark is predictable — never lose them.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Summaries: paraphrase, don't copy. If your summary sounds like the original, you will lose marks for not paraphrasing. Rewrite in your own words.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Figurative language: three steps, always. Identify the technique → Quote → Explain the effect on the reader. One step missing = marks lost.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Passive voice in all tenses. Word geskryf / is geskryf / sal geskryf word / sou geskryf word / is geskryf geword. Write all five from memory.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Past papers are the best revision tool. Three full past papers under timed conditions, marked with the memorandum, is worth more than a month of notes.
