subjects.expectIntro: Graad 12 Afrikaans Huistaal is die NSS-jaar. Elke taak tel. Leerders produseer hul beste letterkundige analise oor voorgeskrewe prosa, gedigte en drama, skryf gepoleerde formele opstelle en demonstreer beheer oor alle taalvaardighede. Vraestel 1 toets taal in konteks, Vraestel 2 toets letterkunde, en Vraestel 3 is uitgebreide skryfwerk. Daar is geen nuwe inhoud nie — hierdie jaar gaan oor meesterskap, toepassing en prestasie onder druk.

expectItems.label: Vraestel 2
expectItems.value: Letterkunde — prosa, gedigte, drama — voorgeskrewe tekste

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Prosahersiening en Vraestel 3-skryfwerk
topics: Diepgaande hersiening van voorgeskrewe roman — karakter, tema, narratiewe tegniek, literêre middele
Letterkundige opstel: tesis-gebaseerd, PEEL-paragrawe, 400–500 woorde — tydsgebonde oefening
Kontekstuele vrae: gedeelte in konteks, karaktermotivering, effek van taal
Narratiewe opstel: Graad 12-standaard — boeiende opening, ontwikkelde plot, bevredigende oplossing
Beskrywende opstel: sintuiglike detail, beeldspraak, gevarieerde sinstruktuur
Woordeskat vir skryfwerk: presiese woordkeuse, vermy cliché, gebruik konnotasie doelbewus
Vraestel 1-vaardighede: begripsstrategieë, opsommingtegniek — 70- en 100-woord opsommings
Mondeling: voorbereide toespraak — SBA-taak, formeel geassesseer

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Poësie en Vraestel 1-taal
topics: Voorgeskrewe gedigteantologie: hersien alle gedigte — tema, beelding, woordkeuse, toon, vorm
Vergelykende opstel: vergelyk twee of drie voorgeskrewe gedigte — 400+ woorde
Kontekstuele vrae oor poësie: verduidelik 'n strofe, identifiseer 'n middel, verduidelik die effek
Ongesiene poësie: onafhanklike analise — eksamentegniek en tydsberekening
Vraestel 1-taalvrae: woordsoorte, tye, stem, rede, kongruensie, bysinne
Begrip: letterlike, inferensiële, evalueringsvraeë, kritiese vrae — alle vraagsoorte
Visuele/mediateksanalise: multimodale vrae in Vraestel 1-formaat
Transaksionele skryfwerk hersiening: formele brief, verslag, CV — NSS-uitleg en register

termCards.label: Term 3

Kontekstuele vrae oor drama: gedeelte, subteks, dramatiese ironie, toneelkuns
Argumenterende en beskouende opstelle: finale polering — tydsgebonde 45-minuut-omstandighede
Vraestel 2-eksamentegniek: hoe om tyd te verdeel oor prosa-, poësie- en dramavrae
Vraestel 1-eksamentegniek: hoe om begrip-, opsomming- en taalafdelings te benader
Vraestel 3-eksamentegniek: beplan in 5 minute, skryf in 40, proeflees in 5

Hersiening: alle taalstrukture — tye, stem, rede, kongruensie, bysinne

Opstelskryfwerk: oefen een van elke soort per week — letterkundig, argumenterend, narratief
Vorige vraestelle: Vraestelle 1, 2 en 3 van vorige jare onder tydsgebonde omstandighede
Merk eie werk: gebruik merkriglyn om te identifiseer waar punte verloor word
NSS-eksamen: Vraestel 1 (3 uur), Vraestel 2 (3 uur), Vraestel 3 (2.5 uur)
Na-eksamen: reflekteer, vier, gaan vorentoe

Vergelyk voorgeskrewe gedigte in 'n uitgebreide opstel
Beantwoord kontekstuele vrae met presiese teksgetuienis
Analiseer ongesiene prosa en poësie onafhanklik
Skryf 'n gepoleerde narratiewe of beskrywende opstel
Skryf 'n argumenterende of beskouende opstel met teenargument
Produseer NSS-standaard transaksionele tekste uit die geheue
Skryf 70- en 100-woord opsommings akkuraat
Beantwoord alle Vraestel 1-taalvraagsoorte
Pas alle grammatika op NSS-vlak toe onder eksamenomstandighede
Verdeel tyd korrek oor alle drie vraestelle
Gebruik merkriglyn om eie foute te identifiseer en reg te stel

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Ken jou voorgeskrewe tekste van binne en van buite. Het 10 aanhalings gememoriseer vir elke teks met die tegniek en effek.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Tesis eerste, altyd. Voor jy 'n enkele liggaamsparagraaf skryf, skryf jou tesis. Dit neem 30 sekondes en spaar 20 minute se ongeorganiseerde skryfwerk.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Opsommingtegniek is gratis punte. Gebruik slegs die teks se inligting, parafraseer behoorlik, tel woorde presies, nommer jou punte.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Vraestel 1-taalvrae herhaal. Dieselfde grammatikale konstruksies verskyn elke jaar. Oefen vorige vraestelle.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Jy het die werk gedoen. Vertrou dit. Graad 12-eksamensenuweagtigheid is werklik. Asemhaal. Lees elke vraag twee keer. Wys jou denke. Jy het dit.

Trial exam: Papers 1 and 2 under full exam conditions
Mark trial exam: use NSC marking guidelines — identify specific marks lost

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Final revision and NSC examination
topics: Targeted revision: address weaknesses identified in trial exam
Past paper practice: at least three full sets of previous NSC papers
Writing practice: one essay per day in the week before the exam
Grammar: daily revision — 15 minutes per topic across all structures
Vocabulary: review personal word list compiled across Grade 12
Examination technique: read every question twice, answer what is asked, check word counts
NSC examination: Paper 1 and Paper 2
Post-exam: celebrate — you earned it

skillChips: Write NSC-standard formal letter and report under time pressure
Write a 300-word argumentative essay in 40 minutes
Write 70- and 100-word summaries accurately
Answer all Paper 1 language question types
Use passive voice in all tenses accurately
Apply all four conditional sentence types in writing
Identify and explain all types of figurative language
Analyse visual and multi-modal texts
Manage time across both NSC papers
Use NSC marking guidelines to identify own errors
Write confidently across all English text types
Demonstrate secure command of all FET grammar

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: NSC letter layout is free marks. Address, date, reference, salutation, body, closing. Predictable marks — never lose them.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Summaries: paraphrase, don't copy. If your summary sounds like the original, you lose marks. Rewrite everything in your own words.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Figurative language: three steps. Identify → Quote → Explain effect. Missing one step loses marks every time.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Passive in all tenses. Is written / was written / will be written / would be written / has been written. Know all five.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Past papers beat notes every time. Three timed past papers marked with the memo is the most effective exam preparation possible.

subjects.hubDescription: NSC exam technique — timed writing, summaries, language structures and past papers.

subjects.title: Grade 12 English Home Language | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned English Home Language for Grade 12. Term-by-term topics, skills, exam technique and free papers with memos.
subjects.tagline: this is what it's all been for
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 12 English Home Language is the NSC year. Every task counts toward your final mark. Learners produce their best literary analysis across prescribed prose, poetry and drama, write polished formal essays, and demonstrate command of all language skills developed across Grades 10 and 11. Paper 1 tests language in context, Paper 2 tests literature, and Paper 3 is extended writing. There is no new content — this year is about mastery, application and performance under pressure.

expectItems.label: Paper 2
expectItems.value: Literature — prose, poetry, drama — prescribed texts

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Prose revision and Paper 3 writing
topics: Deep revision of prescribed novel — character, theme, narrative technique, literary devices
Literary essay: thesis-driven, PEEL paragraphs, 400–500 words — timed practice
Contextual questions: passage in context, character motivation, effect of language
Narrative essay: Grade 12 standard — engaging opening, developed plot, satisfying resolution
Descriptive essay: sensory detail, figurative language, varied sentence structure
Vocabulary for writing: precise diction, avoiding cliché, using connotation deliberately
Paper 1 skills: comprehension strategies, summary technique — 70- and 100-word summaries
Oral: prepared speech — SBA task, formally assessed

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Poetry and Paper 1 language
topics: Prescribed poetry anthology: revise all poems — theme, imagery, diction, tone, form
Comparison essay: compare two or three prescribed poems — 400+ words
Contextual questions on poetry: explain a stanza, identify a device, explain its effect
Unseen poetry: independent analysis — exam technique and timing
Paper 1 language questions: parts of speech, tenses, voice, speech, concord, clauses
Comprehension: literal, inferential, evaluative, critical — all question types
Visual/media text analysis: multi-modal questions in Paper 1 format
Transactional writing revision: formal letter, report, CV — NSC layout and register

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Drama and final exam preparation
topics: Prescribed drama: full text revision — structure, character arc, dramatic devices, theme
Essay on drama: argue a thesis about character or theme — timed, under exam conditions
Contextual questions on drama: passage, subtext, dramatic irony, stagecraft
Argumentative and discursive essays: final polish — under 45-minute timed conditions
Paper 2 exam technique: how to allocate time across prose, poetry and drama questions
Paper 1 exam technique: how to approach comprehension, summary and language sections
Paper 3 exam technique: plan in 5 minutes, write in 40, proofread in 5
Trial exam: full paper under exam conditions — analyse results and target weak areas

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Targeted revision and NSC examination
topics: Revision: all prescribed texts — prose, poetry, drama — key quotes and analysis points
Revision: all grammar structures — tenses, voice, speech, concord, clauses
Summary writing: practise 10 summaries under timed conditions
Essay writing: practise one of each type per week — literary, argumentative, narrative
Past paper practice: Papers 1, 2 and 3 from previous years under timed conditions
Mark your own work: use marking guidelines to identify where you lose marks
NSC exam: Paper 1 (3 hours), Paper 2 (3 hours), Paper 3 (2.5 hours)
Post-exam: reflect, celebrate, move forward

skillChips: Write a thesis-driven literary essay in under 45 minutes
Compare prescribed poems in an extended essay
Answer contextual questions with precise textual evidence
Analyse unseen prose and poetry independently
Write a polished narrative or descriptive essay
Write an argumentative or discursive essay with counter-argument
Produce NSC-standard transactional texts from memory
Write 70- and 100-word summaries accurately
Answer all Paper 1 language question types
Apply all grammar at NSC level under exam conditions
Allocate time correctly across all three papers
Use marking guidelines to identify and fix own errors

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Know your prescribed texts by heart. Have 10 quotes memorised for each text with the technique and effect. You should be able to write a paragraph about any character or theme without thinking.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Thesis first, always. Before writing a single body paragraph, write your thesis. It takes 30 seconds and saves 20 minutes of unfocused writing.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Summary technique is free marks. Use only the text's information, paraphrase properly, count words exactly, number your points. These are systematic marks — don't lose them.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Paper 1 language questions recycle. The same grammar constructions appear every year. Practise past papers and you will see the patterns.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: You have done the work. Trust it. Grade 12 exam nerves are real. Breathe. Read every question twice. Show your thinking. You've got this.

subjects.hubDescription: NSC exam preparation — prescribed texts, literary essays, Paper 1 language and Paper 3 writing.

subjects.title: Grade 12 Life Orientation | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Life Orientation for Grade 12. Term-by-term topics, skills, exam technique and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 12 Life Orientation is the final year and all assessment is school-based — there is no external exam. The CAPS curriculum focuses on completing the personal, social and career development journey of the FET Phase, with particular emphasis on life after matric, application processes and managing the transition to tertiary education, work or entrepreneurship. Every LO submission counts directly toward your final mark.

expectItems.label: Four focus areas
expectItems.value: Personal development · citizenship · career · physical education

expectItems.label: Key tasks
expectItems.value: Personal development plan · career application · community project

expectItems.label: Key focus
expectItems.value: Life after matric · application processes · transition planning

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Personal development: matric pressure and resilience
topics: Managing matric stress: evidence-based strategies — exercise, sleep, social support, time management
Burnout vs stress: how to recognise burnout early and what to do
Revision strategies backed by cognitive science: retrieval practice, spaced repetition, interleaving
Sleep and exam performance: why 8 hours matters more than an extra hour of study
Nutrition and hydration for cognitive performance during exam season
Physical Education: personal fitness programme — self-designed, self-monitored
Fitness assessment: final Senior Phase baseline comparison — celebrate improvement
Goal setting: SMART goals for matric results, gap year and tertiary entry

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Citizenship and social responsibility
topics: SA's democratic challenges: voter apathy, corruption, state capture — what young people can do
Environmental responsibility: climate justice, COP commitments, SA's renewable energy transition
Digital citizenship: cyber law in SA, POPIA, responsible social media use at 18+
Community project: design, implement and reflect — minimum 8 hours of meaningful contribution
Gender-based violence: personal commitment to prevention and allyship
Volunteerism and civic engagement: how to find and participate in SA community organisations
Physical Education: team sport — final season, leadership roles, sportsmanship
Reflect on growth as a citizen across the FET Phase

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Applications and career transition
topics: University application: NSFAS application, CAO/institutional applications — deadlines and process
TVET and FET college application: programmes, requirements, NCV and N-course pathways
Bursary application: write and submit at least one bursary application — reviewed and refined
Gap year planning: structured vs unstructured — how to make a gap year productive
Learnership and apprenticeship: how to find them, requirements, NQF levels
Interview skills: prepare for a tertiary or job interview — mock interview practice
Physical Education: individual activity of choice — maintain active lifestyle
Personal development plan: final version — subject results, career goals, action steps, timeline

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Transition, exam support and celebration
topics: NSC exam support: time management strategies, dealing with exam anxiety, the night before
Post-exam planning: receiving results, understanding your APS, supplementary exams
Gap year vs immediate study: make a conscious, researched decision
Financial literacy for young adults: opening a bank account, budgeting independently, avoiding debt
Rights as an adult in SA: at 18 you can vote, sign contracts, access financial services
Physical Education: fun final activity — celebrate the physical journey
SBA portfolio: submit final portfolio — check all tasks are included and complete
Celebrate: you have completed 12 years of school

skillChips: Apply evidence-based exam stress management strategies
Design and execute a personal fitness programme
Explain SA's democratic processes and citizenship responsibilities
Plan and reflect on a meaningful community project
Submit a complete bursary or tertiary application
Write a polished personal statement
Plan a realistic post-matric transition
Apply financial literacy skills as an independent adult
Manage time effectively across NSC exam season
Identify and use SA support structures for tertiary access
Demonstrate sustained physical fitness improvement
Reflect on personal growth across the FET Phase

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8.5"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="4.8"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="1.1" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/></svg>
tips.text: Every SBA submission is your exam. There is no NSC paper. Every task is a direct mark. Submit everything, on time, to your best ability.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Personal development plan must be specific. Vague plans score low. Subject results → APS → programme requirement → institution → application date → action taken. Be specific.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: The community project needs a reflection. Implementation alone is not enough. Reflect on what you contributed, what you learned and how you grew. That reflection earns marks.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M2 9 12 4l10 5-10 5z"/><path d="M6 11.5V17c0 1.5 2.7 3 6 3s6-1.5 6-3v-5.5"/><path d="M22 9v6"/></svg>
tips.text: Start applications in Term 3, not Term 4. NSFAS, CAO and most bursaries close before matric results are released. Don't wait for results to apply.

subjects.hubDescription: Final LO year — matric support, applications, community project and transition planning. SBA only.

subjects.title: Grade 12 Mathematical Literacy | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Mathematical Literacy for Grade 12. Term-by-term topics, skills, exam technique and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 12 Mathematical Literacy is the NSC year. Learners apply all the real-world mathematical skills of Grades 10 and 11 to complex, multi-step problems across finance, measurement, data and maps. Paper 1 is a basic skills paper and Paper 2 is a complex application paper — both are contextual throughout. The key is accuracy, showing all working and interpreting results in context.

expectItems.label: Paper 1
expectItems.value: Basic skills — all four topics, straightforward context

expectItems.label: Key focus
expectItems.value: Exam technique · multi-step problems · financial literacy

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Advanced finance and taxation
topics: Income tax: full calculation using tax tables — rebates, thresholds, medical tax credits
Net salary calculation: gross income → deductions → net pay — full payslip
VAT: VAT-inclusive/exclusive in business contexts — complete invoices
Compound interest and depreciation: A = P(1+i)ⁿ and A = P(1−i)ⁿ — apply to vehicles, property
Loan repayment: instalment calculations, total repayment, interest paid — compare loan offers
Exchange rates: multi-step currency conversions — holiday budget, import/export context
Inflation: calculate real value over time — pension, savings, living costs
Insurance: premiums, excess, claims — interpret policy documents

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Measurement, maps and scale
topics: Pythagoras in 3D contexts: find missing lengths in prisms and pyramids
Surface area and volume: cone, sphere, pyramid — apply in packaging, architecture, civil contexts
Unit conversion: complex multi-step — e.g. litres/second to kilolitres/hour
Scale drawings: read and draw floor plans, site plans — calculate actual measurements
Maps: read a topographic map — contour lines, gradient, distance
GPS coordinates: interpret and use — practical navigation context
Project planning: timelines, Gantt charts, cost calculations — construction or event context
Tiling/paving: calculate quantities with wastage, compare quotes, calculate total cost

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Data, probability and exam practice
topics: Data: sampling, collection, organisation — evaluate research methodology
Represent data: choose the correct graph type, draw accurately, label fully
Five-number summary: min, Q1, median, Q3, max — from raw and grouped data
Box-and-whisker: draw and compare two data sets — identify outliers and skewness
Ogive: draw from cumulative frequency table — use to find percentiles
Scatter plot: line of best fit — make predictions, interpret correlation
Probability: combined events — addition rule, tree diagrams, two-way tables
Trial exam: Papers 1 and 2 under full exam conditions — use memorandum to identify gaps

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Final revision and NSC examination
topics: Targeted revision: address weaknesses identified in trial exam
Finance: practise all calculation types — tax, interest, depreciation, exchange rates
Measurement: practise area, volume, surface area — all shapes, with unit conversion
Data: practise drawing and interpreting all graph types under timed conditions
Probability: practise tree diagrams and two-way tables — read questions carefully
Past paper practice: at least three full sets under timed conditions
Examination technique: show all working, include units, interpret answers in context
NSC examination: Paper 1 (3 hours), Paper 2 (3 hours)

skillChips: Calculate net salary from gross income using a full payslip
Apply income tax tables to calculate tax payable
Calculate compound interest and depreciation
Complete a full loan repayment analysis
Apply Pythagoras in 3D measurement contexts
Calculate volume and surface area of cones, spheres and pyramids
Read topographic maps and calculate gradient
Draw and interpret an ogive and box-and-whisker plot
Construct and interpret a scatter plot with line of best fit
Calculate probability using tree diagrams and two-way tables
Manage time across both NSC papers
Show all working and interpret every answer in context

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="2" y="5" width="20" height="14" rx="2"/><path d="M2 10h20"/></svg>
tips.text: Tax tables are given — master them. Find your bracket, read the base tax, add the percentage of the excess. Write every step. This is a 20+ mark question in Paper 2.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="4.5" y="2.5" width="15" height="19" rx="2"/><path d="M8 6.5h8"/><path d="M8 11h.01M12 11h.01M16 11h.01M8 15h.01M12 15h.01M16 15h.01M8 19h.01M12 19h.01M16 19h.01"/></svg>
tips.text: Units in every answer, every time. R, m², litres, km/h — missing units costs marks systematically across both papers.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="m3 16 6-6 4 4 8-9"/><path d="M15 5h6v6"/></svg>
tips.text: Paper 2 questions are multi-step. Read the full question before calculating. Identify what is being asked in the last sentence. Then work backwards to find what you need.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="4.5" y="2.5" width="15" height="19" rx="2"/><path d="M8 6.5h8"/><path d="M8 11h.01M12 11h.01M16 11h.01M8 15h.01M12 15h.01M16 15h.01M8 19h.01M12 19h.01M16 19h.01"/></svg>
tips.text: Show every step of working. ML examiners award marks at each step. A wrong final answer with correct working still earns partial marks.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Past papers are the best prep. ML questions repeat contexts and calculation types. Three timed past papers with the memo is the most efficient revision possible.

subjects.hubDescription: NSC exam preparation — taxation, finance, measurement, data and probability in context.

subjects.title: Grade 12 Mathematics | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Mathematics for Grade 12. Term-by-term topics, skills, exam technique and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 12 Mathematics is the NSC year. The CAPS curriculum consolidates all FET content — algebra, functions, calculus, trigonometry, Euclidean geometry, analytical geometry, statistics and probability — and introduces differential calculus as a major new topic. Paper 1 covers algebra, functions, calculus, finance and probability. Paper 2 covers statistics, analytical geometry, trigonometry and Euclidean geometry. Every concept from Grades 10 and 11 reappears — mastery of prior content is non-negotiable.

expectItems.label: Paper 2
expectItems.value: Statistics · analytical geometry · trig · Euclidean geometry

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Calculus: limits, derivatives and applications
topics: Limits: definition, calculate limits from first principles — f'(x) = lim[f(x+h)−f(x)]/h
Differentiate from first principles: polynomials, f(x) = xⁿ
Differentiation rules: power rule, sum/difference rule, constant multiple
Notation: f'(x), dy/dx, Dₓ[f(x)]
Differentiate: polynomials, rational functions (rewrite first), surd functions
Applications: gradient of tangent at a point — find equation of tangent and normal
Second derivative: f''(x) — concavity, points of inflection
Cubic functions: sketch using derivatives — intercepts, stationary points, concavity

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Functions, finance and sequences
topics: Quadratic, exponential, logarithmic functions: full revision — transformations, inverses
Determine equations of functions from graphs — all types
Exponential equations and logarithms: solve using log laws
Arithmetic sequences: Tₙ = a + (n−1)d, Sₙ = n/2(2a + (n−1)d)
Geometric sequences: Tₙ = arⁿ⁻¹, Sₙ = a(rⁿ−1)/(r−1), S∞ = a/(1−r) for |r| < 1
Financial mathematics: nominal vs effective interest rates — convert between them
Annuities: future value F = x[(1+i)ⁿ−1]/i, present value P = x[1−(1+i)^(−n)]/i
Sinking fund: set up and solve — replace an asset after depreciation

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Trigonometry and geometry
topics: Trig identities: full revision — prove compound angle, double angle identities
Trig equations: general solution and specific interval
2D and 3D trig problems: sine rule, cosine rule, area formula — multi-step
Euclidean geometry: full revision — triangle theorems, circle theorems
Circle theorem proofs: write formal proofs — state theorem, reason at every step
Analytical geometry: circle equation, tangent to circle, perpendicular bisector
Trial exam: full Papers 1 and 2 under exam conditions
Mark trial exam: use marking guidelines — identify specific topics losing marks

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Final revision and NSC examination
topics: Targeted revision: calculus, trig identities, circle geometry, sequences — based on trial exam gaps
Past papers: at least three full sets under timed conditions
Paper 1 technique: calculus questions — show derivative first, then application
Paper 2 technique: geometry proofs — state theorem at every step, never assume
Statistics: regression, correlation — interpret r-value, use least-squares line
Probability: counting principles, permutations, combinations — practise varied question types
Examination: Paper 1 (3 hours), Paper 2 (3 hours)
Post-exam: reflect on the journey — you have grown enormously

skillChips: Differentiate from first principles
Apply differentiation rules to polynomials, rational and surd functions
Find equations of tangents and normals
Sketch cubic functions using calculus
Solve problems using arithmetic and geometric series
Calculate future and present value of annuities
Set up and solve sinking fund problems
Prove and apply all trig identities
Solve trig equations to general solution
Write formal Euclidean geometry proofs
Find equations of circles and tangents
Interpret regression and correlation in statistics

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="4.5" y="2.5" width="15" height="19" rx="2"/><path d="M8 6.5h8"/><path d="M8 11h.01M12 11h.01M16 11h.01M8 15h.01M12 15h.01M16 15h.01M8 19h.01M12 19h.01M16 19h.01"/></svg>
tips.text: Calculus: show the derivative before applying it. Write f'(x) = ... before finding the gradient, maximum or minimum. Examiners award a method mark for the derivative.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Geometry proofs: every statement needs a reason. (angles of a triangle = 180°), (tangent ⊥ radius), (opp. angles of cyclic quad. are supp.). No reason = no mark.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Series: identify arithmetic or geometric first. Check if there is a common difference (arithmetic) or common ratio (geometric) before choosing a formula.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="4.5" y="2.5" width="15" height="19" rx="2"/><path d="M8 6.5h8"/><path d="M8 11h.01M12 11h.01M16 11h.01M8 15h.01M12 15h.01M16 15h.01M8 19h.01M12 19h.01M16 19h.01"/></svg>
tips.text: Calculus applications follow a fixed method. Find the derivative → set it to zero → solve → classify using second derivative. Always in that order.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Every past paper marks the same topics. Calculus, trig identities and circle geometry appear in every NSC paper. Master these three first.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Vir begripsopgawes — soek die antwoord in die teks. Die meeste antwoorde op letterlike vrae is direk in die gegewe teks. Leer om die teks te skandeer vir sleutelwoorde.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Moenie bang wees om foute te maak nie. Die beste manier om Afrikaans te leer is om dit te gebruik — selfs as dit nie perfek is nie. Elke fout is 'n kans om te leer.

subjects.expectIntro: Afrikaans Home Language in Grade 4 is taught to learners for whom Afrikaans is their primary home language. The CAPS curriculum covers four integrated skills: listening and speaking, reading and viewing, writing and presenting, and language structures and conventions. By the end of Grade 4, learners are expected to read Afrikaans texts independently, write structured paragraphs, and demonstrate a solid understanding of Afrikaans grammar. The content and skills mirror those of English HL but are applied within the Afrikaans language.

Gebruik verlede, teenwoordige en toekomende tyd korrek
Skryf 'n gestruktureerde paragraaf
Identifiseer tipe sinne

Herken vergelykings en alliterasie

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Lees die vrae voor die gedeelte. In begripstoetse maak dit dit baie makliker om die antwoord vinnig te vind. Onderstreep sleutelwoorde in elke vraag voordat jy begin lees.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Gebruik die merktoedeling as riglyn. A question worth (2) needs two separate points. 'n Vraag wat (1) werd is, benodig slegs een duidelike antwoord. Skryf nooit 'n enkele woord vir 'n 2-merkervraag nie.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Haal altyd aan uit die teks wanneer jy bewys gee. Skryf: 'Die teks sê …' om die eksaminator presies te wys waar jy jou bewys gevind het.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Leer jou woordsoorte deur jou eie voorbeelde te maak. Skryf jou eie sinne met naamwoorde, werkwoorde en byvoeglike naamwoorde uit jou alledaagse lewe.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M12 7v5l3.5 2"/></svg>
tips.text: Kontroleer jou tye nadat jy geskryf het. Een van die mees algemene foute in Graad 4-skryfwerk is om tussen verlede en teenwoordige tyd te wissel. Gaan terug en kontroleer elke werkwoord.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Bou woordeskat deur 'n woordeboek te hou. Elke keer as jy 'n woord lees wat jy nie ken nie, skryf dit neer met sy betekenis en gebruik dit in 'n sin.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Build vocabulary every day. Learn 5 new English words every day. Write them down with a meaning in your home language and use each one in a sentence. Within a month you will have 150 new words.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Read the question before the passage. In comprehension tests, knowing what you are looking for makes it much easier to find the answer. Underline key words in each question first.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: For comprehension — find the answer in the text. Most answers to literal questions are directly in the given text. Learn to scan the text for keywords from the question.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Do not be afraid to make mistakes. The best way to learn English is to use it — even if it is not perfect. Every mistake is a chance to improve.

By the end of the year, learners should be able to read a passage independently, answer both literal and inferential questions, write a basic paragraph with a topic sentence, and identify core parts of speech such as nouns, verbs and adjectives.

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Narrative Texts, Nouns & Sentences
topics: Reading and comprehension of short narrative texts
Common nouns, proper nouns and collective nouns

Identify nouns, verbs, adjectives

Identify types of sentences

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Read the questions before the passage. In comprehension tests, knowing what you are looking for makes it much easier to find the answer quickly and accurately. Underline key words in each question before you start reading.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Use the mark allocation as a guide. A question worth (2) marks needs two separate points. A question worth (1) mark needs only one clear answer. Never write a single word for a 2-mark question.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Quote from the passage when giving evidence. When asked to support your answer, copy a short phrase from the text. Write: "The text says '…'" to show the examiner exactly where you found your evidence.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Learn your parts of speech by making your own examples. Don't just memorise definitions — write your own sentences using nouns, verbs and adjectives from your everyday life. "Thandi (noun) quickly (adverb) ate (verb) a delicious (adjective) mango."

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M12 7v5l3.5 2"/></svg>
tips.text: Check your tenses after you write. One of the most common errors in Grade 4 writing is switching between past and present tense mid-paragraph. After finishing a writing task, go back and check every verb — are they all in the same tense?

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Build vocabulary by keeping a word book. Every time you read a word you don't know, write it down with its meaning and use it in a sentence. Strong vocabulary is the single biggest advantage in English exams — it helps you understand passages and write better answers.

By the end of Grade 4, learners should be able to write a short isiZulu paragraph and answer basic comprehension questions.

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Introduction & simple isiZulu texts
topics: Basic isiZulu vocabulary — greetings (sanibonani, sawubona), family, colours, numbers
Simple narrative texts — read and answer literal questions
Common nouns (amagama aqondisa izinto) — people, animals, things
Present tense of common isiZulu verbs
Write short isiZulu sentences about yourself and your family
Oral: basic isiZulu greetings and classroom conversations

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Description & vocabulary building
topics: Read descriptive isiZulu texts and identify key information
Adjectives (amagama achazayo) — colour, size, shape
Singular and plural forms of simple isiZulu nouns
Basic punctuation in isiZulu texts
Write a short description of a picture or place in isiZulu
Oral: describe a picture using simple isiZulu sentences

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Informational texts & past tense
topics: Read simple isiZulu informational texts — notices, instructions
Simple past tense (isikhathi esedlule) of regular isiZulu verbs
Synonyms — vocabulary expansion in isiZulu
Prepared reading with focus on isiZulu pronunciation and tone
Write a short report about an activity or event in isiZulu
Oral: tell about a past experience using isiZulu past tense

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Revision & poetry
topics: Simple persuasive and poetic isiZulu texts — identify the main idea
Rhyme (ukuphinda) and rhythm in simple isiZulu poems (izinkondlo)
Revision of nouns, verbs and adjectives in isiZulu
Revision of present and past tense in isiZulu
Write a simple short isiZulu poem or rhyme
Oral: recite a memorised isiZulu poem or rhyme (inkondlo)

Sebenzisa amagama abalulekile ngokufanele

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Ukuqonda — thola impendulo embhalweni. Izimpendulo eziningi zezibuzo zamazwi aqondile zitholakala ngqo embhalweni onikwayo.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>

subjects.title: Grade 4 Life Skills | CAPS Study Materials | Curio Learning
subjects.description: Grade 4 Life Skills study materials aligned to CAPS. Beginning Knowledge, Creative Arts and Physical Education — free study guides and support.
subjects.expectIntro: Life Skills in Grade 4 is a broad subject that combines three distinct components: Beginning Knowledge and Personal and Social Wellbeing, Creative Arts, and Physical Education. Together they develop the whole learner — intellectually, creatively, socially and physically. The Beginning Knowledge component covers personal health, safety, relationships and the environment. Creative Arts develops visual art, music, drama and dance skills. Physical Education builds physical fitness, team skills and an understanding of movement.

expectItems.label: Three components
expectItems.value: Beginning Knowledge · Creative Arts · Physical Education

expectItems.label: Key focus
expectItems.value: Whole-learner development — mind, body and creative expression

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Personal wellbeing & creative arts
topics: Personal identity: who am I? — strengths, values, interests
Relationships: family, friends, community — roles and responsibilities
Healthy lifestyle: nutrition, exercise, rest and hygiene
Road safety and personal safety rules
Creative Arts — Visual Art: drawing and painting using line, shape and colour
Creative Arts — Music: rhythm, beat, tempo — clap and sing
Physical Education: locomotor movements — running, jumping, hopping
Ball skills: catching, throwing, kicking

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Social wellbeing, environment & arts
topics: Emotions: identifying, naming and managing feelings
Peer pressure: recognising and responding assertively
Drug, alcohol and tobacco awareness — health risks
My community: local services, roles and responsibilities
Creative Arts — Drama: freeze, mime and role play
Creative Arts — Dance: movement to music, body awareness
Physical Education: non-locomotor movements — bending, twisting, stretching
Athletics: running, jumping for distance and height

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Environment, culture & creative expression
topics: Environmental awareness: pollution, conservation, recycling
Human rights and responsibilities — everyone belongs
Cultural diversity in South Africa — celebrating differences
Creative Arts — Visual Art: collage, clay and 3D construction
Creative Arts — Music: simple songs and action songs
Physical Education: games skills — striking, fielding
Team games: rules, fair play and cooperation
Physical fitness: flexibility, strength and endurance activities

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Revision, performance & physical challenge
topics: Revision: personal safety, healthy choices, emotions and community
Creative Arts — performance: share and present creative work
Creative Arts — Music: play simple percussion instruments
Physical Education: gymnastics — rolling, balancing and jumping sequences
Outdoor games and small-sided team games
Goal setting: personal growth targets for Grade 5
Life skills revision: making good choices in different situations
Celebrating achievements — individual and group

skillChips: Identify personal strengths and values
Describe healthy lifestyle choices
Name road safety and personal safety rules
Identify and manage emotions
Recognise peer pressure and respond assertively
Describe local community services
Create artwork using line, shape and colour
Demonstrate rhythm and beat in music
Perform locomotor and non-locomotor movements
Play team games with fair play
Describe environmental responsibilities
Explain the importance of cultural diversity
Identify health risks of drugs, alcohol and tobacco
Set personal goals

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8.5"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="4.8"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="1.1" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/></svg>
tips.text: For written tests — learn key vocabulary. Life Skills tests often ask you to define terms like 'peer pressure', 'assertive', 'nutrition' and 'conservation'. Learn the correct definitions and practise using them in sentences.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 3v5M12 16v5M3 12h5M16 12h5M6 6l3 3M15 15l3 3M18 6l-3 3M9 15l-3 3"/></svg>
tips.text: Creative Arts assessments reward effort and process. In visual art and music, teachers assess your effort, creativity and understanding of concepts as much as the final product. Engage fully and explain your thinking.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8.5"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="4.8"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="1.1" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/></svg>
tips.text: Physical Education is assessed practically. PE marks come from participation and correct technique. Attend every lesson, try your best and listen carefully to instructions on how to perform each skill correctly.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Link Life Skills to your real life. The best way to remember content is to connect it to your own experience. When you study emotions, think about a time you felt that way. When you study safety rules, think about your journey to school.

subjects.title: Grade 4 Mathematics | CAPS Study Materials | Curio Learning
subjects.description: Grade 4 Mathematics study materials aligned to the CAPS curriculum. Numbers, operations, fractions, geometry, measurement and data — free papers and memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 4 Mathematics marks the transition from concrete number work to more abstract mathematical thinking. The CAPS curriculum covers five main content areas: Numbers, Operations and Relationships, Patterns, Functions and Algebra, Space and Shape (Geometry), Measurement, and Data Handling. Learners work with whole numbers up to 10 000, are introduced to common fractions, and begin to solve multi-step problems. Mental mathematics and number sense remain central — a strong Grade 4 mathematician can calculate quickly, spot patterns and explain their reasoning.

expectItems.label: Number range
expectItems.value: Whole numbers to 10 000 · Fractions halves, thirds, quarters

expectItems.label: Key shift
expectItems.value: Concrete counting → abstract operations → problem solving

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Whole numbers, operations & patterns
topics: Count, order, compare and represent whole numbers to 10 000
Place value: units, tens, hundreds, thousands
Addition and subtraction to 10 000 with and without regrouping
Multiplication tables: 2, 3, 4, 5, 10 — mental recall
Number patterns — extend and describe rules
2D shapes: identify, name and describe properties
Symmetry — lines of symmetry in shapes
Mental mathematics: round numbers to nearest 10 and 100

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Fractions, multiplication & geometry
topics: Common fractions: halves, thirds, quarters, fifths, sixths, eighths, tenths
Fractions on a number line — order and compare
Multiplication: 2-digit × 1-digit using expanded notation
Division: sharing and grouping with remainders
3D objects: cubes, rectangular prisms, pyramids, cylinders, cones, spheres
Length: estimate, measure and record using mm, cm, m, km
Perimeter of 2D shapes — count and calculate
Area using informal units and then standard units

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Properties of operations, time & data
topics: Properties of operations: commutative, associative, distributive
Multiples and factors — identify and list
Division: long division with 2-digit divisors (introduction)
Numeric and geometric patterns — tables and rules
Time: read analogue and digital clocks, calculate intervals
Mass: estimate, measure and record using g and kg
Capacity/Volume: estimate, measure and record using ml and l
Data: collect, organise and represent in tally tables and bar graphs

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Revision, problem solving & data
topics: Revision of all four operations with whole numbers to 10 000
Word problems: multi-step with all four operations
Equivalent fractions — halves, quarters, eighths
Transformations: tessellations and symmetry patterns
Temperature: read thermometers in °C
Probability: language of probability (certain, impossible, likely, unlikely)
Data revision: pictographs and bar graphs with many-to-one correspondence
Number sentences and solving for unknowns: □ + 5 = 12

skillChips: Count, order and compare numbers to 10 000
Know multiplication tables to 10×10
Add and subtract with regrouping
Multiply 2-digit by 1-digit numbers
Divide with remainders
Work with common fractions
Identify and describe 2D and 3D shapes
Measure length, mass, capacity and temperature
Calculate perimeter and area
Read analogue and digital clocks
Extend and describe number patterns
Collect and represent data in graphs
Solve multi-step word problems
Round numbers to nearest 10 and 100

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="4.5" y="2.5" width="15" height="19" rx="2"/><path d="M8 6.5h8"/><path d="M8 11h.01M12 11h.01M16 11h.01M8 15h.01M12 15h.01M16 15h.01M8 19h.01M12 19h.01M16 19h.01"/></svg>
tips.text: Learn your multiplication tables first. Almost everything in Grade 4 Maths — fractions, division, word problems — requires fast multiplication. Spend 5 minutes every day drilling your tables until they are automatic.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Show all your working. In tests, marks are given for method not just the answer. Even if your final answer is wrong, you can still earn marks by showing correct working steps.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Underline what the question is asking. Word problems contain a lot of information. Underline the question (usually the last sentence) and the key numbers before you start calculating.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="4.5" y="2.5" width="15" height="19" rx="2"/><path d="M8 6.5h8"/><path d="M8 11h.01M12 11h.01M16 11h.01M8 15h.01M12 15h.01M16 15h.01M8 19h.01M12 19h.01M16 19h.01"/></svg>
tips.text: Check your answer by working backwards. After solving, verify by reversing the operation. If you found 48 ÷ 6 = 8, check: 8 × 6 = 48. This takes 5 seconds and catches most errors.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="m3 16 6-6 4 4 8-9"/><path d="M15 5h6v6"/></svg>
tips.text: Draw a picture for geometry questions. If a question describes a shape or space problem, draw it out before calculating. A sketch helps you see what operation is needed.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Mental maths daily makes everything easier. Practise adding and subtracting multiples of 10 and 100 in your head. A strong number sense means less calculator dependence and faster working in tests.

subjects.title: Grade 4 Natural Sciences & Technology | CAPS Study Materials | Curio Learning
subjects.description: Grade 4 Natural Sciences and Technology study materials aligned to CAPS. Life, matter, energy and planet Earth — free papers and memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Natural Sciences and Technology in Grade 4 combines science investigation with basic technology design, giving learners a foundation for understanding both the natural world and how humans interact with it. The CAPS curriculum is structured around four knowledge strands: Life and Living, Matter and Materials, Energy and Change, and Planet Earth and Beyond. Learners conduct simple investigations, ask questions, make predictions, observe and record results. The Technology component introduces learners to the design process — identifying a problem, designing and making a solution, and evaluating it.

expectItems.label: Main strands
expectItems.value: Life & Living · Matter & Materials · Energy & Change · Planet Earth

expectItems.label: Key skill
expectItems.value: Scientific investigation: observe, predict, test, record, conclude

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Life and living — plants
topics: Structure and function of plants: roots, stem, leaves, flowers, fruit, seeds
How plants make food: photosynthesis — sunlight, water, carbon dioxide
Conditions for plant growth: light, water, soil, temperature
Plant adaptations: succulents, water plants, desert plants
Technology: design and build a simple plant watering system
Investigation: test what plants need to grow (fair test)
Classification: flowering vs non-flowering plants
SA indigenous plants and their importance

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Matter and materials
topics: Properties of materials: hard/soft, rough/smooth, transparent/opaque, flexible/rigid
Metals and non-metals — properties and uses
Magnetic and non-magnetic materials — investigation
Conductors and insulators of heat and electricity
Physical changes: dissolving, melting, evaporation
Technology: choose appropriate materials for a design task
Mixtures: sand and water, sand and salt — separating mixtures
Responsible use and recycling of materials

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Energy and change
topics: Forms of energy: light, heat, sound, kinetic, potential, electrical
Sources of energy: sun, fire, electricity, food
Sound: vibration, pitch, volume — investigation
Light: reflection, shadows, transparent vs opaque
Electricity: simple circuits — battery, wire, bulb, switch
Technology: design and build a simple electrical circuit
Non-renewable vs renewable energy sources
Energy conservation in South Africa

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Planet Earth and beyond
topics: Structure of the Earth: crust, mantle, core
Rocks: igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic — formation and properties
Soil: components, types and importance for plant growth
Erosion: causes, effects and prevention
The solar system: the Sun, eight planets and their order
Day and night: rotation of the Earth
Seasons: revolution of the Earth around the Sun
Technology: make a model of the solar system

skillChips: Plan and conduct fair tests
Identify structures and functions in plants and animals
Describe properties of common materials
Classify materials as magnetic/non-magnetic
Explain physical changes
Build and describe a simple electrical circuit
Name and describe forms of energy
Describe the structure of the Earth
Explain day, night and seasons
Name the planets in order from the Sun
Design a solution to a simple technology problem
Record and present investigation results
Identify renewable and non-renewable energy sources
Explain the importance of soil

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M9 2h6M10 2v6.5L4.5 18a2 2 0 0 0 1.7 3h11.6a2 2 0 0 0 1.7-3L14 8.5V2"/><path d="M7.5 14.5h9"/></svg>
tips.text: Understand the process of investigation. In tests you are often asked to describe a fair test. Remember: change only ONE variable, keep everything else the same, and observe what happens.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Use diagrams — they earn marks. Labelled diagrams of plants, animals, circuits or the solar system are worth marks. Practise drawing and labelling them from memory.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 2 4 14h6l-1 8 9-12h-6l1-8z"/></svg>
tips.text: Learn the key vocabulary. Natural Sciences uses specific technical words. Words like 'photosynthesis', 'conductor', 'transparent' and 'metamorphic' have precise meanings — learn and use them correctly.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M3 12h18M12 3c2.5 2.5 3.8 5.6 3.8 9s-1.3 6.5-3.8 9c-2.5-2.5-3.8-5.6-3.8-9S9.5 5.5 12 3z"/></svg>
tips.text: Connect concepts to real life. The best way to remember science content is to connect it to something you have seen. When you study erosion, think of a hillside after heavy rain. This makes answers easier to recall in exams.

subjects.hubDescription: Life and living, matter and materials, energy and change, and planet Earth for Grade 4.

subjects.title: Grade 4 Social Sciences | CAPS Study Materials | Curio Learning
subjects.description: Grade 4 Social Sciences study materials aligned to CAPS. History and geography integrated — early SA history, maps, settlements and environments.
subjects.expectIntro: Social Sciences in Grade 4 integrates History and Geography into one subject, helping learners understand the world they live in — its past and its physical features. The History component explores early settlements in South Africa, the origins of people in the region, and key historical events. The Geography component focuses on maps and map skills, the physical features of South Africa, and the relationship between people and their environments. Learners develop critical thinking by analysing sources, interpreting maps and drawing connections between historical events and their present-day consequences.

expectItems.label: Key skills
expectItems.value: Source analysis, map reading, comparing environments

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: History: early human settlements
topics: Early humans in Southern Africa — hunter-gatherers (San people)
Evidence of early human settlement: rock art, tools, middens
Herder-farmers: Khoikhoi people and their way of life
Early farming communities: Bantu-speaking peoples
Migration of early peoples across Southern Africa
The concept of a timeline — BCE and CE
Primary and secondary sources — what is historical evidence?
Oral history: how communities preserve their past

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Geography: maps and mapwork
topics: What is a map? Purpose and types of maps
Map elements: title, key/legend, compass rose, scale
Cardinal and intermediate directions: N, S, E, W, NE, NW, SE, SW
Grid references — locating places on a map
Physical maps of South Africa: provinces, major cities, rivers, mountains
Political maps: neighbouring countries of South Africa
Sketch maps — drawing simple maps of familiar areas
Aerial photographs vs maps — similarities and differences

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: History: heritage and early trade
topics: African kingdoms — Great Zimbabwe as a trade centre
Trade routes in early Southern Africa
Arab traders and their influence on the East Coast of Africa
The Mapungubwe kingdom — significance and evidence
South African heritage sites and their importance
Cultural heritage: traditions, language, food, music
SA Constitution and the importance of cultural diversity
Monuments and memorials — what do they tell us?

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Geography: environments and human activity
topics: Physical environments of South Africa: savanna, fynbos, Karoo, desert, grassland
Climate and vegetation — relationship between the two
How people settle in different environments — urban vs rural
Natural resources: water, minerals, soil, forests
Human impact on the environment: deforestation, pollution, overgrazing
Sustainable use of natural resources
Environmental challenges in South Africa
Simple graphs and tables showing population and land use data

skillChips: Read and interpret maps using cardinal directions
Use grid references to locate places
Identify map elements: key, scale, compass rose
Describe early human settlements in SA
Explain what historical evidence is
Name SA provinces, major cities and rivers
Describe early African kingdoms
Identify South African biomes and vegetation
Explain the relationship between climate and vegetation
Analyse simple historical sources
Describe human impact on the environment
Explain the importance of heritage
Compare urban and rural settlements
Draw a simple sketch map

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M3 12h18M12 3c2.5 2.5 3.8 5.6 3.8 9s-1.3 6.5-3.8 9c-2.5-2.5-3.8-5.6-3.8-9S9.5 5.5 12 3z"/></svg>
tips.text: Learn the map elements by heart. Every map test will ask you about the key, compass rose, scale and title. These are quick easy marks — make sure you always know all four.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: For history questions — use dates and names. Good history answers include specific people, places and dates. Instead of 'a long time ago' write 'in the 13th century'. Specific details earn more marks.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Draw maps from memory to practise. A great way to study geography is to draw the map of South Africa from memory — place the provinces, capital cities and major rivers. Do this once a week and you will remember it.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M3 12h18M12 3c2.5 2.5 3.8 5.6 3.8 9s-1.3 6.5-3.8 9c-2.5-2.5-3.8-5.6-3.8-9S9.5 5.5 12 3z"/></svg>
tips.text: Link history and geography together. The best Social Sciences students understand how geography shaped history — why people settled near rivers, how trade routes followed coastlines, and why some areas are more populated than others.

subjects.expectIntro: Grade 5 Afrikaans First Additional Language builds on the basic vocabulary and structures introduced in Grade 4. The CAPS curriculum develops practical Afrikaans communication — reading slightly longer texts with understanding, writing short paragraphs, and using a wider range of grammatical structures. Learners extend their core Afrikaans vocabulary, develop reading strategies and begin to write more independently. By the end of Grade 5, learners should be able to write a short structured paragraph, answer inferential comprehension questions, and use past and future tense with confidence.

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Narrative texts & extended vocabulary
topics: Read short Afrikaans narrative texts and answer literal and simple inferential questions
Revision of nouns, verbs and adjectives from Grade 4
Introduction of adverbs of manner and time
Present and past tense of common Afrikaans verbs — revision and extension
Write a short structured paragraph about a personal experience
Oral: short prepared talk using Afrikaans phrases

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Descriptive texts & grammar extension
topics: Read descriptive Afrikaans texts — identify key details and main idea
Degrees of comparison with adjectives: positief, komparatief, superlatief
Plural forms of nouns — including irregular plurals
Punctuation: inverted commas for direct speech
Write a short descriptive paragraph about a person or place
Oral: describe a picture using comparative adjectives

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Informational texts & tenses
topics: Read simple informational Afrikaans texts — notices, reports
Future tense — sal + infinitive
Simple conditional sentences — as ... dan ...
Synonyms and antonyms in Afrikaans — vocabulary development
Write a short report or recount in Afrikaans
Oral: retell a past event using correct Afrikaans tense

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Revision & poetry
topics: Simple persuasive and poetic Afrikaans texts — identify main idea and purpose
Rhyme and rhythm in simple Afrikaans poems
Revision of nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs and tenses
Prefixes and suffixes — how they change meaning
Write a simple Afrikaans poem or descriptive paragraph
Oral: recite a memorised Afrikaans poem

skillChips: Read short Afrikaans texts with understanding
Use degrees of comparison
Form plural nouns including irregular forms
Use present, past and future tense
Write a short structured Afrikaans paragraph
Identify rhyme and rhythm in Afrikaans poems
Use basic Afrikaans conjunctions
Answer inferential comprehension questions in Afrikaans

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Build vocabulary daily. Learn 5 new Afrikaans words every day. Write them with their English meaning and use each one in a sentence.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Read the question before the passage. In comprehension tests, knowing what you are looking for makes it much easier to find the evidence quickly.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: For comprehension — find the answer in the text. Most literal answers are directly in the text. Scan for keywords from the question.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Practise Afrikaans out loud. The best way to learn Afrikaans is to speak it, even if it is not perfect. Read sentences aloud to improve pronunciation and fluency.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Do not be afraid to make mistakes. Every mistake is a chance to learn. Afrikaans grammar follows clear patterns — once you understand the rules, they apply consistently.
