subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Afrikaans Home Language study materials for Grade 5. Comprehension, grammar, writing and poetry — free papers and memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 5 Afrikaans Home Language extends the foundations of Grade 4 to longer and more complex Afrikaans texts. The CAPS curriculum focuses on four integrated skills: luister en praat (listening and speaking), lees en kyk (reading and viewing), skryf en aanbied (writing and presenting), and taalstrukture en -konvensies (language structures and conventions). Learners work with multi-paragraph texts, encounter more sophisticated grammar including adverbs and degrees of comparison, and are expected to write structured paragraphs across different text types.

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Narratiewe tekste, voornaamwoorde & sinstrukture
topics: Lees en begrip van narratiewe tekste — letterlike en inferensiële vrae
Hersiening van naamwoorde, werkwoorde en byvoeglike naamwoorde
Voornaamwoorde: persoonlik, besitlik, betreklik (wat, wie, wat)
Saamgestelde en komplekse sinne
Paragraafskryfwerk: onderwerpsin en ondersteunende besonderhede
Leestekens: direkte rede — aanhalingstekens
Mondeling: bespreek 'n verhaal, vertel in volgorde

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Beskrywende tekste, bywoorde & paragraafskryfwerk
topics: Lees beskrywende en visuele tekste — advertensies, plakkate
Bywoorde van wyse, tyd en plek
Trappe van vergelyking: byvoeglike naamwoorde en bywoorde
Voor- en agtervoegsels — woordeskatuitbreiding
Paragraafskryfwerk: beskrywende skryfwerk met beplanning
Sinonieme, antonieme en homonieme
Mondeling: beskryf 'n toneel of ondervinding in besonderhede

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Informatiewe tekste, tye & rede
topics: Lees informatiewe tekste — verslae, artikels, diagramme
Hersiening en uitbreiding van verlede, teenwoordige, toekomende tyd
Lydende en bedryfssin — inleiding
Direkte rede teenoor indirekte rede — omskakeling tussen vorme
Onderwerp-werkwoordooreenstemming — meer komplekse sinne
Opsomming: identifiseer hoofpunte uit 'n gedeelte
Skryf 'n verslag of informatiewe paragraaf

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Oorredende tekste, poësie & hersiening
topics: Oorredende tekste — tegnieke, toon, doel
Poësie: strofes, rym, ritme, vergelyking, metafoor, personifikasie
Beeldspraak — identifiseer en verduidelik effek
Hersiening van alle taalstrukture
Meervuldige oorredende paragrawe
Begripshersiening: letterkunde en nie-fiksie
Mondeling: kort toespraak of dramatiese voorlees

skillChips: Lees en verstaan meervoudige paragraaftekste
Identifiseer en gebruik betreklike voornaamwoorde
Skryf saamgestelde en komplekse sinne
Produseer gestruktureerde beskrywende en narratiewe paragrawe
Gebruik bywoorde korrek
Omskakeling tussen direkte en indirekte rede
Identifiseer lydende en bedryfssin
Vat 'n gedeelte saam in eie woorde
Herken en verduidelik beeldspraak
Gebruik trappe van vergelyking
Spel hoëfrekwensie-woorde korrek
Pas korrekte leestekens toe

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Lees die vrae voor die gedeelte. In begripstoetse, as jy weet waarna jy soek, help dit jou om bewys vinniger te vind. Onderstreep sleutelwoorde in elke vraag eers, lees dan die teks met die vrae in gedagte.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Gebruik die merktoedeling as riglyn. 'n (2)-merkvraag benodig twee afsonderlike punte. 'n (4)-merkvraag benodig vier. Skryf nooit 'n enkele sin vir 'n meermerkvraag nie — jy sal punte verloor.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Haal aan uit die teks wanneer bewys gevra word. Skryf: 'Die teks sê ...' of 'Volgens die gedeelte ...' om presies te wys waar jou bewys vandaan kom.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Leer jou grammatika deur jou eie voorbeelde te maak. Skryf jou eie sinne wat die reël demonstreer. Dit dwing jou om te verstaan, nie net te memoriseer nie.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M12 7v5l3.5 2"/></svg>
tips.text: Kontroleer jou tye en stem nadat jy geskryf het. Twee van die mees algemene foute in Grade 5 en 6 is om tye te meng en die stem (bedryf/lydend) in die middel van 'n paragraaf te wissel.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Bou woordeskat deur wyd te lees. Elke tekssoort wat jy teëkom — romans, koerante, webtuistes — bou jou woordeskat. Sterk woordeskat is die grootste voordeel in Afrikaans-eksamens.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>

subjects.description: CAPS-aligned English Home Language study materials for Grade 5. Comprehension, grammar, writing and poetry — free papers and memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 5 English Home Language builds directly on the foundations of Grade 4, extending reading comprehension to longer and more complex texts, widening the range of language structures studied, and developing writing across a broader variety of text types. The CAPS curriculum focuses on four integrated skills: listening and speaking, reading and viewing, writing and presenting, and language structures and conventions. Learners encounter more nuanced comprehension questions requiring inference and evaluation, and are expected to produce structured multi-paragraph writing. Grammar becomes more sophisticated, with expanded work on parts of speech, sentence types and punctuation.

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Narrative texts, pronouns & sentence types
topics: Reading and comprehension of narrative texts — literal and inferential questions
Revision of nouns, verbs and adjectives from Grade 4
Pronouns: personal, possessive, relative (who, which, that)
Compound and complex sentences
Paragraph writing: topic sentence and supporting details
Punctuation: direct speech — inverted commas
Oral: discuss a story, retell in sequence

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Descriptive texts, adverbs & paragraph writing
topics: Read descriptive and visual texts — advertisements, posters
Adverbs of manner, time and place
Degrees of comparison: adjectives and adverbs
Prefixes and suffixes — extending vocabulary
Paragraph writing: descriptive writing with planning
Synonyms, antonyms and homophones
Oral: describe a scene or experience in detail

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Informational texts, tenses & speech
topics: Read informational texts — reports, articles, diagrams
Revision and extension of past, present, future tense
Passive and active voice — introduction
Direct vs indirect speech — convert between forms
Subject-verb agreement — more complex sentences
Summarising: identify main points from a passage
Writing a report or informational paragraph

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Persuasive texts, poetry & revision
topics: Persuasive texts — techniques, tone, purpose
Poetry: stanzas, rhyme, rhythm, simile, metaphor, personification
Figurative language — identify and explain effect
Revision of all grammar structures covered
Multi-paragraph persuasive writing
Comprehension revision: literature and non-fiction
Oral: short speech or dramatic reading

skillChips: Read and understand multi-paragraph texts
Identify and use relative pronouns
Write compound and complex sentences
Produce structured descriptive and narrative paragraphs
Use adverbs correctly
Convert between direct and indirect speech
Identify passive and active voice
Summarise a passage in own words
Recognise and explain figurative language
Use degrees of comparison
Spell high-frequency words correctly
Apply correct punctuation including inverted commas

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Read the questions before reading the passage. In comprehension tests, knowing what you are looking for helps you find evidence faster. Underline key words in each question first, then read the text with those questions in mind.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Use the mark allocation as a guide. A (2)-mark question needs two distinct points. A (4)-mark question needs four. Never write a single sentence for a multi-mark question — you will lose marks.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Quote from the text when asked for evidence. Write: 'The text says '…'' or 'According to the passage…' to show exactly where your evidence comes from. Examiners reward this.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Learn your grammar by making your own examples. Don't just copy definitions — write your own sentences that demonstrate the rule. This forces you to understand, not just memorise.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M12 7v5l3.5 2"/></svg>
tips.text: Check your tenses and voice after writing. Two of the most common errors in Grades 5 and 6 are mixing tenses and accidentally switching between active and passive voice mid-paragraph. Read every verb and ask: is this consistent?

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Build vocabulary by reading widely. Every text type you encounter — novels, newspapers, websites, cereal boxes — builds your vocabulary. Strong vocabulary is the single biggest advantage in English exams.

termCards.heading: Informational texts & tenses
topics: Read simple isiZulu informational texts — notices, simple instructions
Past tense forms of regular isiZulu verbs — extension
Introduction to future tense in isiZulu
Synonyms in isiZulu — vocabulary development
Write a short isiZulu report or recount
Oral: retell a past event in isiZulu using correct tense

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Revision & poetry
topics: Simple isiZulu poetry — identify stanzas, rhyme, mood
Revision of nouns, verbs, adjectives and tenses in isiZulu
Prefixes in isiZulu — how they change meaning
Write a simple isiZulu poem or descriptive paragraph
Oral: recite a memorised isiZulu poem (inkondlo)

skillChips: Read short isiZulu texts with understanding
Form plural nouns using noun class patterns
Use present and past tense in isiZulu
Write a short structured isiZulu paragraph
Identify rhyme and rhythm in isiZulu poems
Answer inferential comprehension questions
Use basic isiZulu conjunctions
Build vocabulary through context clues

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Build isiZulu vocabulary every day. Learn 5 new isiZulu words every day. Write them with meanings and use each in a sentence. Within a month you will have 150 new words.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Read the question before the passage. In comprehension tests, knowing what you are looking for helps you find evidence faster.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: For comprehension — find the answer in the text. Most literal answers are directly in the given text. Scan for keywords from the question.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Learn isiZulu noun classes gradually. IsiZulu grammar is based on noun classes. Learn one class at a time and practise its concords (agreement) in sentences.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Do not be afraid to make mistakes. IsiZulu follows consistent patterns once you know the noun classes. Every mistake helps you understand the pattern better.

subjects.hubDescription: IsiZulu First Additional Language for Grade 5 — ukufunda, ukubhala nezakhiwo zolimi.

subjects.title: Grade 5 Life Skills | CAPS Study Materials | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Life Skills study materials for Grade 5. Beginning Knowledge, Creative Arts and Physical Education — free study guides and support.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 5 Life Skills continues to develop the whole learner across three components: Beginning Knowledge and Personal and Social Wellbeing, Creative Arts, and Physical Education. The Beginning Knowledge component extends work on personal identity, health, relationships and citizenship. Creative Arts develops visual art, music, drama and movement skills with growing confidence and creativity. Physical Education builds fitness, coordination and team sport skills. Grade 5 places increasing emphasis on leadership, responsibility and making healthy choices.

expectItems.label: Three components
expectItems.value: Beginning Knowledge · Creative Arts · Physical Education

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Personal identity, health & creative arts
topics: Personal identity: values, beliefs, strengths and areas for growth
Goal setting: short- and medium-term personal goals
Healthy lifestyle: balanced diet, exercise, sleep and hygiene — in more depth
The media and healthy body image — critical thinking
Creative Arts — Visual Art: colour theory, texture, pattern
Creative Arts — Music: reading basic notation, rhythm patterns
Physical Education: locomotor and non-locomotor movement combinations
Athletics: sprinting, jumping, throwing technique

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Relationships, citizenship & creative arts
topics: Relationships: peer pressure — recognising, resisting, assertiveness skills
Bullying: types, effects, how to respond and report
Rights and responsibilities: the SA Constitution and children's rights
Community and citizenship: what it means to contribute
Creative Arts — Drama: character development, freeze frames, improvisation
Creative Arts — Dance: African dance forms, body percussion
Physical Education: ball sports skills — striking, catching, fielding
Team games: communication, cooperation, rules and fair play

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Environment, culture & creative expression
topics: Environment: human rights and environmental responsibility
Cultural diversity: celebrating South Africa's cultural wealth
Heritage: how communities preserve their history and identity
Critical thinking: analysing messages in advertising and media
Creative Arts — Visual Art: printmaking, mixed media, sculpture
Creative Arts — Music: pentatonic scale, songs from different SA traditions
Physical Education: invasion games — soccer, netball, basketball principles
Fitness: aerobic endurance and flexibility activities

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Revision, performance & personal goals
topics: Revision: health, relationships, rights, community and environment
Creative Arts — performance showcase: share creative work
Creative Arts — Music: create and perform a short composition
Physical Education: gymnastics — rolling, balancing, jumping sequences
Cooperative games and outdoor challenges
Goal review: assess progress on personal goals set in Term 1
Preparing for Grade 6: reflecting on growth and next steps
Celebration of individual and group achievements

skillChips: Set and review personal short-term goals
Identify and resist peer pressure assertively
Describe children's rights under the SA Constitution
Create artwork using colour, texture and pattern
Demonstrate rhythm patterns in music
Perform locomotor and non-locomotor movement sequences
Apply team sport skills in games
Explain the importance of cultural diversity
Analyse media messages critically

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8.5"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="4.8"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="1.1" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/></svg>
tips.text: For written tests — learn key vocabulary. Life Skills tests ask you to define terms like 'puberty', 'assertive', 'biodiversity', 'Bill of Rights'. Learn the exact definitions and use them in sentences.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 3v5M12 16v5M3 12h5M16 12h5M6 6l3 3M15 15l3 3M18 6l-3 3M9 15l-3 3"/></svg>
tips.text: Creative Arts assessments reward process, not just product. Teachers assess your engagement, creative thinking and understanding of concepts, not just the final artwork or performance. Participate fully and explain your choices.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8.5"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="4.8"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="1.1" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/></svg>
tips.text: PE is assessed practically — attend every lesson. PE marks come from participation and correct technique. Attend every lesson, listen carefully to instructions and try your best at every skill.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Connect Life Skills to your real life. The content is most memorable when connected to your own experience. When studying puberty, think about changes you are noticing. When studying rights, think about your school rules.

subjects.hubDescription: Beginning Knowledge, Creative Arts and Physical Education combined for Grade 5.

subjects.title: Grade 5 Mathematics | CAPS Study Materials | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Mathematics study materials for Grade 5. Numbers, operations, fractions, geometry, measurement and data — free papers and memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 5 Mathematics extends the number range to 999 999 and deepens understanding of all four operations. The CAPS curriculum covers five content areas: Numbers, Operations and Relationships, Patterns, Functions and Algebra, Space and Shape (Geometry), Measurement, and Data Handling. Fractions are extended to include equivalent fractions and fraction operations. Decimal fractions are introduced. Geometry work deepens understanding of 2D shapes and 3D objects with an emphasis on properties. Mental mathematics and estimation remain central throughout.

expectItems.label: Number range
expectItems.value: Whole numbers to 999 999 · Common and decimal fractions

expectItems.label: Key concepts
expectItems.value: Equivalent fractions · decimal fractions · properties of shapes

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Whole numbers, multiplication & patterns
topics: Count, order, compare and represent whole numbers to 999 999
Place value: units through hundred thousands
Multiplication: 3-digit × 2-digit using various strategies
Division: 3-digit ÷ 2-digit with and without remainders
Multiples and factors — HCF and LCM (introduction)
Number patterns — extend, describe and create
2D shapes: classify and describe properties
Symmetry: more than one line of symmetry

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Common fractions & decimal fractions
topics: Common fractions: extend to twelfths, sixteenths
Equivalent fractions — simplify and compare
Add and subtract fractions with the same denominator
Decimal fractions: tenths and hundredths on a number line
Convert between common and decimal fractions
Decimal addition and subtraction
3D objects: classify, describe nets
Length: convert between mm, cm, m, km

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Properties of operations, measurement & data
topics: Properties of whole number operations: commutative, associative, distributive
Order of operations — introduction (no brackets yet)
Numeric patterns: constant difference and ratio
Time: calculate time intervals using timetables
Mass: convert between g, kg, ton
Capacity: convert between ml, l
Data: collect, organise, represent — bar graphs, pictographs, pie charts
Range, mode and median of a data set

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Revision, probability & geometry
topics: Revision of all four operations with whole numbers to 999 999
Word problems: multi-step with all operations
Perimeter and area of regular and irregular shapes
Transformations: reflection, translation, rotation
Temperature: converting between Celsius contexts
Probability: likelihood scale — certain, likely, unlikely, impossible
Integers: introduction — meaning of negative numbers
Solving number sentences with unknowns: □ × 6 = 48

skillChips: Count, order and compare numbers to 999 999
Multiply 3-digit by 2-digit numbers
Divide 3-digit by 2-digit with remainders
Find equivalent fractions and simplify
Add and subtract common fractions same denominator
Work with decimal fractions to hundredths
Convert between mm, cm, m, km
Calculate range, mode and median
Identify properties of 2D shapes and 3D objects
Perform transformations: reflection, translation
Solve number sentences with unknowns
Describe and extend number patterns

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="4.5" y="2.5" width="15" height="19" rx="2"/><path d="M8 6.5h8"/><path d="M8 11h.01M12 11h.01M16 11h.01M8 15h.01M12 15h.01M16 15h.01M8 19h.01M12 19h.01M16 19h.01"/></svg>
tips.text: Learn your multiplication tables thoroughly. Almost everything in Grade 5 and 6 Maths — fractions, ratios, percentages, division — requires fast multiplication. Drill your tables until they are automatic.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Show all your working. Marks are given for method, not just the final answer. Even if your answer is wrong, correct working earns marks.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Underline what the question is asking. Word problems contain a lot of information. Underline the actual question (usually the last sentence) and the key numbers before calculating.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="4.5" y="2.5" width="15" height="19" rx="2"/><path d="M8 6.5h8"/><path d="M8 11h.01M12 11h.01M16 11h.01M8 15h.01M12 15h.01M16 15h.01M8 19h.01M12 19h.01M16 19h.01"/></svg>
tips.text: Check by working backwards. After solving, verify by reversing the operation. If 48 ÷ 6 = 8, check: 8 × 6 = 48. This catches most errors in seconds.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="m3 16 6-6 4 4 8-9"/><path d="M15 5h6v6"/></svg>
tips.text: Draw diagrams for geometry and data questions. If a question describes a shape or data set, sketch it before calculating. A visual representation helps you see which operation is needed.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Mental maths daily makes everything easier. Practise adding and subtracting multiples of 10, 100 and 1 000 in your head. Strong number sense means faster, more accurate working in tests.

subjects.hubDescription: Numbers, operations, fractions, geometry, measurement and data — the full Grade 5 CAPS maths guide.

subjects.title: Grade 5 Natural Sciences & Technology | CAPS Study Materials | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Natural Sciences and Technology study materials for Grade 5. Life, matter, energy and planet Earth — free papers and memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 5 Natural Sciences and Technology builds on Grade 4 content and extends learners' scientific understanding across the four knowledge strands: Life and Living, Matter and Materials, Energy and Change, and Planet Earth and Beyond. Learners conduct increasingly independent investigations, make predictions, record data in tables and draw basic graphs. The Technology component develops design thinking — learners identify a problem, plan a solution, build a prototype and evaluate it. Grade 5 introduces the human body, food webs and ecosystems, as well as electrical and mechanical systems.

expectItems.label: Main strands
expectItems.value: Life & Living · Matter & Materials · Energy & Change · Planet Earth

expectItems.label: Key skill
expectItems.value: Scientific investigation: predict, test, record, conclude

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Life and living — animals and ecosystems
topics: Classification of animals: vertebrates and invertebrates
Vertebrates: fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, mammals — characteristics
Food chains and food webs — producer, consumer, predator, prey
Ecosystems: biotic and abiotic components
Human impact on ecosystems: pollution, habitat destruction, conservation
Adaptation: how animals are suited to their environment
Technology: design a simple model to reduce environmental impact
Investigation: classify local animals using identification keys

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Matter and materials — mixtures and solutions
topics: Mixtures: homogeneous and heterogeneous mixtures
Solutions: solute, solvent, solution — examples in daily life
Separating mixtures: filtering, evaporation, sieving, decanting, magnetism
Dissolving: factors affecting rate of dissolving — temperature, stirring, particle size
Conservation of mass when mixing materials
Chemical change vs physical change — introduction
Technology: design a water filtration device
Investigation: test factors affecting how quickly sugar dissolves

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Energy and change — electrical systems
topics: Electric circuits: series and parallel circuits
Circuit diagrams: symbols for battery, wire, bulb, switch, resistor
Conductors and insulators — revision and extension
Effect of adding more batteries or bulbs to a circuit
Magnets and electromagnetism — introduction
Sound energy: vibration, pitch, volume, reflection
Technology: build and modify a simple circuit
Investigation: compare brightness of bulbs in series vs parallel

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Planet Earth — weather, water and beyond
topics: The water cycle: evaporation, condensation, precipitation, collection
Weather: cloud types, rainfall, temperature, wind — reading weather maps
Climate vs weather — difference and South African examples
Rocks and minerals: properties and uses in technology
Fossils: formation and what they tell us about the past
Our solar system: planets, moons, asteroids, comets
Technology: build a model of the water cycle
Investigation: collect and analyse local weather data

skillChips: Classify animals as vertebrates or invertebrates
Construct and interpret food chains and food webs
Describe components of an ecosystem
Separate mixtures using appropriate methods
Draw and interpret circuit diagrams
Build simple series and parallel circuits
Describe the water cycle
Read and record weather data
Plan and conduct a fair test
Record data in tables and basic graphs
Identify fossils and explain their significance
Describe the solar system

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M9 2h6M10 2v6.5L4.5 18a2 2 0 0 0 1.7 3h11.6a2 2 0 0 0 1.7-3L14 8.5V2"/><path d="M7.5 14.5h9"/></svg>
tips.text: Understand the fair test process. In tests you are often asked to describe or design a fair test. Remember: change only ONE variable, keep everything else the same, and observe what happens.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Use labelled diagrams — they earn marks. Labelled diagrams of plants, animals, circuits, the water cycle or the solar system are worth marks. Practise drawing and labelling them from memory.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 2 4 14h6l-1 8 9-12h-6l1-8z"/></svg>
tips.text: Learn the key vocabulary. Natural Sciences uses precise technical vocabulary. Words like 'photosynthesis', 'vertebrate', 'conductor' and 'decomposer' have specific meanings — use them correctly.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M3 12h18M12 3c2.5 2.5 3.8 5.6 3.8 9s-1.3 6.5-3.8 9c-2.5-2.5-3.8-5.6-3.8-9S9.5 5.5 12 3z"/></svg>
tips.text: Connect science to real life. The best way to remember content is to connect it to real examples. When you study the water cycle, think of rain. When you study food webs, think of your local environment.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M9 2h6M10 2v6.5L4.5 18a2 2 0 0 0 1.7 3h11.6a2 2 0 0 0 1.7-3L14 8.5V2"/><path d="M7.5 14.5h9"/></svg>
tips.text: Know the difference between physical and chemical change. Physical change is reversible (cutting, dissolving). Chemical change is irreversible (burning, rusting). This distinction appears in almost every Grade 5 and 6 NST test.

subjects.hubDescription: Life and living, matter and materials, energy and change, and planet Earth for Grade 5.

subjects.title: Grade 5 Social Sciences | CAPS Study Materials | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Social Sciences study materials for Grade 5. History and geography — maps, environments, SA history and early civilisations — free papers and memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 5 Social Sciences integrates History and Geography to deepen learners' understanding of South Africa and the wider world. The History component examines pre-colonial societies, the arrival of European settlers and the early history of the Cape Colony. The Geography component extends map skills, introduces different types of maps and covers South Africa's physical and human geography — including biomes, natural resources and settlement patterns. Learners continue to develop source-analysis and map-reading skills.

expectItems.label: Key skills
expectItems.value: Source analysis · map reading · environmental comparison

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: History: pre-colonial societies in SA
topics: Pre-colonial Southern Africa: San, Khoikhoi, Bantu-speaking societies
Different ways of living: hunter-gatherers, herders, farmers
Social structures: families, clans, chiefs
Oral traditions: how history was preserved without writing
Evidence of pre-colonial societies: rock art, archaeological sites, oral histories
The concept of primary and secondary sources — revision and extension
Comparing pre-colonial communities: similarities and differences
African trade networks before European contact

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Geography: South Africa's physical geography
topics: South Africa's landforms: escarpment, highveld, lowveld, coastal plains, mountains
Major rivers of South Africa: Orange, Vaal, Limpopo, Tugela
Biomes of South Africa: fynbos, Karoo, savanna, grassland, forest, desert
Climate regions: relationship between rainfall and biome
Natural resources: soil, water, minerals, forests, wildlife
Human settlement patterns: why people settle where they do
Maps: topographic maps — contour lines, spot heights
Aerial photographs — interpreting land use

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: History: European contact and the Cape
topics: European exploration: reasons for searching for sea routes to Asia
Bartolomeu Dias and Vasco da Gama — discovery of the Cape
The Portuguese at the Cape: refreshment station
Dutch East India Company (VOC) — establishing the Cape Colony
Jan van Riebeeck and the founding of the Cape settlement (1652)
The Khoikhoi and the VOC: initial contact, trade, conflict
Introduction of slavery at the Cape
The expansion of the Cape Colony and conflict with indigenous peoples

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Geography: human geography and environment
topics: Population: South Africa's population distribution — urban and rural
Push and pull factors: why people move (migration)
Urban growth: informal settlements, urban planning challenges
Environmental challenges: water scarcity, deforestation, soil erosion in SA
Conservation: national parks, nature reserves, community conservation
Sustainable development — what it means for South Africa
Climate change effects in southern Africa
Comparing urban and rural environments in South Africa

skillChips: Describe pre-colonial societies in Southern Africa
Analyse primary and secondary historical sources
Identify South Africa's major landforms and rivers
Name and describe South Africa's biomes
Read and interpret topographic maps with contour lines
Explain why European explorers came to the Cape
Describe the founding of the Cape Colony
Explain push and pull factors for migration
Identify environmental challenges facing South Africa
Compare urban and rural environments

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M3 12h18M12 3c2.5 2.5 3.8 5.6 3.8 9s-1.3 6.5-3.8 9c-2.5-2.5-3.8-5.6-3.8-9S9.5 5.5 12 3z"/></svg>
tips.text: Learn the map elements by heart. Every map test will ask about the key, compass rose, scale and title. These are easy marks — always know all four and apply them first.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Use specific names and dates in history answers. Good history answers include specific people, places and dates. Instead of 'a long time ago' write '1652'. Specific details earn more marks.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Draw maps to practise geography. Draw South Africa's biomes, major rivers and provinces from memory once a week. This is the most effective geography revision technique.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M3 12h18M12 3c2.5 2.5 3.8 5.6 3.8 9s-1.3 6.5-3.8 9c-2.5-2.5-3.8-5.6-3.8-9S9.5 5.5 12 3z"/></svg>
tips.text: Link history and geography together. The best Social Sciences students understand how geography shaped history — why settlements were built near rivers, why trade routes followed coastlines, why certain areas had conflict.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="10.5" cy="10.5" r="7"/><path d="M20.5 20.5 15.8 15.8"/></svg>
tips.text: When analysing sources, always ask: who wrote this, when and why? The source's origin, date and purpose determine whether it is reliable and what perspective it represents. Always reference the source in your answer.

subjects.expectIntro: Grade 6 Afrikaans Home Language is the final year of the Intermediate Phase and prepares learners for the Senior Phase. The CAPS curriculum consolidates and extends all four language skills to a high level, working with complex texts, sophisticated grammar including modals and conditional sentences, and extended writing tasks that require planning, drafting and editing. Learners develop a secure command of Afrikaans grammar and are expected to apply it accurately in their own independent writing.

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Narratiewe tekste, komplekse sinne & gevorderde voornaamwoorde
topics: Lees langer narratiewe en transaksionele tekste
Betreklike voornaamwoorde: wat, wie, wie se — in komplekse sinne
Komplekse sinne: hoofsin en bysin
Voegwoorde: onderskikkend (omdat, alhoewel, terwyl, tensy, as)
Paragraafskryfwerk: beplanning, konsep en hersiening
Apostroof: besit en sametrekking — hersiening en uitbreiding
Mondeling: groepbespreking, mondelinge aanbieding

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Beskrywende tekste, modale werkwoorde & formele skryfwerk
topics: Lees formele en informele tekste — briewe, e-posse, artikels
Modale werkwoorde: kan, kon, mag, moet, sal, sou, wil
Voorwaardelike sinne — eerste en tweede kondisionaal
Beeldspraak: vergelyking, metafoor, personifikasie, alliterasie, onomatopee
Formele briefskryfwerk: uitleg en register
Woordvorming: wortels, voor- en agtervoegsels
Mondeling: voorbereide toespraak, debatinleiding

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Informatiewe tekste, stem & opsomming
topics: Lees informatiewe, argumenterende en visuele tekste
Bedryfssin en lydende sin — uitgebreide oefening en omskrywing
Indirekte rede: direk na indirek en terug
Tydhersiening: voltooide tye (teenwoordig voltooid, verlede tyd voltooid)
Opsommingskryfwerk: identifiseer hoofpunte, parafraseer, skryf eie weergawe
Transaksionele skryfwerk: advertensie, kennisgewing, dagboek
Mondeling: luister en neem notas; formele reaksie

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Hersiening, poësie & uitgebreide skryfwerk
topics: Poësie-analise: beelding, stemming, toon, tema, struktuur
Paragraaf- en opstelskryfwerk: inleiding, liggaam, gevolgtrekking
Hersiening van alle taalstrukture: woordsoorte, tye, rede, stem
Begripsvaardighede: letterlike, inferensiële, evalueringsvraeë
Leestekenshersiening: alle tekens gedek in Grade 4–6
Mondeling: voorbereide voorlees, gedigopsê of kort drama
Eksamenbereiding: tydbestuur en antwoordstrategieë

skillChips: Lees en analiseer komplekse tekste van verskillende soorte
Gebruik modale werkwoorde en voorwaardelike sinne
Skryf formele briewe met korrekte uitleg
Omskakeling tussen bedryfssin en lydende sin
Skryf in voltooide tye
Identifiseer beeldspraak en verduidelik die effek
Beplan, skryf konsep en hersien uitgebreide skryfwerk
Skryf 'n gestruktureerde meervoudige paragraafopstel
Vat saam en parafraseer 'n teks
Analiseer poësie vir beelding, stemming en tema
Pas alle leestekens korrek toe
Gebruik onderskikkende voegwoorde in komplekse sinne

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Lees die vrae voor die gedeelte. In begripstoetse, as jy weet waarna jy soek, help dit jou om bewys vinniger te vind. Onderstreep sleutelwoorde in elke vraag eers, lees dan die teks met die vrae in gedagte.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Gebruik die merktoedeling as riglyn. 'n (2)-merkvraag benodig twee afsonderlike punte. 'n (4)-merkvraag benodig vier. Skryf nooit 'n enkele sin vir 'n meermerkvraag nie — jy sal punte verloor.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Haal aan uit die teks wanneer bewys gevra word. Skryf: 'Die teks sê ...' of 'Volgens die gedeelte ...' om presies te wys waar jou bewys vandaan kom.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Leer jou grammatika deur jou eie voorbeelde te maak. Skryf jou eie sinne wat die reël demonstreer. Dit dwing jou om te verstaan, nie net te memoriseer nie.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M12 7v5l3.5 2"/></svg>
tips.text: Kontroleer jou tye en stem nadat jy geskryf het. Twee van die mees algemene foute in Grade 5 en 6 is om tye te meng en die stem (bedryf/lydend) in die middel van 'n paragraaf te wissel.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Bou woordeskat deur wyd te lees. Elke tekssoort wat jy teëkom — romans, koerante, webtuistes — bou jou woordeskat. Sterk woordeskat is die grootste voordeel in Afrikaans-eksamens.

subjects.expectIntro: Grade 6 English Home Language is the final year of the Intermediate Phase and consolidates skills before the transition to the Senior Phase. The CAPS curriculum extends all four skills — listening and speaking, reading and viewing, writing and presenting, and language structures and conventions — to a level that prepares learners for the demands of Grade 7. Texts become longer and more complex, comprehension questions require higher-order thinking, and extended writing tasks require planning, drafting and editing. Learners are expected to have a secure understanding of grammar and to apply it accurately in their own writing.

expectItems.label: Key shift
expectItems.value: Extended writing · higher-order comprehension · Senior Phase readiness

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Narrative texts, complex sentences & advanced pronouns
topics: Reading longer narrative and transactional texts
Relative pronouns: who, whose, which, that — in complex sentences
Complex sentences: main clause and subordinate clause
Conjunctions: subordinating (because, although, while, unless, if)
Paragraph writing: planning, drafting and revising
Apostrophes: possession and contraction — revision and extension
Oral: group discussion, oral presentation

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Descriptive texts, modal verbs & formal writing
topics: Read formal and informal texts — letters, emails, articles
Modal verbs: can, could, may, might, must, should, would
Conditional sentences: first and second conditional
Figures of speech: simile, metaphor, personification, alliteration, onomatopoeia
Formal letter writing: layout and register
Word formation: roots, prefixes and suffixes
Oral: prepared speech, debate introduction

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Informational texts, voice & summary
topics: Read informational, argumentative and visual texts
Active and passive voice — extended practice and rewriting
Reported speech: direct to indirect and back
Tense revision: perfect tenses (present perfect, past perfect)
Summary writing: identify main points, paraphrase, write own version
Transactional writing: advertisement, notice, diary
Oral: listen and take notes; formal response

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Revision, poetry & extended writing
topics: Poetry analysis: imagery, mood, tone, theme, structure
Paragraph and essay writing: introduction, body, conclusion
Revision of all grammar: parts of speech, tenses, speech, voice
Comprehension skills: literal, inferential, evaluative questions
Punctuation revision: all marks covered across Grades 4–6
Oral: prepared reading, poem recitation or short drama
Examination preparation: time management and answer strategies

skillChips: Read and analyse complex texts of different types
Use modal verbs and conditional sentences
Write formal letters with correct layout
Convert between active and passive voice
Write in perfect tenses
Identify figures of speech and explain their effect
Plan, draft and revise extended writing
Write a structured multi-paragraph essay
Summarise and paraphrase a text
Analyse poetry for imagery, mood and theme
Apply all punctuation marks correctly
Use subordinating conjunctions in complex sentences

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Read the questions before reading the passage. In comprehension tests, knowing what you are looking for helps you find evidence faster. Underline key words in each question first, then read the text with those questions in mind.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Use the mark allocation as a guide. A (2)-mark question needs two distinct points. A (4)-mark question needs four. Never write a single sentence for a multi-mark question — you will lose marks.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Quote from the text when asked for evidence. Write: 'The text says '…'' or 'According to the passage…' to show exactly where your evidence comes from. Examiners reward this.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Learn your grammar by making your own examples. Don't just copy definitions — write your own sentences that demonstrate the rule. This forces you to understand, not just memorise.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M12 7v5l3.5 2"/></svg>
tips.text: Check your tenses and voice after writing. Two of the most common errors in Grades 5 and 6 are mixing tenses and accidentally switching between active and passive voice mid-paragraph. Read every verb and ask: is this consistent?

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Build vocabulary by reading widely. Every text type you encounter — novels, newspapers, websites, cereal boxes — builds your vocabulary. Strong vocabulary is the single biggest advantage in English exams.

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Informational texts & direct speech
topics: Read isiZulu informational texts — articles and simple reports
Direct speech in isiZulu — identification and use
Revision of future tense
Vocabulary extension — context clues and word families
Write a short isiZulu informational paragraph
Oral: summarise a short isiZulu text in own words

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Revision & poetry
topics: IsiZulu poetry — identify izaga (proverbs), izinkondlo, rhythm and tone
Figurative language in isiZulu — ukuphinda, izithombe
Revision of all grammar: nouns, verbs, tenses, concords
Write a short persuasive paragraph or simple isiZulu poem
Oral: recite a memorised isiZulu poem or proverb

skillChips: Read longer isiZulu texts with understanding
Use noun class agreement (concords)
Write compound sentences in isiZulu
Use simple modal expressions
Write a short isiZulu letter
Identify isiZulu figurative language and proverbs
Write a structured multi-sentence isiZulu paragraph
Use synonyms and antonyms in isiZulu

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Build isiZulu vocabulary every day. Learn 5 new isiZulu words every day. Write them with meanings and use each in a sentence. Within a month you will have 150 new words.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Read the question before the passage. In comprehension tests, knowing what you are looking for helps you find evidence faster.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: For comprehension — find the answer in the text. Most literal answers are directly in the given text. Scan for keywords from the question.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Learn isiZulu noun classes gradually. IsiZulu grammar is based on noun classes. Learn one class at a time and practise its concords (agreement) in sentences.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Do not be afraid to make mistakes. IsiZulu follows consistent patterns once you know the noun classes. Every mistake helps you understand the pattern better.

subjects.hubDescription: IsiZulu First Additional Language for Grade 6 — extended vocabulary and sentence structures.

subjects.title: Grade 6 Life Skills | CAPS Study Materials | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Life Skills study materials for Grade 6. Beginning Knowledge, Creative Arts and Physical Education — free study guides and support.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 6 Life Skills is the final year of the Intermediate Phase and consolidates whole-learner development at a level that prepares learners for the Senior Phase. The Beginning Knowledge and Personal and Social Wellbeing component addresses adolescent development, relationships, rights and responsibilities and community engagement. Creative Arts develops independent creative expression across visual art, music, drama and dance. Physical Education focuses on sport-specific skills, team play and personal fitness goals.

expectItems.label: Three components
expectItems.value: Beginning Knowledge · Creative Arts · Physical Education

expectItems.label: Key focus
expectItems.value: Adolescent development · independent creativity · sport-specific skills

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Adolescent development & wellbeing
topics: Physical changes during puberty: what to expect and how to manage
Emotional changes in adolescence: mood fluctuations, identity formation
Healthy relationships: trust, respect, communication, boundaries
Online safety: cyberbullying, digital footprint, screen time management
Creative Arts — Visual Art: perspective drawing, still life, observational drawing
Creative Arts — Music: part-singing, harmony, SA contemporary music
Physical Education: athletics — technique in running, jumping and throwing events
Fitness assessment: measure and set personal fitness goals

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Rights, responsibilities & creative arts
topics: The South African Constitution: Bill of Rights in everyday context
Gender equality: challenging stereotypes and discrimination
Child protection: abuse prevention, safe adults, reporting
Community service: what it is and how to engage
Creative Arts — Drama: scripted performance, directing techniques
Creative Arts — Dance: dance styles — hip hop, contemporary, kwaito
Physical Education: net and wall games — volleyball, tennis principles
Team strategy: planning moves, positions and communication

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Health, substance awareness & arts
topics: Substance abuse: alcohol, tobacco, cannabis — short and long-term effects
Peer pressure and substance use — refusal skills
First aid: basic first aid procedures — bleeding, choking, burns
Environmental health: water quality, sanitation, safe food handling
Creative Arts — Visual Art: digital art, photography composition
Creative Arts — Music: improvisation and composition using instruments
Physical Education: striking and fielding games — cricket, rounders
Physical fitness: strength, endurance and flexibility circuit training

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Transition, performance & celebration
topics: Preparing for the Senior Phase: study skills, time management, self-discipline
Managing change: new schools, friendships, academic expectations
Creative Arts — performance showcase: all art forms represented
Physical Education: indigenous games and recreational activities
Sport and recreation for life: the value of staying active
Reflection: personal growth across Grade 6
Goal setting for Grade 7
Farewell and celebration of Intermediate Phase completion

skillChips: Describe physical and emotional changes in puberty
Explain healthy relationship boundaries
Apply online safety knowledge
Describe the Bill of Rights in everyday context
Create observational drawings with perspective
Perform in a scripted drama
Demonstrate sport-specific skills in games
Apply basic first aid for common injuries
Set personal fitness goals and track progress
Explain the effects of substance abuse

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8.5"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="4.8"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="1.1" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/></svg>
tips.text: For written tests — learn key vocabulary. Life Skills tests ask you to define terms like 'puberty', 'assertive', 'biodiversity', 'Bill of Rights'. Learn the exact definitions and use them in sentences.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 3v5M12 16v5M3 12h5M16 12h5M6 6l3 3M15 15l3 3M18 6l-3 3M9 15l-3 3"/></svg>
tips.text: Creative Arts assessments reward process, not just product. Teachers assess your engagement, creative thinking and understanding of concepts, not just the final artwork or performance. Participate fully and explain your choices.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8.5"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="4.8"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="1.1" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/></svg>
tips.text: PE is assessed practically — attend every lesson. PE marks come from participation and correct technique. Attend every lesson, listen carefully to instructions and try your best at every skill.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Connect Life Skills to your real life. The content is most memorable when connected to your own experience. When studying puberty, think about changes you are noticing. When studying rights, think about your school rules.

subjects.hubDescription: Adolescent development, rights, creative arts and fitness for Grade 6.

subjects.title: Grade 6 Mathematics | CAPS Study Materials | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Mathematics study materials for Grade 6. Numbers, operations, fractions, geometry, measurement and data — free papers and memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 6 Mathematics is the final year of the Intermediate Phase and extends the number range to whole numbers up to 999 999 and decimals to at least two decimal places. The CAPS curriculum consolidates all five content areas and deepens work on fractions, ratios, percentages and the properties of 2D and 3D shapes. Algebraic thinking is extended through number patterns and equations with unknowns. Data handling is developed with more complex graphs and the introduction of probability. Grade 6 Maths prepares learners for the formal algebra and geometry of Grade 7.

expectItems.label: Number range
expectItems.value: Whole numbers to 999 999 · Decimals to 2dp · Percentages

expectItems.label: Key concepts
expectItems.value: Ratio · percentage · integers · formal properties of shapes

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Whole numbers, ratio & patterns
topics: Count, order, compare and represent whole numbers to 999 999
Prime numbers, composite numbers, prime factorisation
Ratio and rate — simplify and use in real contexts
Input and output values — flow diagrams and tables
Numeric patterns: constant ratio patterns
Geometric patterns: identify the rule and extend
2D shapes: classify quadrilaterals by properties
Angle: types and measuring with a protractor

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Fractions, percentages & decimals
topics: Common fractions: add and subtract with different denominators
Multiply a fraction by a whole number
Percentages: find the percentage of a quantity
Convert between fractions, decimals and percentages
Decimal fractions to 3 decimal places
Decimal multiplication: decimal × whole number
3D objects: describe, classify and draw nets
Surface area of rectangular prisms (informal)

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Algebra, measurement & data
topics: Algebraic expressions: substitution into simple expressions
Equations: find the value of the unknown
Properties of operations — consolidation
Perimeter and area: triangles and composite figures
Volume of rectangular prisms
Data: mean, median, mode and range
Represent data: double bar graphs and pie charts
Analyse and interpret graphs — ask critical questions

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Integers, probability & revision
topics: Integers: order, compare, add and subtract
Number lines extending to negative numbers
Probability: experimental vs theoretical probability
Tree diagrams for simple probability events
Transformations: tessellations and enlargements
Revision of all fractions, percentages and decimals
Multi-step word problems across all content areas
Examination preparation: showing working and checking answers

skillChips: Work with whole numbers to 999 999
Use prime factorisation
Apply ratio and rate in real contexts
Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators
Multiply a fraction by a whole number
Convert between fractions, decimals and percentages
Measure and calculate angles
Calculate perimeter and area of triangles
Calculate volume of rectangular prisms
Find mean, median, mode and range
Solve algebraic equations
Add and subtract integers

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="4.5" y="2.5" width="15" height="19" rx="2"/><path d="M8 6.5h8"/><path d="M8 11h.01M12 11h.01M16 11h.01M8 15h.01M12 15h.01M16 15h.01M8 19h.01M12 19h.01M16 19h.01"/></svg>
tips.text: Learn your multiplication tables thoroughly. Almost everything in Grade 5 and 6 Maths — fractions, ratios, percentages, division — requires fast multiplication. Drill your tables until they are automatic.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Show all your working. Marks are given for method, not just the final answer. Even if your answer is wrong, correct working earns marks.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Underline what the question is asking. Word problems contain a lot of information. Underline the actual question (usually the last sentence) and the key numbers before calculating.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="4.5" y="2.5" width="15" height="19" rx="2"/><path d="M8 6.5h8"/><path d="M8 11h.01M12 11h.01M16 11h.01M8 15h.01M12 15h.01M16 15h.01M8 19h.01M12 19h.01M16 19h.01"/></svg>
tips.text: Check by working backwards. After solving, verify by reversing the operation. If 48 ÷ 6 = 8, check: 8 × 6 = 48. This catches most errors in seconds.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="m3 16 6-6 4 4 8-9"/><path d="M15 5h6v6"/></svg>
tips.text: Draw diagrams for geometry and data questions. If a question describes a shape or data set, sketch it before calculating. A visual representation helps you see which operation is needed.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Mental maths daily makes everything easier. Practise adding and subtracting multiples of 10, 100 and 1 000 in your head. Strong number sense means faster, more accurate working in tests.

subjects.hubDescription: Ratio, percentage, fractions, integers, geometry and data — the full Grade 6 CAPS maths guide.

subjects.title: Grade 6 Natural Sciences & Technology | CAPS Study Materials | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Natural Sciences and Technology study materials for Grade 6. Life, matter, energy and planet Earth — free papers and memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 6 Natural Sciences and Technology is the final year of the Intermediate Phase and consolidates scientific literacy at a level that prepares learners for Grade 7. The CAPS curriculum extends all four knowledge strands and introduces more complex scientific concepts including reproduction, chemical changes, the water cycle and renewable energy systems. Learners are expected to plan and conduct fair investigations independently, interpret results and draw evidence-based conclusions. The Technology component requires learners to apply the complete design process with greater independence.

expectItems.label: Main strands
expectItems.value: Life & Living · Matter & Materials · Energy & Change · Planet Earth

expectItems.label: Key skill
expectItems.value: Independent fair tests · interpreting results · evidence-based conclusions

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Life and living — reproduction and growth
topics: Reproduction in plants: sexual and asexual reproduction
Pollination: self- and cross-pollination, agents of pollination
Seed dispersal: wind, water, animals, explosive mechanisms
Reproduction in animals: sexual reproduction, life cycles
Human reproductive system — introduction
Growth and development in humans: puberty changes
Technology: design a seed dispersal experiment
Investigation: germination — conditions needed for seeds to sprout

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Matter and materials — chemical change
topics: Chemical changes: burning, rusting, cooking — irreversible changes
Evidence of chemical change: colour change, gas production, heat, smell
Acids and bases: introduction — safe examples in daily life (vinegar, baking soda)
Indicators: litmus paper, red cabbage juice
Oxidation: rust formation and rust prevention
Ceramics, glass and fibres — properties and uses
Technology: design a product using knowledge of materials
Investigation: test household liquids as acid or base

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Energy and change — energy sources and systems
topics: Forms of energy revision: kinetic, potential, thermal, light, sound, electrical, chemical
Energy transfer and transformation — energy chain diagrams
Renewable energy: solar, wind, hydro, biomass
Non-renewable energy: coal, oil, gas, nuclear
South Africa's energy challenges and Eskom
Simple machines: lever, pulley, wheel and axle, inclined plane
Technology: design a wind turbine or solar cooker
Investigation: compare efficiency of different simple machines

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Planet Earth — atmosphere and beyond
topics: The atmosphere: layers — troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere
Composition of the atmosphere: nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide, water vapour
The greenhouse effect and climate change — causes and consequences
Ozone layer: depletion and protection
Earthquakes and volcanoes: causes, effects and safety
The Moon: phases, tides, lunar and solar eclipses
Space exploration: satellites, space stations, Mars missions
Technology: design a model showing the greenhouse effect

skillChips: Describe plant and animal reproduction
Explain pollination and seed dispersal
Identify evidence of chemical change
Test substances as acid or base
Describe renewable and non-renewable energy sources
Explain energy transfer and transformation
Describe layers of the atmosphere
Explain the greenhouse effect
Describe the lunar cycle and tidal patterns
Design and evaluate a technology solution
Plan an independent fair investigation
Interpret results and draw evidence-based conclusions

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M9 2h6M10 2v6.5L4.5 18a2 2 0 0 0 1.7 3h11.6a2 2 0 0 0 1.7-3L14 8.5V2"/><path d="M7.5 14.5h9"/></svg>
tips.text: Understand the fair test process. In tests you are often asked to describe or design a fair test. Remember: change only ONE variable, keep everything else the same, and observe what happens.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Use labelled diagrams — they earn marks. Labelled diagrams of plants, animals, circuits, the water cycle or the solar system are worth marks. Practise drawing and labelling them from memory.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 2 4 14h6l-1 8 9-12h-6l1-8z"/></svg>
tips.text: Learn the key vocabulary. Natural Sciences uses precise technical vocabulary. Words like 'photosynthesis', 'vertebrate', 'conductor' and 'decomposer' have specific meanings — use them correctly.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M3 12h18M12 3c2.5 2.5 3.8 5.6 3.8 9s-1.3 6.5-3.8 9c-2.5-2.5-3.8-5.6-3.8-9S9.5 5.5 12 3z"/></svg>
tips.text: Connect science to real life. The best way to remember content is to connect it to real examples. When you study the water cycle, think of rain. When you study food webs, think of your local environment.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M9 2h6M10 2v6.5L4.5 18a2 2 0 0 0 1.7 3h11.6a2 2 0 0 0 1.7-3L14 8.5V2"/><path d="M7.5 14.5h9"/></svg>
tips.text: Know the difference between physical and chemical change. Physical change is reversible (cutting, dissolving). Chemical change is irreversible (burning, rusting). This distinction appears in almost every Grade 5 and 6 NST test.

subjects.hubDescription: Reproduction, chemical change, energy systems and the atmosphere for Grade 6.

subjects.title: Grade 6 Social Sciences | CAPS Study Materials | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Social Sciences study materials for Grade 6. History and geography — maps, environments, SA history and early civilisations — free papers and memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 6 Social Sciences is the final year of the Intermediate Phase and covers the most complex content yet. The History component traces the history of the slave trade, resistance movements and the early 19th century in southern Africa. The Geography component examines world geography — continents and oceans, world biomes, global environmental challenges and the geography of southern Africa in a world context. Learners practise higher-order source analysis and develop the ability to write structured historical and geographical responses.

expectItems.label: Key skills
expectItems.value: Higher-order source analysis · world geography · structured writing

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: History: the slave trade
topics: Origins of the transatlantic slave trade — why and how it began
The Middle Passage — conditions and human suffering
Slavery at the Cape: who was enslaved, where they came from
Life of enslaved people at the Cape — daily conditions, culture, resistance
The Slave Lodge in Cape Town as historical evidence
Forms of resistance: running away, work slowdowns, revolts
Abolition of slavery: causes and key figures
Impact of the end of slavery on the Cape Colony

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Geography: world geography and mapping
topics: Continents and oceans of the world — location and characteristics
Latitude and longitude — using coordinates to locate places
Time zones: how and why they exist
World biomes: tropical rainforest, desert, grassland, temperate, tundra, polar
Global climate patterns: factors affecting world climate
World population distribution — reasons for dense and sparse settlement
Thematic maps: population maps, climate maps, vegetation maps
GIS — introduction to digital mapping

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: History: resistance in southern Africa (19th century)
topics: The Mfecane/Difaqane — causes, key events and consequences
Shaka kaSenzangakhona and the rise of the Zulu kingdom
The Voortrekkers: reasons for the Great Trek
Conflicts between Voortrekkers and African kingdoms
The Battle of Blood River (1838) — different perspectives
African kingdoms resisting colonial expansion: Xhosa, Sotho, Zulu
Moshoeshoe I and the formation of the Basotho nation
Sources and perspectives: the importance of hearing different voices

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Geography: environment and sustainability
topics: Global environmental challenges: deforestation, desertification, ocean pollution
Climate change: causes, evidence, global impacts
South Africa's environmental agreements: international context
Sustainable development goals (SDGs) — relevant examples
Energy choices: fossil fuels vs renewable energy globally
Water as a scarce global resource — conflicts over water
Comparing environmental management in different countries
Writing a structured geographical response using evidence

skillChips: Explain causes and conditions of the slave trade
Use latitude and longitude to locate places
Identify and describe world biomes
Explain the Mfecane and its consequences
Describe the Great Trek and its causes
Analyse different historical perspectives on the same event
Explain global environmental challenges
Use thematic maps to extract information
Write a structured historical response using evidence
Describe sustainable development goals with examples

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M3 12h18M12 3c2.5 2.5 3.8 5.6 3.8 9s-1.3 6.5-3.8 9c-2.5-2.5-3.8-5.6-3.8-9S9.5 5.5 12 3z"/></svg>
tips.text: Learn the map elements by heart. Every map test will ask about the key, compass rose, scale and title. These are easy marks — always know all four and apply them first.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Use specific names and dates in history answers. Good history answers include specific people, places and dates. Instead of 'a long time ago' write '1652'. Specific details earn more marks.
