tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Draw maps to practise geography. Draw South Africa's biomes, major rivers and provinces from memory once a week. This is the most effective geography revision technique.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M3 12h18M12 3c2.5 2.5 3.8 5.6 3.8 9s-1.3 6.5-3.8 9c-2.5-2.5-3.8-5.6-3.8-9S9.5 5.5 12 3z"/></svg>
tips.text: Link history and geography together. The best Social Sciences students understand how geography shaped history — why settlements were built near rivers, why trade routes followed coastlines, why certain areas had conflict.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="10.5" cy="10.5" r="7"/><path d="M20.5 20.5 15.8 15.8"/></svg>
tips.text: When analysing sources, always ask: who wrote this, when and why? The source's origin, date and purpose determine whether it is reliable and what perspective it represents. Always reference the source in your answer.

subjects.hubDescription: Slave trade, Mfecane, world geography and environmental sustainability for Grade 6.

subjects.title: Grade 7 Afrikaans First Additional Language | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Afrikaans First Additional Language for Grade 7. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 7 Afrikaans First Additional Language builds on the functional literacy of the Intermediate Phase. Learners read slightly more complex Afrikaans texts, write structured paragraphs across different text types, and use a wider range of grammatical structures. The focus is on developing practical Afrikaans communication skills in preparation for the increasing demands of Grades 8 and 9.

expectItems.label: Key progression
expectItems.value: Multi-paragraph writing · transactional texts · extended vocabulary

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Narrative texts and extended sentence structures
topics: Read Afrikaans narrative texts and answer literal, inferential and evaluative questions
Compound and complex sentences using coordinating and subordinating conjunctions
Revision and extension of present, past and future tense
Relative pronouns: wat, wie in sentences
Write a structured narrative paragraph with introduction, development and conclusion
Vocabulary building: word families, synonyms, antonyms in Afrikaans
Direct speech: punctuation and use in narrative writing
Oral: short prepared talk on a personal topic in Afrikaans

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Descriptive and transactional texts
topics: Read descriptive Afrikaans texts and formal texts (letters, notices, advertisements)
Modal verbs: kan, mag, moet, sal, wil, sou — in context
Degrees of comparison: adjectives and adverbs
Apostrophe for possession and contraction
Write a formal Afrikaans letter or informal letter
Write a short descriptive paragraph about a place or person
Word formation: prefixes and suffixes in Afrikaans
Oral: describe a picture or process in Afrikaans

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Informational texts and direct/indirect speech
topics: Read Afrikaans informational and argumentative texts
Direct speech to indirect speech and back — conversion practice
Passive voice — recognition and simple use in Afrikaans
Revision of tenses — all tenses covered so far
Write a short Afrikaans informational paragraph or advertisement
Vocabulary: context clues to work out word meanings
Conjunctions: coordinating and subordinating — extended list
Oral: summarise an Afrikaans text in own words

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Persuasive texts, poetry and revision
topics: Read persuasive Afrikaans texts — identify techniques, tone, purpose
Simple Afrikaans poetry: stanzas, rhyme, rhythm, simile, personification
Identify figurative language in Afrikaans poems
Revision of all grammar: nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, tenses, speech
Write a short persuasive paragraph in Afrikaans
Write a simple Afrikaans poem or creative paragraph
Oral: recite a memorised Afrikaans poem or dialogue
Examination preparation: comprehension strategies and time management

skillChips: Read Afrikaans texts with understanding
Use modal verbs in context
Write compound and complex Afrikaans sentences
Convert direct to indirect speech in Afrikaans
Write a formal Afrikaans letter
Identify Afrikaans figurative language
Write a structured multi-paragraph Afrikaans text
Use degrees of comparison
Build vocabulary through prefixes, suffixes and context
Summarise an Afrikaans text in own words

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Build Afrikaans vocabulary daily. Learn 5 new Afrikaans words with meanings every day. In a term that is 200 new words.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Read the question before the passage. Know what you are looking for before reading.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Write formal letters using the correct layout. Afrikaans formal letters have a specific structure — address, date, salutation, body, closing. Learn it.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Practise Afrikaans out loud. Speaking the language, even imperfectly, accelerates learning.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Use conjunctions to make your writing flow. Connect ideas with: omdat, alhoewel, terwyl, maar, en, of. This lifts your writing immediately.

subjects.hubDescription: Multi-paragraph writing, transactional texts and extended grammar for Grade 7.

subjects.title: Grade 7 Afrikaans Home Language | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Afrikaans Home Language for Grade 7. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Graad 7 Afrikaans Huistaal begin die Seniorfase en stel hoër eise aan leerders. Hulle werk met prosa, poësie en dramatiese tekste, en produseer uitgebreide formele skryfwerk. Die vier geïntegreerde vaardighede — luister en praat, lees en kyk, skryf en aanbied, en taalstrukture en -konvensies — word op 'n gevorderde vlak ontwikkel met klem op letterkundige analise, formele opstelle en korrekte taalgebruik.

expectItems.label: Sleutelverskuiwing
expectItems.value: Letterkundige analise · formele opstel · gevorderde grammatika

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Prosa en taal: sinstruktuur en tye
topics: Lees 'n prosateks (roman of kortverhale) — letterlike, inferensiële en evalueringsvrae
Identifiseer verteller, karakter, agtergrond, plot en tema in prosa
Tydhersiening en uitbreiding: voltooide tye (teenwoordig, verlede, toekomend voltooid)
Komplekse sinne: hoofsin en bysin, voegwoorde
Indirekte rede: direk na indirek (alle tye)
Opstelskryfwerk: inleiding, liggaamsparagrawe, gevolgtrekkingstruktuur
Woordeskat: konteksaanwysings, woordfamilies, konnotasie vs denotasie
Mondeling: voorbereide toespraak met uitdrukking, pas en duidelikheid

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Poësie en beeldspraak
topics: Lees en analiseer poësie: beelding, toon, stemming, tema, struktuur
Stylfigure: vergelyking, metafoor, personifikasie, hiperbool, alliterasie, assonansie, onomatopee
Identifiseer en verduidelik die effek van taalkeuses in gedigte
Bedryfssin en lydende sin — hersiening en toepassing in eie skryfwerk
Trappe van vergelyking — onreëlmatige byvoeglike naamwoorde en bywoorde
Formele briefskryfwerk: uitleg, register en toon
Leestekens: hersiening van alle Intermediêre Fase tekens + dubbelpunt en kommapunt
Mondeling: gedigopsê of dramatiese voorlees

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Drama en transaksionele skryfwerk
topics: Lees 'n dramatiese teks of uittreksel: toneelrigtings, dialoog, dramatiese middele
Identifiseer konflik, hoogtepunt, karaktermotivering en dramatiese ironie
Transaksionele tekste: advertensie, brosjure, brief, resensie, dagboek
Kenmerke en register van transaksionele tekste
Voorwaardelike sinne: nul-, eerste en tweede kondisionaal
Modale werkwoorde: hersiening en uitbreiding in eie skryfwerk
Woordvorming: voor- en agtervoegsels, wortels — etimologie
Mondeling: rolspel, debat, groepsbespreking

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Visuele tekste, hersiening en opstelskryfwerk
topics: Analiseer visuele tekste: spotprente, advertensies, foto's — samestelling, doel, gehoor
Mediavaardighede: vooroordeel, perspektief, feit vs mening
Paragraafskryfwerk: vergelyk en kontrasteer, oorsaak en gevolg, oorreding
Formele opstel: beplan, konsep, hersien en bied 'n afgewerkte stuk aan
Hersiening van alle grammatika: woordsoorte, tye, stem, rede
Begripshersiening: meerteks-vergelyking
Spelstrategieë: ezelsbruggetjies, patrone, reëls
Mondeling: formele aanbieding met visuele hulpmiddel

skillChips: Analiseer prosa vir karakter, agtergrond en tema
Identifiseer en verduidelik stylfigure in poësie
Skakel direkte na indirekte rede om
Gebruik voltooide tye korrek
Skryf 'n gestruktureerde formele opstel
Produseer akkurate transaksionele tekste
Analiseer visuele en mediatekste krities
Gebruik voorwaardelike sinne en modale werkwoorde
Pas bedryfssin en lydende sin toe
Demonstreer beheersing van leestekens
Lees en voer dramatiese tekste uit
Bou woordeskat deur konteks en etimologie

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Lees die vrae voor die teks. Weet waarna jy soek voor jy die teks lees. Onderstreep sleutelwoorde in elke vraag.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Merktoekenning = merktelling. 'n 4-merkvraag benodig 4 afsonderlike punte. Skryf nooit een sin vir 'n meermerkvraag nie.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Haal aan uit die teks. Gebruik: 'In reël 3 skryf die digter...' of 'Die teks sê...' Bewys verdien punte.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Ken jou stylfigure met voorbeelde. Identifiseer die tegniek, haal aan, verduidelik die effek op die leser.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Skryf opstelle in drie fases. Beplan → Konsep → Hersien. Selfs 5 minute se beplanning lewer 'n sterker opstel.

subjects.hubDescription: Prosa, poësie, drama en formele skryfwerk vir Graad 7 Afrikaans Huistaal.

subjects.title: Grade 7 Creative Arts | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Creative Arts for Grade 7. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 7 Creative Arts develops learners' creative and artistic abilities across four art forms: Visual Arts, Music, Drama and Dance. The CAPS curriculum integrates creative expression with knowledge of art techniques, cultural contexts and performance skills. Learners explore their own creativity while developing an appreciation of South African and global artistic traditions. Schools may focus on two of the four art forms depending on available resources and teacher expertise.

expectItems.label: Art forms
expectItems.value: Visual Arts · Music · Drama · Dance (2 selected)

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Visual Art and Music foundations
topics: Visual Art: elements of design — line, shape, colour, texture, space, form, value
Colour theory: primary, secondary, tertiary colours; warm and cool colours
Drawing techniques: proportion, perspective, shading
Visual Art practical: portrait or observational drawing using pencil or charcoal
Music: elements of music — pitch, rhythm, dynamics, tempo, timbre, texture
Music notation: treble clef, notes on the staff, time signatures (2/4, 3/4, 4/4)
Music practical: perform a piece on an instrument or sing in parts
Art appreciation: analyse a South African artwork using the elements of design

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Drama and Dance
topics: Drama: elements of drama — role, situation, tension, focus, space, time, movement
Voice and body as expressive instruments — warm-ups, breathing, projection
Drama techniques: freeze frame, still image, hot seating, thought tracking
Drama practical: create and perform a short scripted or devised scene
Dance: elements of dance — body, space, time, energy, relationships
South African indigenous dance forms — context and movements
Dance practical: learn and perform a short indigenous or contemporary dance sequence
Drama and Dance appreciation: compare performance styles across cultures

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Intermediate skills in chosen art forms
topics: Visual Art: printmaking — relief printing, monoprint; or sculpture using clay or recycled materials
Visual Art: study of a South African artist — technique, context, personal response
Music: music of South Africa — indigenous, jazz, gospel, kwaito — context and features
Music: composition — create an 8-bar melody or rhythmic composition
Drama: character development — objectives, obstacles, backstory
Drama: performance skills — memorisation, cueing, stage placement
Dance: choreography basics — pattern, motif, development
Combined: plan and contribute to a class arts showcase

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Performance, refinement and appreciation
topics: Visual Art: mixed media artwork combining at least two techniques
Music: ensemble performance — perform in a group, awareness of other parts
Drama: full scene performance — blocking, props, costumes, lighting awareness
Dance: full choreographed performance — group piece with a unifying concept
Arts showcase: present work from all four terms
Art criticism: write a short review of a classmate's or professional's work
South African arts heritage: contribution of SA artists to world culture
Reflection: personal growth as a creative artist across Grade 7

skillChips: Apply the elements of design in visual artworks
Use colour theory in practical art
Draw with correct proportion and perspective
Read basic music notation
Perform music or sing in parts
Use voice and body expressively in drama
Perform a drama scene with character and intention
Perform a dance sequence with awareness of elements
Analyse artworks using correct terminology
Write a short art criticism or review

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 3v5M12 16v5M3 12h5M16 12h5M6 6l3 3M15 15l3 3M18 6l-3 3M9 15l-3 3"/></svg>
tips.text: Practise technique regularly. Art skills improve through repetition. Sketch daily, practise scales, rehearse lines.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Use art vocabulary in written responses. Terms like 'proportion', 'dynamics', 'tension' and 'motif' show understanding and earn marks.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M3 12h18M12 3c2.5 2.5 3.8 5.6 3.8 9s-1.3 6.5-3.8 9c-2.5-2.5-3.8-5.6-3.8-9S9.5 5.5 12 3z"/></svg>
tips.text: Connect art to its cultural context. Understanding where and why an art form developed helps you analyse it far more deeply.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 3v5M12 16v5M3 12h5M16 12h5M6 6l3 3M15 15l3 3M18 6l-3 3M9 15l-3 3"/></svg>
tips.text: Commit fully in drama and dance. Half-hearted performance earns half marks. Commit to character, movement and energy.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Art is about process, not just product. Teachers assess your thinking and creative choices, not just the final piece. Explain your decisions.

subjects.hubDescription: Visual Art, Music, Drama and Dance — creative expression and cultural appreciation.

subjects.title: Grade 7 Economic Management and Science | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Economic Management and Science for Grade 7. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 7 Economic Management and Science (EMS) introduces learners to the foundations of economic and business life. The CAPS curriculum covers three integrated areas: the Economy, Financial Literacy and Entrepreneurship. Learners explore how individuals, businesses and governments make economic decisions, how financial records are kept, and what it means to be entrepreneurial. EMS in Grade 7 focuses on basic concepts that are essential for understanding South Africa's economy and for personal financial management.

expectItems.label: Key concepts
expectItems.value: Needs vs wants · budget · profit · basic bookkeeping

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: The economy: needs, wants and resources
topics: Needs vs wants: distinguishing between them with South African examples
Scarcity: limited resources vs unlimited wants — the basic economic problem
Factors of production: land, labour, capital, entrepreneurship
Economic sectors: primary, secondary, tertiary — with SA examples
The circular flow of income: households and firms
Goods and services: tangible vs intangible
The role of government in the economy: taxes, public services
Opportunity cost: the concept and real-life examples

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Financial literacy: income, expenditure and budgeting
topics: Sources of income: salary, wages, rent, interest, profit
Types of expenditure: fixed vs variable; essential vs non-essential
Personal budget: income minus expenditure — surplus or deficit
The budget cycle: plan, implement, review
Financial institutions: banks, insurance companies, credit unions in SA
Banking services: savings account, current account, fixed deposit
The importance of saving — compound interest (introduction)
Consumer rights and responsibilities in South Africa

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Basic bookkeeping and financial records
topics: The accounting equation: Assets = Liabilities + Owner's Equity
Source documents: receipts, invoices, cash slips — what they record
Cash receipts journal (CRJ): record cash received by a business
Cash payments journal (CPJ): record cash paid by a business
Balancing a simple cash journal
Petty cash: what it is, how it is controlled (petty cash voucher)
Debtors and creditors: who they are and why they matter
Bank reconciliation: concept — why the cash book and bank statement differ

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Entrepreneurship and business in SA
topics: Definition of entrepreneurship — characteristics of a successful entrepreneur
Difference between a business idea and a business opportunity
Types of businesses in SA: sole trader, partnership, close corporation, company
Business plan: components — vision, mission, product/service, market, finance
The role of SMMEs in the South African economy
Marketing mix: product, price, place, promotion (4 Ps)
Profit and loss: calculating gross and net profit
Social entrepreneurship: businesses that solve social problems

skillChips: Distinguish needs from wants and explain scarcity
Describe the factors of production
Identify primary, secondary and tertiary sectors
Draw and explain the circular flow of income
Compile a personal or household budget
Identify types of income and expenditure
Record entries in a cash receipts and payments journal
Explain the accounting equation
Calculate simple profit and loss
Describe characteristics of a successful entrepreneur
Outline components of a simple business plan
Explain consumer rights in South Africa

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="2" y="5" width="20" height="14" rx="2"/><path d="M2 10h20"/></svg>
tips.text: Learn the accounting equation. Assets = Liabilities + Owner's Equity. Every bookkeeping question in EMS connects to this equation.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="m3 16 6-6 4 4 8-9"/><path d="M15 5h6v6"/></svg>
tips.text: Practise journal entries with examples. EMS tests give you source documents and ask you to record them. Practise with real receipts and invoices.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Distinguish EMS terms precisely. 'Revenue' is not the same as 'profit'. 'Debtor' is not the same as 'creditor'. Learn exact definitions.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M3 12h18M12 3c2.5 2.5 3.8 5.6 3.8 9s-1.3 6.5-3.8 9c-2.5-2.5-3.8-5.6-3.8-9S9.5 5.5 12 3z"/></svg>
tips.text: Connect EMS to real SA life. When you buy something at Checkers, you are the consumer in the circular flow. Making it real helps you remember.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: A budget is just income minus expenditure. Don't overthink budgets. List income, list expenses, subtract — check if surplus or deficit.

subjects.hubDescription: Economy, financial literacy, bookkeeping and entrepreneurship for Grade 7.

subjects.title: Grade 7 English First Additional Language | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned English First Additional Language for Grade 7. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 7 English First Additional Language builds on the functional English literacy of the Intermediate Phase. Learners read more complex texts, write structured paragraphs across different text types and use a wider range of grammatical structures. The focus is on practical English communication — reading with understanding, writing clearly and speaking with confidence.

expectItems.label: Key progression
expectItems.value: Multi-paragraph writing · transactional texts · extended vocabulary

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Narrative texts and extended sentence structures
topics: Read narrative texts and answer literal, inferential and evaluative questions
Compound and complex sentences using coordinating and subordinating conjunctions
Revision and extension of present, past and future tense
Relative pronouns: who, which, that in sentences
Write a structured narrative paragraph with introduction, development and conclusion
Vocabulary: word families, synonyms, antonyms
Direct speech: punctuation and use in narrative writing
Oral: short prepared talk on a personal topic

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Descriptive and transactional texts
topics: Read descriptive texts and formal texts (letters, notices, advertisements)
Modal verbs: can, may, must, will, would — in context
Degrees of comparison: adjectives and adverbs
Apostrophe for possession and contraction
Write a formal or informal letter
Write a short descriptive paragraph about a place or person
Word formation: prefixes and suffixes
Oral: describe a picture or process clearly

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Informational texts and direct/indirect speech
topics: Read informational and argumentative texts
Direct speech to indirect speech and back — conversion practice
Passive voice — recognition and simple use
Revision of all tenses covered so far
Write a short informational paragraph or advertisement
Vocabulary: use context clues to work out word meanings
Conjunctions: extended list — coordinating and subordinating
Oral: summarise a text in own words

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Persuasive texts, poetry and revision
topics: Read persuasive texts — identify techniques, tone, purpose
Simple poetry: stanzas, rhyme, rhythm, simile, personification
Identify figurative language in poems
Revision of all grammar: parts of speech, tenses, speech, voice
Write a short persuasive paragraph
Write a simple poem or creative paragraph
Oral: recite a memorised poem or short dialogue
Examination preparation: comprehension strategies and time management

skillChips: Read texts with understanding at Grade 7 level
Use modal verbs in context
Write compound and complex sentences
Convert direct to indirect speech
Write a formal letter with correct layout
Identify figurative language in poems
Write a structured multi-paragraph text
Use degrees of comparison
Build vocabulary through prefixes, suffixes and context
Summarise a text accurately in own words

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Build vocabulary every day. Five new words a day = 200 per term. Strong vocabulary is the biggest advantage in English tests.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Read questions before the passage. Know what you are looking for before reading.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Use the correct letter layout. Address, date, salutation, body, closing. Learn it once and use it every time.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Practise English out loud. Speaking builds fluency and confidence faster than any other method.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Connect ideas with conjunctions. Use because, although, while, but, and, or to make your writing flow better immediately.

subjects.hubDescription: Multi-paragraph writing, transactional texts and extended grammar for Grade 7.

subjects.title: Grade 7 English Home Language | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned English Home Language for Grade 7. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 7 English Home Language marks the start of the Senior Phase. Learners engage analytically with a range of text types — prose, poetry, drama, visual and transactional texts. The four skills (listening and speaking, reading and viewing, writing and presenting, language structures and conventions) are developed at a higher level, with emphasis on literary analysis, formal essay writing and accurate grammar.

expectItems.label: Key shift
expectItems.value: Literary analysis · formal essay · advanced grammar

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Prose and language: sentence structure and tense
topics: Read a prose text (novel or short stories) — literal, inferential, evaluative questions
Identify narrator, character, setting, plot and theme in prose
Tense revision and extension: perfect tenses (present, past, future perfect)
Complex sentences: main and subordinate clauses, conjunctions
Reported speech: direct to indirect (all tenses)
Essay writing: introduction, body paragraphs, conclusion structure
Vocabulary: context clues, word families, connotation vs denotation
Oral: prepared speech with expression, pace and clarity

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Poetry and figurative language
topics: Read and analyse poetry: imagery, tone, mood, theme, structure
Figures of speech: simile, metaphor, personification, hyperbole, alliteration, assonance, onomatopoeia
Identify and explain the effect of language choices in poetry
Active and passive voice — revision and application in own writing
Degrees of comparison — irregular adjectives and adverbs
Formal letter writing: layout, register and tone
Punctuation: revision of all Intermediate Phase marks + colon and semicolon
Oral: poetry recitation or dramatic reading

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Drama and transactional writing
topics: Read a dramatic text or extract: stage directions, dialogue, dramatic devices
Identify conflict, climax, character motivation and dramatic irony
Transactional texts: advertisement, brochure, letter, review, diary
Features and register of transactional texts
Conditional sentences: zero, first and second conditional
Modal verbs: revision and extension in own writing
Word formation: prefixes, suffixes, roots — etymology
Oral: role play, debate, group discussion

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Visual texts, revision and essay writing
topics: Analyse visual texts: cartoons, advertisements, photographs — composition, purpose, audience
Media literacy: bias, perspective, fact vs opinion
Paragraph writing: compare and contrast, cause and effect, persuasive
Formal essay: plan, draft, revise and present a polished piece
Revision of all grammar: parts of speech, tenses, voice, speech
Comprehension revision: multi-text comparison
Spelling strategies: mnemonics, patterns, rules
Oral: formal presentation with visual aid

skillChips: Analyse prose for character, setting and theme
Identify and explain figures of speech in poetry
Convert direct to indirect speech
Use perfect tenses correctly
Write a structured formal essay
Produce accurate transactional texts
Analyse visual and media texts critically
Use conditional sentences and modal verbs
Apply active and passive voice
Demonstrate command of punctuation
Read and perform dramatic texts
Build vocabulary through context and etymology

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Read the questions before the text. Knowing what to look for helps you find evidence faster. Underline key terms in each question first.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Mark allocation = mark count. A 4-mark question needs 4 distinct points. Never write one sentence for a multi-mark question.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Quote from the text. Use: 'In line 3 the poet writes...' or 'The text states...' Evidence earns marks.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Know your figures of speech by example. Don't just define — identify the technique, quote it, explain its effect on the reader.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Write essays in three stages. Plan → Draft → Revise. Even 5 minutes of planning produces a stronger, more organised essay.

subjects.hubDescription: Literary analysis, formal essay, advanced grammar and transactional writing — CAPS Grade 7.

subjects.title: Grade 7 Life Orientation | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Life Orientation for Grade 7. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 7 Life Orientation prepares learners for the personal, social and academic challenges of the Senior Phase. The CAPS curriculum covers five focus areas: Development of the Self in Society, Constitutional Rights and Responsibilities, Life Skills, Physical Education, and Career and Career Choices. Life Orientation in Grade 7 emphasises self-awareness, healthy relationships, citizenship and the development of study and life skills for success in secondary school.

expectItems.label: Five areas
expectItems.value: Self · Rights · Life Skills · PE · Career

expectItems.label: Key focus
expectItems.value: Self-awareness · rights · study skills · physical fitness

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Self in society and physical education
topics: Identity: values, beliefs, personal strengths and areas for growth
Emotional intelligence: identifying, understanding and managing emotions
Adolescent development: physical, cognitive and social-emotional changes
Healthy lifestyle choices: nutrition, sleep, exercise, screen time
Physical Education: locomotor skills, fitness components — strength, endurance, flexibility, speed
Fitness testing: baseline measurements and personal fitness goals
Study skills: time management, planning, creating a study schedule
Goal setting: SMART goals for Grade 7 and beyond

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Constitutional rights and responsibilities
topics: The South African Constitution: structure, Bill of Rights, key principles
Human rights: which rights Grade 7 learners have and how to claim them
Responsibilities that come with rights: at school, at home, in the community
Democracy: how it works in South Africa — elections, parliament, local government
Discrimination and prejudice: recognition, impact, how to respond
Gender-based violence: awareness, causes, prevention, reporting
Child protection: abuse prevention, safe adults and support systems
Civic participation: what it means to be an active citizen

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Life skills: relationships and decision-making
topics: Peer relationships: healthy and unhealthy friendships — what to look for
Peer pressure: types, influence on behaviour, assertiveness and refusal skills
Romantic relationships: respect, boundaries, consent — age-appropriate discussion
Substance abuse: alcohol, tobacco, cannabis — short and long-term effects on the body
Decision-making framework: identify options, consider consequences, choose wisely
Conflict resolution: negotiation, compromise, mediation
Physical Education: team sport skills — strategy, roles, fair play
Mental health: stress management, seeking help, destigmatisation

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Careers and future planning
topics: Self-knowledge for career planning: strengths, interests, values, skills
Overview of career fields: STEM, arts, business, social services, trades
Education pathways in South Africa: NSC, technical schools, FET colleges, universities
The world of work: types of employment, changing job market
Entrepreneurship as a career option
Financial literacy for teens: budgeting, saving, avoiding debt
Physical Education: indigenous games, recreational activities, active living
Reflection: personal growth across Grade 7 — what I have learned about myself

skillChips: Describe personal values, strengths and identity
Apply emotional intelligence in social situations
Explain human rights using the Bill of Rights
Identify responsibilities alongside rights
Describe the dangers of substance abuse
Use a decision-making framework
Apply assertiveness and refusal skills
Set SMART personal and academic goals
Describe career fields and educational pathways
Apply basic stress management strategies
Demonstrate physical fitness and sport skills
Identify and respond to discrimination

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8.5"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="4.8"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="1.1" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/></svg>
tips.text: For written tests — learn definitions precisely. Life Orientation uses specific vocabulary: 'assertive', 'Bill of Rights', 'SMART goal'. Know the exact meanings.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Use examples from real SA life. The best LO answers connect theory to real South African contexts — reference the Constitution, Eskom, GBV statistics.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8.5"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="4.8"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="1.1" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/></svg>
tips.text: PE marks come from participation. Every PE lesson is an assessment opportunity. Attend, try your best and listen to instructions.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Connect LO to your own experience. The content is most memorable when personal. When studying peer pressure, think about real situations you have faced.

subjects.hubDescription: Self-development, rights, decision-making, careers and physical education.

subjects.title: Grade 7 Mathematics | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Mathematics for Grade 7. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 7 Mathematics extends the number system to include integers and the introduction of formal algebra. The CAPS curriculum covers five content areas: Numbers, Operations and Relationships, Patterns, Functions and Algebra, Space and Shape (Geometry), Measurement and Data Handling. Learners begin working with algebraic expressions and equations, geometric proofs about angles and triangles, and more sophisticated data analysis. Grade 7 Maths is a crucial year — the foundations built here underpin all of FET Mathematics.

expectItems.label: Key concepts
expectItems.value: Algebra intro · integers · formal geometry · ratio and proportion

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Integers, whole numbers and exponents
topics: Integers: order, compare, add, subtract, multiply, divide negative numbers
Number lines extending in both directions
Properties of integers: commutative, associative, distributive
Exponents: squares and cubes, square roots and cube roots
Prime factorisation using exponent notation
LCM and HCF using prime factorisation
Multiples and factors — revision and extension
Order of operations (BODMAS) with integers and exponents

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Common fractions, decimals, percentages and ratio
topics: Common fractions: add, subtract, multiply, divide — mixed numbers
Equivalent fractions, simplifying, comparing
Decimal fractions: all four operations to 3 decimal places
Convert between fractions, decimals and percentages
Percentage increase and decrease: calculate and apply
Ratio: simplify, use in real contexts (recipes, maps, scale)
Rate: unit rate and comparison
Proportion: direct proportion — solve proportional problems

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Algebra and geometry
topics: Algebraic expressions: identify terms, like terms, coefficients, constants
Simplify algebraic expressions: collect like terms
Substitute values into algebraic expressions
Solve one-step and two-step linear equations
Geometric figures: classify triangles (sides and angles) and quadrilaterals
Angle relationships: supplementary, complementary, vertically opposite, co-interior, alternate
Parallel lines cut by a transversal — angle relationships
Construct geometric figures using compass and protractor

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Measurement, data and revision
topics: Area and perimeter: triangles, quadrilaterals and composite figures
Volume and surface area of rectangular and triangular prisms
Transformation geometry: reflection, rotation, translation, enlargement
Cartesian plane: plotting and reading coordinates in all four quadrants
Data: mean, median, mode, range of ungrouped data
Represent data: bar graphs, histograms, line graphs, pie charts
Interpret and analyse data: draw conclusions, identify trends
Probability: theoretical probability — list outcomes, calculate probability

skillChips: Add, subtract, multiply and divide integers
Apply BODMAS with integers and exponents
Work with fractions, decimals and percentages fluently
Calculate percentage increase and decrease
Simplify and evaluate algebraic expressions
Solve one- and two-step linear equations
Classify triangles and quadrilaterals by properties
Apply angle relationships in parallel lines
Calculate area, perimeter, volume and surface area
Plot and read coordinates in all four quadrants
Calculate mean, median, mode and range
Determine theoretical probability of simple events

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="4.5" y="2.5" width="15" height="19" rx="2"/><path d="M8 6.5h8"/><path d="M8 11h.01M12 11h.01M16 11h.01M8 15h.01M12 15h.01M16 15h.01M8 19h.01M12 19h.01M16 19h.01"/></svg>
tips.text: Integers need direction, not just size. When multiplying or dividing: same signs = positive, different signs = negative. Learn this rule and apply it every time.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Show all working for full marks. Method marks are awarded even if your final answer is wrong.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Algebra is just arithmetic with letters. When you see 3x + 5 = 17, ask: what number × 3 + 5 = 17? Then formalise it.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="4.5" y="2.5" width="15" height="19" rx="2"/><path d="M8 6.5h8"/><path d="M8 11h.01M12 11h.01M16 11h.01M8 15h.01M12 15h.01M16 15h.01M8 19h.01M12 19h.01M16 19h.01"/></svg>
tips.text: BODMAS is non-negotiable. Brackets → Orders → Division/Multiplication → Addition/Subtraction. Always.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Know your times tables to 12 × 12. Almost every Grade 7 Maths topic requires fast, accurate multiplication. No shortcuts here.

subjects.hubDescription: Integers, algebra, geometry, measurement and data — full Grade 7 CAPS guide.

subjects.title: Grade 7 Natural Science | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Natural Science for Grade 7. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 7 Natural Science develops scientific literacy through the four knowledge strands: Life and Living, Matter and Materials, Energy and Change, and Planet Earth and Beyond. Learners plan and conduct increasingly independent investigations, interpret data, and draw evidence-based conclusions. Grade 7 introduces more sophisticated biological concepts (photosynthesis, reproduction), chemistry concepts (mixtures, solutions, physical and chemical change) and physics concepts (forces, energy transfer and the electromagnetic spectrum).

expectItems.label: Four strands
expectItems.value: Life & Living · Matter & Materials · Energy & Change · Planet Earth

expectItems.label: Key skill
expectItems.value: Independent fair tests · data interpretation · evidence-based conclusions

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Life and living: photosynthesis and nutrition
topics: Photosynthesis: word equation, requirements, products, site (chloroplasts)
Leaf structure: cross-section — palisade cells, spongy mesophyll, stomata, guard cells
Comparison of photosynthesis and respiration
Food and nutrition: macro- and micronutrients, balanced diet, malnutrition
Digestive system: organs, functions — mouth to anus
Absorption of nutrients in the small intestine: villi structure
Excretion: role of kidneys, skin, lungs — removing metabolic waste
Investigation: test leaves for starch using iodine solution

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Matter and materials: chemical change
topics: Difference between physical and chemical change — revision and extension
Evidence of chemical change: heat produced/absorbed, gas, colour change, precipitate
Reactions of acids with metals: acid + metal → salt + hydrogen gas
Reactions of acids with carbonates: acid + carbonate → salt + water + CO₂
Neutralisation: acid + base → salt + water
Indicators: litmus, universal indicator — pH scale introduction
Flame test: identifying metal ions from colour (demonstration)
Investigation: reactions of vinegar with different substances

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Energy: forces and electricity
topics: Contact and non-contact forces: friction, gravity, magnetism, electrostatic
Newton's Laws — introduction to force and motion concepts
Pressure: force ÷ area — Pascal and everyday applications
Simple machines: lever, pulley, wheel and axle, inclined plane — mechanical advantage
Electric circuits: revision and extension — series and parallel, resistors
Ohm's Law: introduction — voltage, current, resistance relationship
Electrical energy: power, energy cost calculation (kWh)
Investigation: factors affecting the extension of a spring (Hooke's Law)

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Planet Earth: atmosphere and beyond
topics: Structure of the Earth: crust, mantle, outer core, inner core
Plate tectonics: tectonic plates, continental drift, evidence
Earthquakes: causes, Richter scale, seismograph, SA context
Volcanoes: types, formation, effects on environment and people
The rock cycle: igneous, sedimentary, metamorphic rocks — formation and transformation
Weather and climate: jet stream, global wind patterns, Hadley cells (introduction)
Beyond Earth: the electromagnetic spectrum — radio, microwave, IR, visible, UV, X-ray, gamma
Space technology: satellites, GPS, weather forecasting, communication

skillChips: Write and explain the photosynthesis word equation
Describe the digestive system and absorption
Identify evidence of chemical change
Describe reactions of acids with metals and carbonates
Explain neutralisation and pH
Describe contact and non-contact forces
Calculate pressure using force ÷ area
Explain mechanical advantage of simple machines
Apply Ohm's Law concepts to circuits
Describe the structure of the Earth
Explain plate tectonics and earthquakes
Identify regions of the electromagnetic spectrum

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M9 2h6M10 2v6.5L4.5 18a2 2 0 0 0 1.7 3h11.6a2 2 0 0 0 1.7-3L14 8.5V2"/><path d="M7.5 14.5h9"/></svg>
tips.text: Know the fair test formula. Change one variable, keep all others constant, measure the outcome. Every investigation question follows this pattern.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Labelled diagrams earn marks. Draw and label: leaf cross-section, digestive system, electric circuit, Earth layers. Practise until automatic.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 2 4 14h6l-1 8 9-12h-6l1-8z"/></svg>
tips.text: Learn the key equations. Pressure = Force ÷ Area. Power = Voltage × Current. These appear in tests every year.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M3 12h18M12 3c2.5 2.5 3.8 5.6 3.8 9s-1.3 6.5-3.8 9c-2.5-2.5-3.8-5.6-3.8-9S9.5 5.5 12 3z"/></svg>
tips.text: Connect science to SA contexts. Earthquakes, water scarcity, load shedding — Natural Science connects directly to South African life.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M9 2h6M10 2v6.5L4.5 18a2 2 0 0 0 1.7 3h11.6a2 2 0 0 0 1.7-3L14 8.5V2"/><path d="M7.5 14.5h9"/></svg>
tips.text: Physical vs chemical change is examinable every year. Physical: reversible, no new substance. Chemical: irreversible, new substance formed. Know examples of both.

subjects.hubDescription: Photosynthesis, chemical change, forces, electricity and plate tectonics.

subjects.title: Grade 7 Social Science | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Social Science for Grade 7. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 7 Social Science integrates History and Geography at a Senior Phase level. The History component explores the world before 1600 — early humans, African kingdoms, ancient civilisations and the trans-Saharan trade — building analytical and source-evaluation skills. The Geography component develops map skills, introduces climate systems, world biomes and the geography of Africa and South Africa in a global context. Learners develop the ability to write structured historical and geographical responses.

expectItems.label: Key skills
expectItems.value: Source analysis · map skills · structured written responses

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: History: early humans and African kingdoms
topics: Human origins in Africa: Out of Africa theory, fossil evidence, key sites in SA
Early human development: Homo habilis, Homo erectus, Homo sapiens
Migration of early humans across the globe — evidence
Stone Age: Early, Middle, Late — technologies and lifestyles
Iron Age in southern Africa: transition from hunter-gatherer to farmer
Mapungubwe: Zimbabwe Culture — trade, social structure, significance
The Kingdom of Mali: Mansa Musa, trans-Saharan gold and salt trade
Great Zimbabwe: architecture, trade, decline — different historical interpretations

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Geography: maps, Africa and climate
topics: Map skills revision and extension: scale, contour lines, grid references (latitude/longitude)
Africa: physical geography — major landforms, rivers, lakes
Africa: political geography — countries, capitals, regional groupings
Climate of Africa: factors affecting climate (latitude, altitude, ocean currents, rainfall)
Southern African climate: highveld, lowveld, Karoo, coastal — characteristics
Biomes of Africa: savanna, rainforest, desert, fynbos — climate and vegetation
Human settlement in Africa: population distribution and reasons
Environmental challenges in Africa: deforestation, desertification, water stress

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: History: ancient civilisations and trade
topics: Ancient Egypt: pharaohs, social structure, religion, technology, Nile geography
Mesopotamia: Babylon, the Code of Hammurabi, writing, irrigation
The Silk Road: trade between East Asia, Central Asia, Middle East and Europe
Indian Ocean trade: ports, goods, participants including East Africa
The Mali and Songhai Empires: Timbuktu as a centre of learning and trade
Ibn Battuta: his travels and historical value as a source
The role of religion in early societies: Islam, Christianity, traditional African religion
Evaluating sources: bias, reliability, origin, purpose — applied to ancient sources

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Geography: South Africa's physical and human geography
topics: South Africa's landforms: Great Escarpment, Highveld, coastal zones
South Africa's drainage regions: Orange, Limpopo, Vaal — watersheds
South Africa's climate regions: Mediterranean, subtropical, semi-arid, temperate
South Africa's biomes: fynbos, Karoo, savanna, grassland, forest
Population distribution in SA: density maps, reasons for patterns
Urbanisation in South Africa: push factors, pull factors, urban challenges
Rural-urban migration: causes, consequences, solutions
Writing a structured geographical response: evidence, explanation, example

skillChips: Describe the Out of Africa theory and early human development
Analyse historical sources for bias and reliability
Describe African kingdoms: Mapungubwe, Mali, Great Zimbabwe
Use coordinates to locate places on a world map
Describe Africa's physical and political geography
Explain factors affecting climate
Identify Africa's major biomes
Describe ancient civilisations: Egypt, Mesopotamia
Explain the Silk Road and Indian Ocean trade
Describe South Africa's landforms, rivers and biomes
Explain urbanisation and rural-urban migration in SA
Write structured historical and geographical responses

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M3 12h18M12 3c2.5 2.5 3.8 5.6 3.8 9s-1.3 6.5-3.8 9c-2.5-2.5-3.8-5.6-3.8-9S9.5 5.5 12 3z"/></svg>
tips.text: Master map elements first. Key, compass rose, scale, title. These earn easy marks in every geography question — always apply them.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Name names in history answers. Specific people, places and dates (Mansa Musa, Timbuktu, 1324) turn a general answer into a great answer.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Structure your written responses. Point → Explanation → Evidence. This three-part pattern works for both history and geography questions.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M3 12h18M12 3c2.5 2.5 3.8 5.6 3.8 9s-1.3 6.5-3.8 9c-2.5-2.5-3.8-5.6-3.8-9S9.5 5.5 12 3z"/></svg>
tips.text: Draw maps to revise geography. Sketch Africa, mark the biomes, major rivers and population centres. Drawing locks information in memory.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="10.5" cy="10.5" r="7"/><path d="M20.5 20.5 15.8 15.8"/></svg>
tips.text: When analysing sources, cite the source. Always reference: 'According to Source A...' and explain what it tells us and whether it is reliable.

subjects.hubDescription: African kingdoms, ancient civilisations, Africa geography and SA physical geography.

subjects.title: Grade 7 Technology | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Technology for Grade 7. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 7 Technology develops design and problem-solving skills through the Design Process: investigate, design, make, evaluate and communicate. Learners apply knowledge of structures, mechanisms, processing and systems and control to practical design challenges. The CAPS curriculum integrates technical drawing, materials knowledge and construction skills with the broader technological literacy required in the modern world. Grade 7 Technology builds the foundation for Engineering, Graphics and Design and other technical subjects in the FET Phase.

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Structures: strength and stability
topics: The Design Process: investigate (problem analysis), design (sketches, notes), make, evaluate, communicate
Structures: natural and human-made structures — what they share
Forces on structures: compression, tension, torsion, shear
Triangulation: why triangles make structures stronger
Frame structures vs shell structures — examples and comparison
Technical drawing: isometric and orthographic (front, top, side view)
Materials: properties — strength, flexibility, hardness, conductivity, cost
Practical: design and build a bridge structure to carry maximum load

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Mechanisms: linking and controlling movement
topics: Mechanisms: devices that change force or movement
Levers: class 1, 2 and 3 levers — fulcrum, load, effort
Pulleys: fixed, moveable and compound — mechanical advantage
Gears: how they work, gear ratios, direction of rotation
Cams and cranks: converting rotary to reciprocating motion
Linkages: parallel, bell-crank, reverse motion linkages
Technical drawing: exploded views and assembly drawings
Practical: design and build a mechanism demonstrating gear or pulley use

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Processing: food, paper and textiles
topics: Processing: changing the properties of materials to make them more useful
Food processing: preservation methods — salting, drying, fermenting, pasteurising
Paper-making process: raw materials, pulping, forming, drying
Textile production: natural fibres (cotton, wool, silk) and synthetic fibres (nylon, polyester)
Weaving, knitting and bonding — how fabric structure affects properties
Recycling and sustainability in processing industries
Technical drawing: cutting planes and sectional views
Practical: design a product that involves processing a raw material

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Systems and control: electrical and electronic
topics: Systems: input, process, output — applied to everyday systems
Control systems: why we use control (safety, efficiency, automation)
Electrical systems: series and parallel circuits — revision and extension in a design context
Electronic components: resistor, capacitor, LED, transistor (basic function)
Switches and sensors: types and uses in control systems
Simple programs: flow diagrams for control — IF-THEN-ELSE logic
Technical drawing: circuit diagrams using correct symbols
Practical: design and build a simple system with a control element (switch, sensor or timer)

skillChips: Apply all five stages of the Design Process
Describe forces on structures: compression, tension, torsion, shear
Explain why triangulation strengthens structures
Draw isometric and orthographic technical drawings
Describe and compare lever, pulley and gear mechanisms
Calculate mechanical advantage
Describe food, paper and textile processing
Explain the systems model: input, process, output
Design and build a practical solution to a problem
Evaluate a design against its original specification
Draw circuit diagrams using correct symbols
Explain basic electronic components and their functions

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M14.7 6.3a4 4 0 0 0-5.4 5.4L3 18l3 3 6.3-6.3a4 4 0 0 0 5.4-5.4l-2.8 2.8-2-2z"/></svg>
tips.text: Learn the Design Process steps by heart. Investigate → Design → Make → Evaluate → Communicate. Every Technology test refers to these stages.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="4.5" y="2.5" width="15" height="19" rx="2"/><path d="M8 6.5h8"/><path d="M8 11h.01M12 11h.01M16 11h.01M8 15h.01M12 15h.01M16 15h.01M8 19h.01M12 19h.01M16 19h.01"/></svg>
tips.text: Technical drawing takes practice. Isometric and orthographic drawing are skills — practise 10 minutes every day in Term 1.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Evaluate honestly against your spec. When you evaluate a solution, compare it to the original specification. What worked? What would you change? This earns marks.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="3.2"/><path d="M12 3v2.2M12 18.8V21M4.9 7.5l1.9 1.1M17.2 15.4l1.9 1.1M3 12h2.2M18.8 12H21M4.9 16.5l1.9-1.1M17.2 8.6l1.9-1.1M7.5 19.1l1.1-1.9M15.4 6.8l1.1-1.9M9.5 4.9l.6-2M14 4.9l-.6-2"/></svg>
tips.text: Understand why triangles are strong. Triangulation is the most important structural concept in Grade 7 Technology. Know it, explain it, draw it.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Technology is about solving real problems. Every design challenge must start with understanding the user and the context. The best designs meet real human needs.

subjects.hubDescription: Design process, structures, mechanisms, processing and systems and control.

subjects.title: Grade 8 Afrikaans First Additional Language | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Afrikaans First Additional Language for Grade 8. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 8 Afrikaans FAL extends the work of Grade 7 to more complex texts and a wider range of writing tasks. Learners write multi-paragraph Afrikaans texts across different registers, handle more advanced grammar including complex tenses and reported speech, and read argumentative and literary texts with understanding.

expectItems.label: Key progression
expectItems.value: Extended paragraphs · argumentative writing · literary texts

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Narrative and descriptive texts
topics: Read Afrikaans narrative and descriptive texts — literal, inferential, evaluative questions
Complex sentences: subordinate clauses of time, reason, condition
Revision of direct and indirect speech — extend to past tense reporting
Degrees of comparison: revision and extension with irregular forms
Write a multi-paragraph Afrikaans narrative essay
Vocabulary: word families, prefixes, suffixes, context clues
Punctuation: colon, semicolon, dash — function and use
Oral: short prepared Afrikaans talk on a personal experience

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Transactional and informational texts
topics: Read Afrikaans formal texts: letters, notices, reports, advertisements
Passive voice in Afrikaans — formation and use
Modal verbs: extended use in conditional sentences
Write a formal Afrikaans letter or email
Write a short Afrikaans report or informational paragraph
Vocabulary: synonyms, antonyms, homonyms in Afrikaans
Concord: subject-verb agreement in complex Afrikaans sentences
Oral: describe and explain a process in Afrikaans

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Argumentative and visual texts
topics: Read Afrikaans argumentative and persuasive texts — identify claim, evidence, tone
Visual texts: advertisement, cartoon — composition, purpose, target audience
Active and passive voice: convert between forms
Relative clauses: wat, wie, wie se in complex sentences
Write a short Afrikaans argumentative paragraph
Identify figurative language: vergelyking, metafoor, personifikasie, hiperbool
Revision of all tenses covered in Grades 7–8
Oral: argue a point of view in Afrikaans

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Poetry, revision and examination preparation
topics: Read Afrikaans poems: identify stanza, rhyme, rhythm, mood, tone, figurative language
Compare two short Afrikaans poems
Revision of all grammar: nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, pronouns, tenses
Revision of direct and indirect speech — all tenses
Write a short Afrikaans poem or creative descriptive paragraph
Comprehension strategies: skim, scan, close reading
Oral: recite and interpret an Afrikaans poem
Examination preparation: time management and answering techniques

skillChips: Read Afrikaans texts with critical understanding
Use passive voice in Afrikaans
Write complex Afrikaans sentences with subordinate clauses
Write a formal Afrikaans letter or report
Identify Afrikaans figurative language and explain its effect
Write a multi-paragraph Afrikaans essay
Convert between active and passive voice
Compare two Afrikaans poems
Use modal verbs in conditional sentences
Summarise and paraphrase Afrikaans texts

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Build vocabulary systematically. Five Afrikaans words daily. By the end of Grade 8 you will have added 800+ words to your vocabulary.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Formal letter format is always tested. Adres, datum, aanhef, liggaam, afsluiting. Learn it and use it every time.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Use the passive voice to vary your writing. Die brief is deur Jan geskryf. This adds variety and sophistication.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Figurative language: name it, quote it, explain it. Never just say 'there is a metaphor'. Quote it, name it, explain the effect.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Use conjunctions to build complex sentences. omdat, alhoewel, terwyl, tensy, sodat — these connect ideas and lift your writing grade.

subjects.hubDescription: Extended paragraphs, argumentative writing, passive voice and poetry.

subjects.title: Grade 8 Afrikaans Home Language | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Afrikaans Home Language for Grade 8. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Graad 8 Afrikaans Huistaal vereis 'n hoër vlak van kritiese betrokkenheid by taal en letterkunde. Leerders werk met meer veeleisende prosa, poësie en drama, en produseer uitgebreide formele en kreatiewe skryfwerk. Grammatika word meer gesofistikeerd, en begripswerk vereis inferensie, evaluering en kritiese lees op 'n vlak wat vooruitberei vir Graad 9.

expectItems.label: Sleutelverskuiwing
expectItems.value: Kritiese analise · uitgebreide opstel · taal vir effek

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Prosa en gevorderde tyd/stem
topics: Lees 'n prosateks — analiseer verteller, karakterontwikkeling, konflik, tema
Identifiseer en verduidelik literêre middele: ironie, aankondiging, simbool, terugflits
Voltooide en voltooide voortgaande tye — vorming en gebruik
Bedryfssin en lydende sin — uitgebreide toepassing in eie skryfwerk
Indirekte rede: alle tye insluitend voltooide vorme
Opstelskryfwerk: analitiese paragraafstruktuur — PEEL
Woordeskat: konnotasie, denotasie, register, toon
Mondeling: voorbereide toespraak of monoloog

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Poësie: kritiese analise
topics: Analiseer gedigte krities — beelding, woordkeuse, toon, stemming, tema, struktuur, vorm
Vergelyk twee gedigte oor 'n soortgelyke tema
Reëloorloop, pouse — hoe hulle pas en betekenis beïnvloed
Stylfiguurhersiening + uitgebrei: oksimoron, paradoks, ironie, eufemisme
Formele brief en e-posskrif — register en toon
Bysinne van tyd, rede, voorwaarde, kontras, doel
Sinverskeidenheid: kort sinne vir klem, komplekse sinne vir besonderhede
Mondeling: gedigopsê met uitdrukking, pas en interpretasie

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Drama en transaksionele skryfwerk
topics: Lees 'n dramateks: analiseer karaktermotivering, konflik, dramatiese ironie, tema
Toneelrigtings en hul narratiewe funksie
Transaksionele skryfwerk: notule, agenda, verslag, formele e-pos, CV (basies)
Kenmerke, formaat en register van elke transaksionele tekssoort
Nominale bysinne: dat-, wh- en of-sinne as onderwerpe en voorwerpe
Kongruensie: onderwerp-werkwoordooreenstemming in komplekse sinne
Voorsetsels van plek, tyd en rigting — korrekte gebruik
Mondeling: debat, formele bespreking of drama-toneel-uitvoering

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Visuele tekste, mediavaardighede en hersiening
topics: Visuele en mediateksanalise: filmplakkaat, infografika, spotprent, nuusartikel
Identifiseer doel, gehoor, vooroordeel, standpunt in mediatekste
Beskrywende en narratiewe opstelskryfwerk — beplanning en konsep
Argumenterende opstel: tesis, teenargument, weerlegging
Hersiening van grammatika: alle tye, stem, rede, kongruensie, bysinne
Begripshersiening: ongesiene prosa, poësie en visuele tekste
Leestekens: hakies, em-streep, ellips — effek en gebruik
Mondeling: formele aanbieding met visuele ondersteuning

skillChips: Analiseer prosa vir literêre middele en tema
Vergelyk twee gedigte met teksgetuienis
Skryf PEEL analitiese paragrawe
Skakel rede om oor alle tye
Pas kongruensie in komplekse sinne toe
Produseer formele transaksionele tekste
Analiseer mediatekste vir vooroordeel en doel
Skryf argumenterende en beskrywende opstelle
Gebruik bysinne korrek
Identifiseer en verduidelik oksimoron, paradoks, ironie
Analiseer drama vir karakter en konflik
Pas leestekens vir effek toe

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: PEEL elke analitiese paragraaf. Punt → Bewys (aanhaling) → Verduidelik die effek → Skakel terug na tema.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Merktoekenning sê hoeveel om te skryf. 2 punte = 2 merke. Skryf nooit een sin vir 'n meermerkvraag nie.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Vergelyk gedigte met konnektiefwoorde. Gebruik: 'Op dieselfde wyse...', 'In teenstelling...', 'Beide digters...'. Dit hef 'n vergelyking van opsomming na analise.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Leer transaksionele teksformate uit die kop. Notule, formele e-pos, CV — elk het 'n vaste formaat. Leer dit eenmalig.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Beplan opstelle voor jy skryf. 5 minute se beplanning = 'n beter gestruktureerde, hoër-puntetelling opstel elke keer.

subjects.hubDescription: Kritiese analise, PEEL opstelle, drama, poësievergelyking en mediavaardighede.

subjects.title: Grade 8 Creative Arts | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Creative Arts for Grade 8. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 8 Creative Arts builds on Grade 7 foundations and develops greater technical skill and creative independence across Visual Arts, Music, Drama and Dance. Learners are expected to show more sophisticated understanding of art techniques and cultural contexts, produce more refined practical work, and develop their ability to critically analyse and respond to art forms from South Africa and the world.

expectItems.label: Art forms
expectItems.value: Visual Arts · Music · Drama · Dance (2 selected)

expectItems.label: Key focus
expectItems.value: Technical refinement · critical analysis · cultural contexts

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Advanced Visual Art and Music
topics: Visual Art: principles of design — balance, contrast, emphasis, movement, pattern, unity
