Perspective drawing: one-point and two-point perspective
Mixed media: combining drawing, painting and collage in a single work
Visual Art practical: observational drawing or still life in colour
Music: intervals — major and minor, perfect intervals; key signatures
Music notation: bass clef, ledger lines, dotted notes, ties and slurs
Music practical: sight-reading exercises and ensemble performance
Art appreciation: formal analysis of a South African artwork — elements and principles

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Drama and Dance: performance skills
topics: Drama: Stanislavski method — given circumstances, objectives, actions, emotion memory
Ensemble work: playing status, listening, responding truthfully on stage
Script analysis: subtext, dramatic arc, character relationships
Drama practical: perform a scene from a prescribed or devised script
Dance: Laban Movement Analysis — body, effort, space, shape
Contemporary dance: floor work, partnering, levels and spatial awareness
Dance practical: perform a structured contemporary or African dance piece
Critical response: write a review of a live or recorded performance

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Art forms in South African context
topics: Visual Art: South African art history — colonial art, protest art, post-apartheid art
Artists: William Kentridge, Irma Stern, Gerard Sekoto, Zanele Muholi — context and technique
Music: South African music genres — marabi, mbaqanga, bubblegum, hip hop — history and features
Music composition: 16-bar composition using call-and-response structure
Drama: South African theatre — Market Theatre, protest theatre, community theatre
Dance: South African popular dance forms — pantsula, gumboot, gwara gwara — context and performance
Comparative analysis: compare two South African artworks or performances
Create a work inspired by a South African artist or tradition

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Performance, critique and showcase
topics: Visual Art: produce a portfolio piece demonstrating growth across the year
Music: full ensemble performance — two contrasting pieces
Drama: full scripted performance with blocking, characterisation and staging
Dance: full choreographed group performance for audience
Arts showcase: present best work across all four art forms
Formal art critique: write a structured analysis of your own work
Peer assessment: give and receive constructive feedback
Reflect on personal development as a creative artist in Grade 8

skillChips: Apply principles of design in visual artworks
Draw using one- and two-point perspective
Read music notation including bass clef
Perform music in an ensemble
Apply Stanislavski method in drama
Perform a scripted scene with character and intention
Apply Laban Movement Analysis in dance
Perform a structured dance piece
Analyse South African artworks in context
Write a formal art critique

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 3v5M12 16v5M3 12h5M16 12h5M6 6l3 3M15 15l3 3M18 6l-3 3M9 15l-3 3"/></svg>
tips.text: Learn the principles of design. Balance, contrast, emphasis, movement, pattern, unity. Know all six and apply them when analysing or creating work.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Art criticism follows a structure. Describe → Analyse (elements/principles) → Interpret (meaning/mood) → Evaluate (success). Use this every time.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 3v5M12 16v5M3 12h5M16 12h5M6 6l3 3M15 15l3 3M18 6l-3 3M9 15l-3 3"/></svg>
tips.text: Commit fully to character. In drama and dance, marks are lost through hesitation. Commit to every choice you make on stage.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M3 12h18M12 3c2.5 2.5 3.8 5.6 3.8 9s-1.3 6.5-3.8 9c-2.5-2.5-3.8-5.6-3.8-9S9.5 5.5 12 3z"/></svg>
tips.text: Know your SA artists. Kentridge, Sekoto, Muholi — know their context, techniques and why their work matters. This comes up in tests.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Portfolio pieces should show process. Keep sketches, drafts and planning. Teachers assess your thinking process, not just the final product.

subjects.hubDescription: Advanced Visual Art, Music, Drama and Dance — SA art history and performance.

subjects.title: Grade 8 Economic Management and Science | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Economic Management and Science for Grade 8. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 8 EMS builds on the Grade 7 foundations of economy, financial literacy and entrepreneurship. Learners extend their bookkeeping skills to include more financial records, deepen their understanding of business structures and the South African economy, and develop more sophisticated entrepreneurial thinking. Financial literacy is extended to include interest calculations, credit and banking in more depth.

expectItems.label: Key concepts
expectItems.value: Interest · business structures · extended bookkeeping · business plan

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: The economy: production and markets
topics: Revision of circular flow — extend to include government and foreign sector
Markets: product market and factor market — how they work
Demand and supply: the law of demand and supply, equilibrium price
Price determination: surplus and shortage — what happens to price
Market structures: perfect competition, monopoly, oligopoly (introduction)
Economic systems: market economy, planned economy, mixed economy — SA context
The role of the Reserve Bank: monetary policy, interest rates, inflation
Gross Domestic Product (GDP): what it measures and why it matters

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Financial literacy: interest and credit
topics: Simple interest: formula, calculate interest earned or paid — I = P × R × T
Compound interest: compare with simple interest, effect of time
Credit: definition, types (hire purchase, credit card, mortgage, overdraft)
Advantages and disadvantages of credit — responsible use
Cost of credit: total cost including interest over the full term
Financial statements: income statement — revenue, expenses, profit/loss
The balance sheet: assets, liabilities, equity — basic layout
Break-even analysis: fixed costs, variable costs, break-even point

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Extended bookkeeping
topics: The accounting equation revision — applied to transactions
Journals: cash receipts journal (CRJ) and cash payments journal (CPJ) — extended
Debtors ledger: individual debtor accounts — record, balance
Creditors ledger: individual creditor accounts — record, balance
General ledger: transfer from journals to ledger accounts
Trial balance: purpose, preparation from ledger balances
Petty cash: imprest system, petty cash vouchers, reimbursement
VAT: concept, VAT-inclusive and VAT-exclusive calculations at 15%

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Entrepreneurship and the South African economy
topics: Business ownership: sole trader, partnership, private company (Pty Ltd), public company
Advantages and disadvantages of each business form
The role of SMMEs in job creation and economic growth in SA
Formal vs informal sector: differences, challenges, opportunities
Business plan: full plan including market research, SWOT analysis, financial projections
Marketing: extended 4Ps + 2Ps (people, process)
Ethics in business: corporate social responsibility, environmental impact
South Africa's economic challenges: unemployment, inequality, poverty — GINI coefficient

skillChips: Explain demand, supply and equilibrium price
Describe the role of the Reserve Bank
Calculate simple and compound interest
Explain different types of credit and their costs
Prepare an income statement
Record transactions in CRJ and CPJ
Prepare individual debtor and creditor accounts
Extract a trial balance from ledger accounts
Calculate VAT-inclusive and exclusive amounts
Describe types of business ownership
Analyse a SWOT for a business
Apply the extended marketing mix

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="2" y="5" width="20" height="14" rx="2"/><path d="M2 10h20"/></svg>
tips.text: Simple interest: I = P × R × T. Principal × Rate × Time. The rate must be in decimal form (15% = 0.15). This is the most tested formula in EMS.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="m3 16 6-6 4 4 8-9"/><path d="M15 5h6v6"/></svg>
tips.text: Double-check that the trial balance balances. Debit total = Credit total. If it does not, find your error before moving on.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Know the difference between assets and liabilities. Assets = what the business owns. Liabilities = what it owes. Equity = what belongs to the owner.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M3 12h18M12 3c2.5 2.5 3.8 5.6 3.8 9s-1.3 6.5-3.8 9c-2.5-2.5-3.8-5.6-3.8-9S9.5 5.5 12 3z"/></svg>
tips.text: Connect EMS to current SA news. Interest rate changes, GDP figures and unemployment statistics all appear in EMS tests. Read the news.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: A business plan follows a fixed structure. Vision → Mission → Product → Market → SWOT → Financials. Know all sections.

subjects.hubDescription: Interest, credit, extended bookkeeping, VAT and business structures.

subjects.title: Grade 8 English First Additional Language | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned English First Additional Language for Grade 8. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 8 English FAL extends the functional English literacy of Grade 7. Learners read more complex texts across a range of genres, write multi-paragraph texts including argumentative and transactional writing, and handle more advanced grammar. The focus is on developing clear, accurate communication in English across different contexts and registers.

expectItems.label: Key progression
expectItems.value: Extended paragraphs · argumentative writing · literary texts

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Narrative and descriptive texts
topics: Read narrative and descriptive texts — literal, inferential, evaluative questions
Complex sentences: subordinate clauses of time, reason, condition
Revision of direct and indirect speech — extend to past tense reporting
Degrees of comparison: revision with irregular forms
Write a multi-paragraph narrative essay
Vocabulary: word families, prefixes, suffixes, context clues
Punctuation: colon, semicolon, dash — function and use
Oral: short prepared talk on a personal experience

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Transactional and informational texts
topics: Read formal texts: letters, notices, reports, advertisements
Passive voice — formation and use
Modal verbs: extended use in conditional sentences
Write a formal letter or email
Write a short report or informational paragraph
Vocabulary: synonyms, antonyms, homonyms
Concord: subject-verb agreement in complex sentences
Oral: describe and explain a process clearly

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Argumentative and visual texts
topics: Read argumentative and persuasive texts — identify claim, evidence, tone
Visual texts: advertisement, cartoon — composition, purpose, target audience
Active and passive voice: convert between forms
Relative clauses: who, which, that in complex sentences
Write a short argumentative paragraph
Identify figurative language: simile, metaphor, personification, hyperbole
Revision of all tenses covered in Grades 7–8
Oral: argue a point of view confidently

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Poetry, revision and examination preparation
topics: Read poems: identify stanza, rhyme, rhythm, mood, tone, figurative language
Compare two short poems
Revision of all grammar: parts of speech, tenses, speech, voice, concord
Write a short poem or creative paragraph
Comprehension strategies: skim, scan, close reading
Oral: recite and interpret a poem
Examination preparation: time management and answering techniques
Review and consolidate all writing formats covered

skillChips: Read texts critically at Grade 8 level
Use passive voice correctly
Write complex sentences with subordinate clauses
Write a formal letter or report
Identify figurative language and explain its effect
Write a multi-paragraph essay
Convert between active and passive voice
Compare two poems using evidence
Use modal verbs in conditional sentences
Summarise and paraphrase texts accurately

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Build vocabulary every day. Five words daily = 800+ new words by end of Grade 8.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Formal letter format must be memorised. Address, date, salutation, body, closing. Learn it and never lose those format marks.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Figurative language: name, quote, explain. Never just say 'there is a simile'. Quote it, name it, explain the effect on the reader.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Use the passive voice to vary your writing. 'The letter was written by John' adds variety. Examiners reward sentence variety.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Argumentative writing needs a clear thesis. Your first paragraph must state your position clearly. Everything else supports it.

subjects.hubDescription: Extended paragraphs, argumentative writing, passive voice and poetry.

subjects.title: Grade 8 English Home Language | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned English Home Language for Grade 8. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 8 English Home Language extends literary and language skills to a higher level of critical engagement. Learners work with more demanding prose, poetry and drama texts and produce extended formal and creative writing. Grammar becomes more sophisticated, comprehension requires inference, evaluation and critical reading, and learners develop the ability to analyse language for effect across a range of text types.

expectItems.label: Key shift
expectItems.value: Critical analysis · extended essay · language for effect

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Prose and advanced tense/voice
topics: Read a prose text — analyse narrator, character development, conflict, theme
Identify and explain literary devices: irony, foreshadowing, symbolism, flashback
Perfect and perfect progressive tenses — formation and use
Active and passive voice — extended application in own writing
Reported speech: all tenses including perfect forms
Essay writing: analytical paragraph structure — PEEL (Point, Evidence, Explain, Link)
Vocabulary: connotation, denotation, register, tone
Oral: prepared speech or podcast-style monologue

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Poetry: critical analysis
topics: Analyse poems critically — imagery, diction, tone, mood, theme, structure, form
Compare two poems on a similar theme
Enjambment, caesura, run-on lines — how they affect pace and meaning
Figures of speech revision + extended: oxymoron, paradox, irony, euphemism
Formal letter and email writing — register and tone
Adverbial clauses: time, reason, condition, contrast, purpose
Sentence variety: short sentences for emphasis, complex sentences for detail
Oral: poetry recital with expression, pace and interpretation

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Drama and transactional writing
topics: Read a drama text: analyse character motivation, conflict, dramatic irony, theme
Stage directions and their narrative function
Transactional writing: minutes, agenda, report, formal email, CV (basic)
Features, format and register of each transactional text type
Nominal clauses: that-, wh- and whether/if-clauses as subjects and objects
Concord: subject-verb agreement in complex sentences
Prepositions of place, time and direction — accurate use
Oral: debate, formal discussion or drama scene performance

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Visual texts, media literacy and revision
topics: Visual and media text analysis: film poster, infographic, cartoon, news article
Identify purpose, audience, bias, viewpoint in media texts
Descriptive and narrative essay writing — planning and drafting
Argumentative/discursive essay: thesis, counter-argument, rebuttal
Revision of grammar: all tenses, voice, speech, concord, clauses
Comprehension revision: unseen prose, poetry and visual texts
Punctuation: parentheses, em dash, ellipsis — effect and use
Oral: formal presentation with visual support

skillChips: Analyse prose for literary devices and theme
Compare two poems using textual evidence
Write PEEL analytical paragraphs
Convert speech across all tenses
Apply concord in complex sentences
Produce formal transactional texts
Analyse media texts for bias and purpose
Write argumentative and descriptive essays
Use adverbial and nominal clauses
Identify and explain oxymoron, paradox, irony
Analyse drama for character and conflict
Apply punctuation for effect

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: PEEL every analytical paragraph. Point → Evidence (quote) → Explain the effect → Link back to theme. Use this for prose, poetry and drama.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Mark allocation tells you how much to write. 2 marks = 2 points. 4 marks = 4 points or 2 well-developed points. Never give one sentence for multi-mark questions.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Compare poems using connectives. Use: 'Similarly...', 'In contrast...', 'Both poets...', 'While Poem A...'. This lifts a comparison from listing to analysing.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Learn transactional text formats cold. CV, minutes, formal email — each has a fixed format. Learn them once, apply them every time.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Plan essays before writing. 5 minutes of planning = a more structured, higher-scoring essay every time.

subjects.hubDescription: Critical analysis, PEEL essays, drama, poetry comparison and media literacy.

subjects.title: Grade 8 Life Orientation | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Life Orientation for Grade 8. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 8 Life Orientation deepens the self-awareness, social responsibility and physical literacy developed in Grade 7. The CAPS curriculum addresses adolescent identity, relationships, rights, career development and physical education at a more mature level, helping learners navigate the social and personal challenges of the Senior Phase with confidence and resilience.

expectItems.label: Five areas
expectItems.value: Self · Rights · Life Skills · PE · Career

expectItems.label: Key focus
expectItems.value: Identity · relationships · rights in practice · career exploration

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Identity and wellbeing
topics: Personal identity: self-concept, self-esteem, self-efficacy — how they develop
Influences on identity: family, culture, religion, media, peer groups
Body image: media influence, healthy vs unhealthy body image, eating disorders (awareness)
Stress: causes, physical and emotional effects, management strategies
Physical Education: aerobic fitness — continuous training, interval training
Fitness testing: measure improvements since Grade 7 baseline
Study skills: note-taking methods, mind maps, summarising
Goal review: assess progress on Grade 7 SMART goals; set new Grade 8 goals

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Rights and social justice
topics: The Constitution: Chapter 2 Bill of Rights — focus on sections most relevant to learners
Equality: racial, gender and disability equality in SA — progress and challenges
Gender-based violence: statistics in SA, causes, prevention, support systems
Online rights and responsibilities: cyberbullying, digital privacy, screen time
Social media: benefits, risks, responsible use
The justice system: how it works, rights of the accused, restorative justice
Community engagement: how learners can contribute to social change
Physical Education: team sports — tactics, positions, rules, fair play

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Relationships and decision-making
topics: Healthy relationships: qualities, boundaries, communication, mutual respect
Romantic relationships in adolescence: consent, age-appropriateness, pressure
Sexual health: puberty revision, reproductive health, STI awareness (age-appropriate)
Substance abuse: extended — gateway drugs, addiction cycle, rehabilitation
Problem-solving: identify problem, generate solutions, evaluate, implement, review
Conflict resolution: communication strategies, mediation, win-win solutions
Physical Education: individual sport or outdoor challenge
Mental health: recognising depression and anxiety, seeking help, reducing stigma

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Careers and future planning
topics: Career clusters: investigative, artistic, social, enterprising, conventional, realistic
Personality types and career fit: Holland Codes introduction
South Africa's labour market: growth sectors, skills shortages, future of work
Education pathways: matric, gap year, FET college, university — what each requires
Bursaries and financial aid in SA: NSFAS, Funza Lushaka, corporate bursaries
Physical Education: indigenous games, recreational activities, reflection on fitness journey
Entrepreneurship as a career: case studies of young SA entrepreneurs
Personal development plan: skills, experiences, goals for Grade 9 and beyond

skillChips: Describe self-concept, self-esteem and self-efficacy
Apply stress management strategies
Explain key sections of the Bill of Rights
Identify and respond to GBV
Use a structured problem-solving framework
Explain the addiction cycle
Apply conflict resolution strategies
Describe career clusters and personality types
Identify SA education pathways and bursaries
Demonstrate sport-specific and fitness skills
Explain healthy and unhealthy relationship signs
Recognise signs of depression and anxiety

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8.5"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="4.8"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="1.1" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/></svg>
tips.text: Learn specific Bill of Rights sections. Sections 9, 10, 12, 14, 16, 28 — know the section numbers and what rights they protect.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Use SA statistics in answers. LO examiners reward specific SA data. Know approximate GBV, unemployment and inequality statistics.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8.5"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="4.8"/><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="1.1" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/></svg>
tips.text: PE is a practical assessment. Attend every lesson, demonstrate correct technique and participate fully. These are your marks.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Career planning starts now. Grade 8 is not too early to explore what excites you. Use the career cluster framework to narrow your thinking.

subjects.hubDescription: Identity, relationships, rights, substance abuse, career exploration.

subjects.title: Grade 8 Mathematics | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Mathematics for Grade 8. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 8 Mathematics extends the algebraic and geometric foundations of Grade 7. Learners develop fluency with linear equations, algebraic expressions and functions, and geometry is formalised with proofs about triangles and quadrilaterals. The number system expands to include irrational numbers and the concept of real numbers. Grade 8 Maths is critical — the algebraic and geometric thinking built here is directly required in Grade 10 Maths.

expectItems.label: Key concepts
expectItems.value: Linear equations · functions · congruency · theorem of Pythagoras

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Real numbers and algebraic expressions
topics: Real numbers: rational and irrational numbers — classify, order, represent on number line
Surds: simplify square roots and cube roots — rational vs irrational
Exponential laws: aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ, aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ, (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ, a⁰ = 1
Scientific notation: write large and small numbers, multiply and divide
Algebraic expressions: expand brackets — distributive law
Factorise: common factor, difference of two squares, trinomials (basic)
Add, subtract and multiply algebraic expressions
Simplify fractions with monomial denominators

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Linear equations, inequalities and functions
topics: Solve linear equations: one variable, with brackets, fractions
Solve linear inequalities: represent solution on number line
Simultaneous equations: solve by substitution
Functions: input-output, tables of values, Cartesian plane
Graph y = mx + c: gradient and y-intercept
Interpret gradient: positive, negative, zero, undefined
Graph y = ax²: shape, turning point, axis of symmetry
Direct and inverse proportion: graphs and equations

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Geometry: triangles and quadrilaterals
topics: Angle sum of a triangle: proof and application
Types of triangles: equilateral, isosceles, scalene — properties
Congruent triangles: four conditions — SSS, SAS, AAS, RHS
Similar triangles: AA condition — scale factor, proportional sides
Properties of quadrilaterals: parallelogram, rectangle, rhombus, square, trapezium, kite
Midpoint theorem: statement, proof and application
The Theorem of Pythagoras: proof, application, converse
Trigonometry introduction: sin, cos, tan ratios in right-angled triangles

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Measurement, data and revision
topics: Area and perimeter of composite shapes including circles
Volume and surface area of cylinders, triangular prisms, rectangular prisms
Circles: area, circumference, arc length, area of sector
Data: frequency tables, grouped data
Histograms and frequency polygons
Cumulative frequency: ogive (cumulative frequency curve)
Measures of central tendency: mean, median, mode from grouped data
Scatter plots: draw, identify trend, line of best fit

skillChips: Classify and work with real and irrational numbers
Apply exponential laws
Write numbers in scientific notation
Factorise algebraic expressions
Solve linear equations and inequalities
Solve simultaneous equations by substitution
Draw and interpret y = mx + c graphs
Prove and apply triangle congruency conditions
Apply the Theorem of Pythagoras
Calculate sin, cos, tan ratios
Calculate volume and surface area of prisms and cylinders
Draw and interpret ogives and scatter plots

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="4.5" y="2.5" width="15" height="19" rx="2"/><path d="M8 6.5h8"/><path d="M8 11h.01M12 11h.01M16 11h.01M8 15h.01M12 15h.01M16 15h.01M8 19h.01M12 19h.01M16 19h.01"/></svg>
tips.text: Factorise before you simplify. Always look for a common factor first. Then check for difference of two squares. Then trinomial.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Show every step when solving equations. Method marks are allocated at every step. Even a wrong answer can score marks with correct working.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: For geometry: state the reason. Every statement in a geometry proof needs a reason in brackets. 'angles of a triangle = 180°' is a reason.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="4.5" y="2.5" width="15" height="19" rx="2"/><path d="M8 6.5h8"/><path d="M8 11h.01M12 11h.01M16 11h.01M8 15h.01M12 15h.01M16 15h.01M8 19h.01M12 19h.01M16 19h.01"/></svg>
tips.text: Pythagoras: square, add/subtract, root. c² = a² + b². Write the formula, substitute, calculate, take the square root. Every time.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Functions need a table of values first. Before drawing any graph, calculate at least 3 points. Sketch then refine.

subjects.hubDescription: Real numbers, algebra, functions, congruency, Pythagoras and data.

subjects.title: Grade 8 Natural Science | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Natural Science for Grade 8. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 8 Natural Science extends the four knowledge strands with more sophisticated content. Learners study cell biology, chemical reactions and the periodic table, mechanics and waves, and Earth's place in the solar system. They are expected to plan and conduct independent investigations, interpret data critically, and write formal scientific reports. Grade 8 Natural Science directly prepares learners for Physical Sciences and Life Sciences in the FET Phase.

expectItems.label: Four strands
expectItems.value: Life & Living · Matter & Materials · Energy & Change · Planet Earth

expectItems.label: Key shift
expectItems.value: Cell biology · periodic table · mechanics · formal scientific reports

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Life and living: cells and body systems
topics: Cell theory: all living things are made of cells, cells come from cells
Animal and plant cell structure: organelles and functions — nucleus, mitochondria, chloroplast, cell wall, vacuole
Unicellular vs multicellular organisms: examples and comparison
Cell division: mitosis — overview, importance for growth and repair
The circulatory system: heart structure, blood vessels, blood components and functions
The respiratory system: organs, mechanism of breathing, gas exchange in alveoli
Interaction between circulatory and respiratory systems
Investigation: observe and draw cells using a microscope (or diagrams)

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Matter and materials: atoms and the periodic table
topics: The atom: protons, neutrons, electrons — atomic number, mass number
Elements: definition, symbols, first 20 elements of the periodic table
The periodic table: periods, groups, metals and non-metals, atomic number order
Compounds: definition, molecular formula, name from formula
Chemical formulae: H₂O, CO₂, NaCl, O₂ — what they mean
Physical properties of matter: melting point, boiling point, density, solubility
States of matter: particle model — solid, liquid, gas
Changes of state: melting, freezing, evaporation, condensation, sublimation

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Energy: mechanics and waves
topics: Speed: distance ÷ time — calculate and apply
Velocity and acceleration: introduction — vector vs scalar
Forces: revision + Newton's First and Second Laws
Momentum: p = mv — calculate and apply
Work: W = F × d — calculate
Energy: gravitational potential energy (GPE) and kinetic energy (KE) — calculate
Waves: transverse and longitudinal waves — parts, wavelength, frequency, amplitude
The electromagnetic spectrum: uses of each region in everyday life

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Planet Earth: solar system and space
topics: Earth's place in the solar system: distances, sizes, orbital periods
The Moon: formation theory, surface features, Apollo missions
Tides: gravitational pull of Moon and Sun — spring and neap tides
Eclipses: solar and lunar eclipses — conditions and explanation
Comets, asteroids, meteors, meteorites — features and differences
Stars: life cycle — nebula, main sequence, red giant, white dwarf, supernova, neutron star/black hole
Galaxies: the Milky Way, types of galaxies, scale of the universe
Space exploration: SA's role — SANSA, MeerKAT radio telescope

skillChips: Describe cell structure and the function of organelles
Explain cell division by mitosis
Describe the circulatory and respiratory systems
Use the periodic table to identify elements
Write and interpret chemical formulae
Describe properties of matter and changes of state
Calculate speed, momentum and work done
Apply Newton's First and Second Laws
Describe transverse and longitudinal waves
Identify regions of the electromagnetic spectrum
Describe the solar system and moon phases
Explain the life cycle of a star

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M9 2h6M10 2v6.5L4.5 18a2 2 0 0 0 1.7 3h11.6a2 2 0 0 0 1.7-3L14 8.5V2"/><path d="M7.5 14.5h9"/></svg>
tips.text: Learn the cell organelles and their functions. Nucleus, mitochondria, chloroplast, cell membrane, cell wall, vacuole, ribosomes — know each one's job cold.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Write chemical formulae correctly. H₂O not H2O. Subscripts matter. The formula tells you exactly how many of each atom.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 2 4 14h6l-1 8 9-12h-6l1-8z"/></svg>
tips.text: Know the three mechanics formulae. Speed = d ÷ t. Momentum = m × v. Work = F × d. These appear in every Grade 8 test.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M3 12h18M12 3c2.5 2.5 3.8 5.6 3.8 9s-1.3 6.5-3.8 9c-2.5-2.5-3.8-5.6-3.8-9S9.5 5.5 12 3z"/></svg>
tips.text: The periodic table is not optional. Learn the first 20 elements by name and symbol. Rows are periods, columns are groups.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M9 2h6M10 2v6.5L4.5 18a2 2 0 0 0 1.7 3h11.6a2 2 0 0 0 1.7-3L14 8.5V2"/><path d="M7.5 14.5h9"/></svg>
tips.text: Newton's Laws in plain English. 1st: objects stay as they are unless a force acts. 2nd: F = ma. Apply both in word problems.

subjects.hubDescription: Cell biology, the periodic table, mechanics, waves and space.

subjects.title: Grade 8 Social Science | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Social Science for Grade 8. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 8 Social Science extends historical and geographical knowledge to the period of European expansion and colonialism, and develops deeper geographical analysis of world environments. The History component covers the Renaissance, Reformation, colonialism and the slave trade in depth. The Geography component examines global climate, world biomes, weather systems and South Africa's environments in a global context, with an emphasis on environmental sustainability.

expectItems.label: Key skills
expectItems.value: Source analysis · comparative geography · structured essays

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: History: the Renaissance and Reformation
topics: The Renaissance: meaning, origins in Italy, key ideas — humanism, individualism
Renaissance art and science: Da Vinci, Michelangelo, Galileo, Copernicus
The printing press: Gutenberg, impact on the spread of ideas and literacy
The Protestant Reformation: causes — corruption in the Catholic Church
Martin Luther: the 95 Theses, key beliefs, impact on Europe
John Calvin and Calvinism: predestination, the elect, spread to Geneva
The Counter-Reformation: Council of Trent, Jesuit order
Impact of the Reformation on European society, politics and religious conflict

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Geography: global climate and world environments
topics: Factors affecting climate: latitude, altitude, distance from sea, ocean currents, prevailing winds
World climate zones: tropical, subtropical, arid, temperate, cold, polar
Climate graphs: draw, read and interpret temperature and rainfall data
Biomes and climate: rainforest, desert, grassland, Mediterranean, taiga, tundra
Ocean currents: warm and cold currents — effect on coastal climates
El Niño and La Niña: causes, effects on world and SA climate
Climate change: greenhouse effect, global warming, IPCC evidence
Environmental sustainability: carbon footprint, Paris Agreement, SA commitments

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: History: colonialism and the slave trade
topics: European colonialism: motives — God, gold and glory
Portuguese and Spanish colonialism in Africa and the Americas
Impact of colonialism on indigenous peoples: land, culture, population
The Transatlantic slave trade: routes, scale, conditions
Life of enslaved people in the Americas: resistance, culture, identity
Abolition: William Wilberforce, Toussaint L'Ouverture, role of enslaved people
Legacy of slavery: racism, reparations, Black Lives Matter — connecting past to present
Sources and perspectives: hearing African and enslaved voices in history

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Geography: South Africa's environments
topics: South Africa's drainage basins: Orange-Vaal system, Limpopo, coastal rivers
Dams and water management in SA: Lesotho Highlands Water Project, water crisis
South Africa's soils: types, distribution, land capability
Soil erosion: causes, types (sheet, rill, gully), conservation methods
Mining and the environment in SA: gold, platinum, coal — environmental costs
Land use in SA: commercial farming, subsistence farming, conservation
Urbanisation and the environment: informal settlements, pollution, service delivery
Writing a structured geographical response using maps, statistics and evidence

skillChips: Describe the Renaissance and its key ideas
Explain causes and effects of the Protestant Reformation
Analyse sources from the Reformation period
Interpret climate graphs
Describe world climate zones and biomes
Explain factors affecting climate including ocean currents
Explain the causes and consequences of colonialism
Analyse the Transatlantic slave trade using multiple perspectives
Describe South Africa's drainage basins
Explain soil erosion causes and conservation
Describe SA's land use and environmental challenges
Write structured historical and geographical responses

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M3 12h18M12 3c2.5 2.5 3.8 5.6 3.8 9s-1.3 6.5-3.8 9c-2.5-2.5-3.8-5.6-3.8-9S9.5 5.5 12 3z"/></svg>
tips.text: Climate graphs: read temperature as a line, rainfall as bars. Temperature peaks in summer. Rainfall peaks vary by climate zone. Learn to describe the pattern.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: History: causes AND effects. Most history questions ask about either causes or consequences or both. Always address what the question actually asks.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Structure: PEEL works in Social Science too. Point → Evidence → Explain → Link. Use it for history analysis and geographical responses.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M3 12h18M12 3c2.5 2.5 3.8 5.6 3.8 9s-1.3 6.5-3.8 9c-2.5-2.5-3.8-5.6-3.8-9S9.5 5.5 12 3z"/></svg>
tips.text: Know South Africa's environmental challenges. Water scarcity, soil erosion and mining pollution are all testable in Grade 8 geography.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="10.5" cy="10.5" r="7"/><path d="M20.5 20.5 15.8 15.8"/></svg>
tips.text: Primary sources need source analysis. Who wrote it? When? Why? What does it tell us? What does it leave out? Answer all five every time.

subjects.hubDescription: Renaissance, Reformation, colonialism, global climate and SA environments.

subjects.title: Grade 8 Technology | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Technology for Grade 8. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 8 Technology extends the Design Process skills of Grade 7 to more complex design challenges. Learners work with more sophisticated structures, mechanisms and systems, apply technical drawing skills with greater accuracy, and develop a deeper understanding of how technology impacts society and the environment. The focus on sustainability and responsible design becomes more prominent in Grade 8.

expectItems.label: Key focus
expectItems.value: Advanced mechanisms · sustainable design · technical drawing precision

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Structures: forces and materials
topics: Revision of structural forces: compression, tension, torsion, shear — extended examples
Beam and column structures: how they carry loads
Reinforced structures: how reinforcing materials improve strength
Properties of materials: revision + extended — elasticity, malleability, ductility
Material selection for design: match material properties to design requirements
Technical drawing: orthographic projection — revision and refinement
Tolerances and dimensions in technical drawings
Practical: design and build a structure to carry a specified load using minimal material

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Mechanisms: compound systems
topics: Compound gear trains: multiple gears, gear ratios, speed and direction changes
Belt and chain drives: how they work, mechanical advantage, examples
Rack and pinion: linear motion from rotary motion — car steering example
Screw thread: self-locking, mechanical advantage, applications
Combining mechanisms: design a system using two or more mechanisms
CAD introduction: computer-aided design — basic 2D drawing software
Exploded and assembly drawings — more complex examples
Practical: design and build a mechanism with compound gears or drives

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Systems, control and sustainability
topics: Electronic systems: input devices (sensors, switches), process (transistor, IC), output (LED, buzzer, motor)
Control systems: open-loop and closed-loop control
Feedback: what it is and why it makes control systems more effective
Programmable systems: flowcharts and pseudocode for simple programs
Sustainability: life cycle analysis of a product — cradle to grave
Environmental impact of manufacturing: pollution, waste, energy use
Green design principles: reduce, reuse, recycle in design decisions
Practical: design a system with an electronic control element

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Integrated design project and reflection
topics: Full design project: tackle an open-ended design challenge using all Design Process stages
Investigate: research the problem, interview users, analyse existing solutions
Design: produce annotated sketches, choose and justify best solution
Make: construct the solution using appropriate tools and materials
Evaluate: test against specification, identify successes and improvements
Communicate: produce a design portfolio — drawings, photographs, written report
Technology and society: ethical questions in technology design — who benefits?
Reflect on growth as a designer across Grade 8

skillChips: Describe and apply structural forces in design
Select materials based on their properties
Produce accurate orthographic drawings with dimensions
Calculate compound gear ratios
Describe belt drives, rack and pinion, screw thread
Design a compound mechanism
Identify input, process and output in electronic systems
Distinguish open-loop and closed-loop control
Apply life cycle analysis to a product
Apply green design principles
Complete all stages of the Design Process
Produce a design portfolio with drawings and evaluation

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M14.7 6.3a4 4 0 0 0-5.4 5.4L3 18l3 3 6.3-6.3a4 4 0 0 0 5.4-5.4l-2.8 2.8-2-2z"/></svg>
tips.text: Every design must meet the specification. Before making, write a clear specification. After making, test against it point by point. This is your evaluation.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="4.5" y="2.5" width="15" height="19" rx="2"/><path d="M8 6.5h8"/><path d="M8 11h.01M12 11h.01M16 11h.01M8 15h.01M12 15h.01M16 15h.01M8 19h.01M12 19h.01M16 19h.01"/></svg>
tips.text: Technical drawing accuracy earns marks. Use a ruler, compass and protractor correctly. Messy drawings lose marks even if the concept is correct.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="3.2"/><path d="M12 3v2.2M12 18.8V21M4.9 7.5l1.9 1.1M17.2 15.4l1.9 1.1M3 12h2.2M18.8 12H21M4.9 16.5l1.9-1.1M17.2 8.6l1.9-1.1M7.5 19.1l1.1-1.9M15.4 6.8l1.1-1.9M9.5 4.9l.6-2M14 4.9l-.6-2"/></svg>
tips.text: Gear ratio = driven ÷ driver. If the driver has 20 teeth and the driven has 40 teeth, the gear ratio is 2:1. The driven gear turns at half the speed.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M20 8a8 8 0 0 0-14.6-3.4M4 4v5h5"/><path d="M4 16a8 8 0 0 0 14.6 3.4M20 20v-5h-5"/></svg>
tips.text: Life cycle analysis: think from materials to disposal. Raw materials → manufacturing → use → disposal. Every stage has environmental costs. Know them.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: The best designs solve real human problems. Always start with the user. What do they need? What constraints exist? The best Grade 8 designs are human-centred.

subjects.hubDescription: Advanced mechanisms, electronic systems, sustainability and design portfolio.

subjects.title: Grade 9 Afrikaans First Additional Language | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Afrikaans First Additional Language for Grade 9. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 9 Afrikaans FAL is the final year of the Senior Phase and consolidates functional Afrikaans literacy at a level that prepares learners for the FET Phase. Learners write extended multi-paragraph texts, handle complex grammar, read literary and argumentative texts critically, and produce polished transactional writing. Grade 9 FAL demands independent, accurate use of Afrikaans across a wide range of contexts.

expectItems.label: Key progression
expectItems.value: Extended essays · literary texts · all grammar consolidated

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Narrative and literary texts
topics: Read Afrikaans narrative and literary texts — literal, inferential, evaluative and critical questions
Complex sentence structures: multiple subordinate clauses
All tenses revision: present, past, future, perfect, pluperfect
Direct and indirect speech: all tenses including perfect forms
Write a multi-paragraph Afrikaans narrative or descriptive essay
Vocabulary: register, connotation, context clues, word families
Figurative language: extended — uitgebreide metafoor, paradoks, ironie
Oral: prepared talk or debate in Afrikaans

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Argumentative and transactional texts
topics: Read Afrikaans argumentative texts — identify thesis, arguments, counter-arguments
Write a short Afrikaans argumentative essay with thesis and supporting points
Formal Afrikaans letter, email and report — revision and refinement
Passive voice: full revision — all tenses in passive form
Conditional sentences: all four types in Afrikaans
Concord: subject-verb agreement in complex Afrikaans sentences
Vocabulary extension: idioms and proverbs in Afrikaans
Oral: argue a position formally in Afrikaans

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Visual and informational texts
topics: Visual texts: advertisement, cartoon, infographic — analyse purpose, audience, technique
Afrikaans poetry: sustained analysis — imagery, tone, mood, theme, figurative language
Compare two Afrikaans poems in a structured written response
Relative clauses and nominal clauses — identify and use in own writing
Revision of all grammar structures covered in Grades 7–9
Write a formal Afrikaans review or report
Oral: recite and interpret an Afrikaans poem or present a visual analysis

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Revision and FET preparation
topics: Unseen Afrikaans comprehension: apply all reading skills to an unfamiliar text
Revision of all writing formats: letter, essay, report, summary, poem
Examination techniques: reading questions, managing time, checking work
Grammar consolidation: all tenses, voice, speech, concord, clauses, punctuation
Vocabulary strategies for FET Phase Afrikaans
Oral: final formal prepared speech in Afrikaans
Reflect on growth as an Afrikaans FAL learner across the Senior Phase
Set language goals for Afrikaans in Grade 10

skillChips: Read Afrikaans texts at Grade 9 level with critical understanding
Use all tenses including perfect and pluperfect
Write passive voice in all tenses
Write a structured Afrikaans argumentative essay
Produce polished Afrikaans transactional texts
Analyse Afrikaans poetry using correct terminology
Compare two Afrikaans poems in writing
Use conditional sentences of all four types
Identify nominal and relative clauses
Analyse visual texts in Afrikaans
Apply all Senior Phase grammar in own writing
Write confidently across all required text types

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Consolidate vocabulary before the exam. Make flashcards for Afrikaans words you struggle with. Review daily in Term 4.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Argumentative essays need a clear thesis. State your position in the first paragraph. Every body paragraph must support it.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Passive voice in all tenses. Die brief word geskryf (present) / is geskryf (past) / sal geskryf word (future). Learn all three.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Use the full range of grammar. In Grade 9, examiners expect you to use complex sentences, modal verbs and figurative language naturally in your own writing.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Revise one grammar topic per day in Term 4. Systematic revision beats last-minute cramming every time.

subjects.hubDescription: Extended essays, argumentative writing, literary texts and all grammar consolidated.

subjects.title: Grade 9 Afrikaans Home Language | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Afrikaans Home Language for Grade 9. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Graad 9 Afrikaans Huistaal is die finale jaar van die Seniorfase en stel die hoogste eise aan letterkundige analise, uitgebreide formele skryfwerk en kritiese taalbetrokkenheid voor die OBF-fase. Leerders werk met volledige prosatekste, poësie en dramatiese tekste op 'n analitiese vlak, produseer gepoleerde meervoudige paragraafopstelle, en demonstreer beheer oor gevorderde grammatika, transaksionele skryfwerk en mediavaardighede.

expectItems.label: Letterkunde
expectItems.value: Prosa roman + gedigte + drama — volledige tekste

expectItems.label: Sleutelverskuiwing
expectItems.value: Volgehoue letterkundige analise · gepoleerde formele skryfwerk · OBF-gereedheid

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Prosa: volgehoue letterkundige analise
topics: Lees 'n volledige prosateks — analiseer karakterontwikkeling, plotstruktuur, narratiewe tegniek
Identifiseer en verduidelik ironie (verbaal, situasioneel, dramaties), simbool, motief, allegorie
Derdepersoon alwetend vs beperk vs eerstepersoon vertelling — effek op leser
Volgehoue analitiese opstel: inleiding met tesis, ontwikkelde liggaamsparagrawe (PEEL), gevolgtrekking
Hersiening van alle tye insluitend voltooide voortgaande vorme
Kongruensie: komplekse gevalle — kollektiewe naamwoorde, onbepaalde voornaamwoorde
Woordeskat: register, toon, konnotasie, eufemisme, jargon, cliché
Mondeling: formele voorbereide toespraak met oorredende bedoeling

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Poësie: gevorderde kritiese analise
topics: Analiseer en vergelyk drie gedigte — volgehoue skriftelike reaksie
Uitgebreide stylfigure: uitgebreide metafoor, apostrofe, toespeling, antitese, chiasmus
Reëloorloop, pouse, volta — effek op betekenis, pas, klem
Poëtiese vorme: sonnet (Petrargiaans en Shakespeariaans), vrye vers, ballade — kenmerke
Woordkeuse: konnotasie, denotasie, juxtaposisie — hoe woordkeuses betekenis skep
Formele briewe, e-posse, CV's en dekbriewe — hersiening en verfyning
Voorwaardelike sinne: nul-, eerste, tweede, derde — vorm en betekenis
Mondeling: gedigopsê met analitiese refleksie

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Drama: analise en uitvoering
topics: Lees 'n volledige dramateks — analiseer dramatiese struktuur: eksposisie, stygende aksie, hoogtepunt, dalende aksie, ontknoping
Dramatiese ironie, aankondiging, tragiese fout, deus ex machina — identifikasie en effek
Karakteranalise: motivering, ontwikkeling, verhoudings, rol in tema
Solilokie, terzyde, toneelrigting — dramatiese funksie
Transaksionele skryfwerk: notule, agenda, verslag, persverklaring, formele e-pos — hersiening
Naamwoordelike, byvoeglike en bywoordelike bysinne — identifiseer en gebruik
Sinkombinering: verminder twee sinne tot een met 'n bysin of frase
Mondeling: dramatiese voorlees of uitvoering van 'n toneel

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Ongesiene tekste, hersiening en OBF-voorbereiding
topics: Ongesiene prosa begrip: pas alle letterkundige analise-vaardighede toe op 'n nuwe teks
Ongesiene poësie: analiseer 'n onbekende gedig onafhanklik met korrekte terminologie
Visuele en mediateksanalise: hersien alle vaardighede — doel, gehoor, tegniek, vooroordeel
Argumenterende opstel: tesis-gebaseerd, met teenargument en weerlegging
Beskouende opstel: gebalanseerde siening, weeg getuienis aan beide kante
Grammatikahersiening: alle tye, stem, rede, kongruensie, bysinne, leestekens
Spelling- en woordeskatstrategieë vir OBF-fase gereedheid
Mondeling: formele voorbereide aanbieding — navorsingsgebaseerde onderwerp

skillChips: Analiseer prosa vir narratiewe tegniek en literêre middele
Skryf 'n tesis-gedrewe analitiese opstel
Vergelyk drie gedigte met teksgetuienis
Identifiseer en verduidelik uitgebreide metafoor, toespeling en antitese
Analiseer poëtiese vorm: sonnet, vrye vers, ballade
Analiseer drama vir struktuur, karakter en tema
Produseer gepoleerde transaksionele tekste
Identifiseer en gebruik naamwoordelike, byvoeglike en bywoordelike bysinne
Skryf argumenterende en beskouende opstelle
Analiseer ongesiene prosa en poësie onafhanklik
Evalueer mediatekste vir vooroordeel en doel
Demonstreer beheer oor alle grammatika op Seniorfase-vlak

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Het 'n duidelike tesis voor jy skryf. Elke analitiese en argumenterende opstel benodig 'n tesis — 'n duidelike, betwisbare stelling. Skryf dit eers.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Haal presies en kortliks aan. Kort, goed gekose aanhalings is beter as lang ones. Haal net aan wat jy nodig het en verduidelik onmiddellik die effek.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Vergelyk met konnektiefwoorde. 'Beide digters...', 'Terwyl Gedig A gebruik...', 'In teenstelling met...'. Dit dui op vergelyking eerder as afsonderlike analise.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 6c-1.8-1.6-4.3-2.3-8-2v14c3.7-.3 6.2.4 8 2 1.8-1.6 4.3-2.3 8-2V4c-3.7-.3-6.2.4-8 2z"/><path d="M12 6v14"/></svg>
tips.text: Ken jou bysoorte uit die kop. Naamwoordelike bysin (optree as onderwerp/voorwerp), byvoeglike bysin (beskryf 'n naamwoord), bywoordelike bysin (wysig 'n werkwoord).

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Graad 9 is jou OBF-aanloopbaan. Die gewoontes wat jy nou bou — beplanning, aanhaal, verduidelik effek — is presies wat Graad 10-eksaminatore soek.

subjects.hubDescription: Volgehoue letterkundige analise, tesis-gedrewe opstelle, drama en OBF-gereedheid.

subjects.title: Grade 9 Creative Arts | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Creative Arts for Grade 9. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 9 Creative Arts is the final year of the Senior Phase and demands the highest level of technical skill, critical thinking and creative independence. Learners produce a substantial body of practical work, engage deeply with South African and global art traditions, and develop the ability to critically analyse and write about art forms. Grade 9 Creative Arts prepares learners for the specialist arts subjects of the FET Phase.

expectItems.label: Art forms
expectItems.value: Visual Arts · Music · Drama · Dance (2 selected)

expectItems.label: Key focus
expectItems.value: Technical mastery · independent creativity · critical writing · FET readiness

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Advanced technique in Visual Art and Music
topics: Visual Art: advanced composition — rule of thirds, golden ratio, focal point, negative space
Life drawing: figure drawing with proportion, gesture, foreshortening
Printmaking: complex multi-colour relief or screen printing process
Visual Art practical: substantial mixed media or printmaking portfolio piece
Music: advanced notation — complex rhythms, compound time, transposition
Harmony: triads, chord progressions — I, IV, V, vi — in major and minor keys
Music performance: solo or ensemble — Grade 9 level AMEB equivalent pieces
Art history: Modernism and Post-Modernism — key movements and artists

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Drama and Dance: advanced performance
topics: Drama: Brecht vs Stanislavski — Epic Theatre vs Method — theory and application
Physical theatre: devised work using physical storytelling, mime, mask
Script writing: structure a short original script with dramatic arc and subtext
Drama practical: perform a devised or scripted piece for an audience
Dance: choreographic forms — binary, ternary, rondo, theme and variation
Contact improvisation and partnering — trust, weight sharing, flow
Dance practical: choreograph and perform a group piece with clear concept
Performance critique: written analysis of own and others' work using correct terminology

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Arts in social and cultural context
topics: Visual Art: South African contemporary art — themes of identity, memory, politics, environment
Curate a mini-exhibition of own work with artist statements for each piece
Music: world music traditions — Indian classical, African drumming, Latin, American blues
Music: arrangement — take a melody and arrange it for a small ensemble
Drama: community theatre and applied drama — Theatre for Development (TfD) in SA
Dance: global dance traditions — flamenco, bharatanatyam, Afro-contemporary — context and features
Comparative analysis essay: compare two artworks or performances across cultural contexts
Interdisciplinary project: combine at least two art forms in one creative response

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Portfolio, performance and reflection
topics: Visual Art: final portfolio — select, mount and present best 5 pieces with written reflection
Music: end-of-year performance — solo and ensemble, including an original composition
Drama: final scripted performance — full production elements including design brief
Dance: final performance — group piece demonstrating all Grade 9 skills
Arts showcase: present to a wider audience
Final art criticism essay: 500-word formal analysis of a professional artwork or performance
Peer and self-assessment: structured reflection on creative growth
Prepare for FET Arts subjects: what each subject requires

skillChips: Apply advanced composition principles in visual art
Produce a multi-colour print or complex mixed media work
Draw the human figure with proportion and gesture
Read and perform complex music notation
Demonstrate chord progressions in performance
Apply Brechtian and Stanislavskian techniques in drama
Write and perform an original short script
Choreograph a group dance with a clear concept
Write a formal art criticism essay
Curate work with artist statements
Analyse art across cultural contexts
Compare two works in a structured analytical response

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 3v5M12 16v5M3 12h5M16 12h5M6 6l3 3M15 15l3 3M18 6l-3 3M9 15l-3 3"/></svg>
tips.text: Artist statements show your thinking. For every major practical piece, write a short statement: what you made, why you made it, what you learned. This is assessed.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: Art criticism: describe → analyse → interpret → evaluate. Use this four-step structure every time you write about an artwork or performance.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M12 3v5M12 16v5M3 12h5M16 12h5M6 6l3 3M15 15l3 3M18 6l-3 3M9 15l-3 3"/></svg>
tips.text: Grade 9 performance must show intention. Every movement, line and gesture should be a deliberate choice. Explain your choices if asked.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M3 12h18M12 3c2.5 2.5 3.8 5.6 3.8 9s-1.3 6.5-3.8 9c-2.5-2.5-3.8-5.6-3.8-9S9.5 5.5 12 3z"/></svg>
tips.text: Know at least three SA artists in depth. For Visual Art: Kentridge, Muholi, Bester. For Music: Hugh Masekela, Miriam Makeba, Sibongile Khumalo.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Your portfolio tells your story. A strong portfolio shows growth, range and reflection. Include work from different terms and explain what you learned.

subjects.hubDescription: Advanced technique, portfolio, capstone performance and FET Arts subject preparation.

subjects.title: Grade 9 Economic Management and Science | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned Economic Management and Science for Grade 9. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 9 EMS is the final year and consolidates all three areas — Economy, Financial Literacy and Entrepreneurship — at a level that prepares learners for Accounting, Business Studies and Economics in the FET Phase. Learners complete a full set of financial records, analyse the South African economy in depth, and develop a comprehensive business plan. Grade 9 EMS is a crucial year for learners planning FET business and economics subjects.

expectItems.label: Key concepts
expectItems.value: Full bookkeeping cycle · financial analysis · SA economic challenges

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: The South African economy in depth
topics: Revision of circular flow — four-sector model (households, firms, government, foreign)
Macroeconomic goals: economic growth, full employment, price stability, balanced trade
Inflation: causes (demand-pull, cost-push), effects, CPI calculation
Unemployment: types (frictional, structural, cyclical, seasonal), causes, consequences in SA
Monetary policy: repo rate, prime rate — how the Reserve Bank controls inflation
Fiscal policy: government budget — expansionary and contractionary
Economic indicators: GDP, GDP per capita, inflation rate, unemployment rate
SA's economic challenges: inequality (Gini coefficient), poverty, load shedding

termCards.label: Term 2
termCards.heading: Financial literacy: financial statements and analysis
topics: Income statement: revenue, cost of sales, gross profit, expenses, net profit
Balance sheet: assets (fixed and current), liabilities (long-term and current), owner's equity
Cash flow statement: operating, investing and financing activities — concept
Financial ratios: gross profit %, net profit %, return on investment — calculate and interpret
Break-even analysis: break-even point in units and in rand
Budgets: cash budget — prepare and analyse surplus/deficit
Simple and compound interest: full revision — apply in financial contexts
VAT: revision — VAT-inclusive and exclusive, VAT returns concept

termCards.label: Term 3
termCards.heading: Full bookkeeping cycle
topics: Source documents: invoices, receipts, credit notes — identify and process
Journals: CRJ, CPJ, debtors journal (DJ), creditors journal (CJ) — all four
General journal (GJ): adjustments, corrections, depreciation entries
Ledger accounts: post from all journals to individual ledger accounts
Trial balance: extract from all ledger balances — check it balances
Debtors and creditors control accounts: reconcile with subsidiary ledgers
Depreciation: straight-line method — calculate and record
Financial year-end: closing entries concept

termCards.label: Term 4
termCards.heading: Entrepreneurship and FET preparation
topics: Full business plan: executive summary, business description, market analysis, SWOT, marketing plan, operational plan, financial projections
Market research: primary and secondary research — tools, methods, analysis
Consumer behaviour: factors affecting buying decisions — psychological, social, economic
The entrepreneurial process: idea → opportunity → feasibility → launch → growth
Social entrepreneurship: triple bottom line — people, planet, profit
Ethics in business: black economic empowerment (BEE), BBBEE in SA context
Prepare for FET: overview of Accounting, Business Studies, Economics — what each covers
Reflect on financial literacy growth: personal finance goals for the future

skillChips: Explain macroeconomic goals and indicators
Describe monetary and fiscal policy
Calculate inflation using CPI
Describe types of unemployment
Prepare an income statement and balance sheet
Calculate financial ratios and interpret results
Prepare and analyse a cash budget
Complete the full bookkeeping cycle (all four journals)
Post journals to ledger and extract a trial balance
Calculate depreciation using straight-line method
Write a full business plan
Explain SA's economic challenges with data

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><rect x="2" y="5" width="20" height="14" rx="2"/><path d="M2 10h20"/></svg>
tips.text: The bookkeeping cycle has a fixed order. Source documents → Journals → Ledger → Trial balance. Never skip a step.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="m3 16 6-6 4 4 8-9"/><path d="M15 5h6v6"/></svg>
tips.text: Financial ratios need the formula and interpretation. Gross profit % = (Gross profit ÷ Revenue) × 100. Then say whether it is good or bad and why.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M13 4 20 11 9 22H2v-7z"/><path d="M11.5 5.5 18.5 12.5"/></svg>
tips.text: EMS uses specific terminology. 'Revenue' not 'money received'. 'Debtor' not 'person who owes'. Precision earns marks.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><path d="M3 12h18M12 3c2.5 2.5 3.8 5.6 3.8 9s-1.3 6.5-3.8 9c-2.5-2.5-3.8-5.6-3.8-9S9.5 5.5 12 3z"/></svg>
tips.text: Know SA's economic statistics. Approximate unemployment rate (~32%), Gini coefficient (~0.63), GDP growth — these appear in exam questions.

tips.iconSvg: <svg width="15" height="15" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" style="flex-shrink:0"><path d="M7 20h10M12 20v-8"/><path d="M12 12c0-3.5-2.5-6-7-6 0 4.5 2.5 6.5 7 6z"/><path d="M12 10c0-3 2-5 6-5 0 3.5-2 5.5-6 5z"/></svg>
tips.text: Understand the business plan structure. Every section serves a purpose. Know what each section must contain and why it matters.

subjects.hubDescription: Full bookkeeping cycle, financial statements, SA economy and comprehensive business plan.

subjects.title: Grade 9 English First Additional Language | CAPS | Curio Learning
subjects.description: CAPS-aligned English First Additional Language for Grade 9. Term-by-term topics, skills and free papers with memos.
subjects.expectIntro: Grade 9 English FAL consolidates functional English literacy at the highest Senior Phase level. Learners write extended multi-paragraph texts, handle complex grammar, read literary and argumentative texts critically, and produce polished transactional writing. Grade 9 FAL demands independent, accurate use of English across a wide range of contexts in preparation for the FET Phase.

expectItems.label: Key progression
expectItems.value: Extended essays · literary texts · all grammar consolidated

termCards.label: Term 1
termCards.heading: Narrative and literary texts
topics: Read narrative and literary texts — literal, inferential, evaluative and critical questions
